I know i'll be back here, who doesn't like fast / delicious / attentive service?
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Upon entering, you're greeted by the friendly woman at the counter who quickly remembers regular customers' names. Although my visits are sporadic, I haven't been fortunate enough to have my name remembered yet. One recent find that I love is the vegetarian breakfast sandwiches, available all day. Personally, I enjoy the veggie sausage with havarti on an everything bagel. The deli also offers other tasty options like the veggie club sandwich, chicken cheesesteak hoagie, and chicken salad on a croissant. All the menu items taste fresh and are reasonably priced, with my favorite bagel sandwich costing between $2.09 and $2.99, cheaper than Wawa. The helpful staff will provide menus if needed and are happy to make recommendations and accommodate special requests. Don't forget to indulge in their impressive selection of snacks, including delicious chocolate bars, a variety of drinks, a wide range of chips, and addictive hi-chew candies in multiple flavors. With their fast, delicious, and attentive service, I know I'll be revisiting this place.

input: We stopped in for brunch and we weren't expecting the food to be so delicious.  The 3 meat hash was amazing, as was the turkey sandwich and bagel/salmon.  The employees were very friendly and accommodating.  A little pricey, but well worth.  We will visit again if in the area.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We had an unexpectedly delicious brunch at this restaurant. The 3 meat hash, turkey sandwich, and bagel with salmon were all amazing. The employees were friendly and accommodating. Though a bit pricey, it was definitely worth it. We'll definitely come back if we're in the area.

input: Nice little bar located at the very far end of Terminal E and Tampa International. The airport recently added several new restaurants with a "local vibe" and this is one of them. There isn't a ton of seating but it also isn't close to the TSA area so it's a bit hidden. Hey have TVs if you wanna catch a game while you wait for your flight. Food is very reasonably price for the portion size. Appetizers run from $5-$10 and majority of sandwiches are $12. I didn't order any food but it looked amazing! Drinks are tasty and Prices are not terrible. Think 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50. You cannot take alcoholic beverages into the terminal (Columbia does this I think). I had a Manhattan for $11 and it was very tasty. Staff is attentive and friendly. I know my new spot when I'm waiting on a Delta flight!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Located at the far end of Terminal E at Tampa International Airport, this nice little bar is one of the airport's new restaurants with a local vibe. Though not close to the TSA area, it offers a limited seating arrangement. However, it does have TVs for those who want to catch a game during their wait. The food prices here are very reasonable, with appetizers ranging from $5 to $10 and most sandwiches priced at $12. Although I didn't try any food, it looked amazing. The bar offers tasty drinks at not-so-terrible prices, such as a 22oz Jai Alai for $8.50. Keep in mind that alcoholic beverages cannot be taken into the terminal. I personally enjoyed a delicious Manhattan for $11. The staff at this bar is attentive and friendly, making it my go-to spot when waiting for a Delta flight.

input: The depot burger is so delicious along with the shishito peppers! Perfect food, perfect atmosphere, perfect drinks!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The depot burger and shishito peppers are both incredibly delicious at the restaurant. The food, atmosphere, and drinks are all perfect.

input: Quality of this store has gone downhill over the past few years. In the past,  I was able to easily choose from a wide selection of food at reasonable prices any time of day. I have noticed recently that the produce is not as fresh, but more expensive,  and the prices of the organic foods are more expensive than Whole Foods. This morning I debated on going to Wegmans or going to this store. I only had to get a few items so I decided on this Giant since it was closer. Big mistake. I have seen on average at least 3 or 4 people shopping around 5 a.m. In the past but today just me. They had all of the store roped off where it was impossible to get to certain aisles and very difficult to get to the register. In my frustration I went under a rope to get soup.  I was then berated by a number of people who were supposed to be cleaning the floors but some were just standing around doing nothing. I couldn't even walk out of the closest door because that was blocked off. If they needed to clean the floor they should have closed the store for a few hours. It would have taken less time at Wegmans which is where I will shop for now on.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The store's quality has declined in recent years. Previously, there was a wide selection of affordable food available throughout the day. However, the produce is now less fresh and more expensive, while the prices of organic foods are higher than at Whole Foods. Today, I debated between going to Wegmans or this store for a few items and chose the latter due to proximity. It turned out to be a mistake. There used to be multiple shoppers around 5 a.m., but today I was the only one. The store had roped off certain aisles and it was difficult to reach the register. In frustration, I went under a rope to retrieve soup and was reprimanded by individuals who were supposed to be cleaning the floors. Some of them were idle, and the closest exit was also blocked. It would have been more efficient to shop at Wegmans, where I'll be going from now on.

input: This place is a hidden gem.  It is located in a strip mall, but this restaurant is anything but a strip mall restaurant.   My husband took me here for my birthday and I was blown away with the whole experience.  It's a very modern, romantic atmosphere.  The food is excellent.  I was shocked by the Fois gras-amazing.  I had the prix fixe menu and I loved ordering 3 courses.  The short ribs were great, but I want to try something new next time.  The desserts were awesome.  I usually take caramel, but there was a caramel tart that was to die for.  Can't wait to go back!!!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This hidden gem, located in a strip mall, defies the notion of a typical strip mall restaurant. My birthday dinner here was an unforgettable experience, thanks to its modern and romantic atmosphere. The food surpassed all expectations, particularly the incredible Fois gras. Opting for the prix fixe menu allowed me to enjoy three delicious courses. The short ribs were excellent, though next time I'd like to try something different. The desserts were simply awesome, especially the irresistible caramel tart. I am eagerly looking forward to returning soon!

input:
--------DINNER REVIEW----------

I rarely write reviews, but this honestly was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. It was objectively a horrible experience, even without comparing it to the hype it receives, and ruined what was supposed to be a nice birthday dinner celebration. 

We had a group of 8 that had a reservation made well in advance. Short wait, but not too bad. Keep in mind, it seemed like a normal Friday night, but weren't super busy or at-capacity.

It was a birthday dinner, so I told the hostesses that it was her birthday, and asked if they could bring out something for her at the end of the meal, which was acknowledged. Pretty standard stuff, whether at a Applebee's or the French Laundry. We were sat at a booth right next to the Maitre D' stand, and next to all the wait staff's home base, so pretty much no excuse for not getting any attention. 

After getting us waters, it took them a LONG time to even come by and acknowledge us. After ordering wine, it took them another good 15-20 minutes to even bring us our wine, and no one even checked in on us! (hint: if you're running a restaurant, wine is your profit center and doesn't take any work other than taking a bottle off a shelf and opening it. bring it out ASAP...). 

After ordering food, it was more of the same...a long wait for food to start coming out and no one checking in on us AT ALL. We drank the bottles we ordered and had to get up and flag someone down to get another wine order. A couple of us even got up during the meal to remind them to bring out something for birthday girl at the end of the meal. 

Once our meal was done and taken away, we were given dessert menus and the server disappeared for 10-15 minutes... AGAIN. After coming back, he asked what dessert we wanted, so we ordered some coffees... and waited... and waited. Eventually we got up and asked him what was going on and if they were going to bring anything out like we asked multiple times. 

They finally brought out a couple of cookies with a candle...

In summary, the food was pretty hit or miss, pretty mediocre for this price point. Whipped feta, like other reviews have said, was amazing, and the Braised Lamb was really good. But the Sirloin was chewy and bland and the Grilled Caesar tasted like a soggy, luke-warm, wilted mess (two orders were left untouched by a group of 8). Atmosphere was nice and trendy. But the service, which is a huge reason to spend your hard-earned $ at a restaurant, was absolutely horrendous. 

I really love going to cool, popular restaurants and having a great time, and I hate writing such a negative review, but I had to share my experience, especially for a restaurant that is getting an awful lot of (undeserved) hype.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This was one of the worst group dining experiences I've ever had. Despite making a reservation well in advance, the service was extremely poor. We had to wait a long time for attention, wine, and food. Even though we reminded them multiple times, they forgot to bring something for the birthday celebration. The food was mediocre, with some dishes being good and others being chewy and bland. The atmosphere was nice, but the service was horrendous. I had to share this negative review for a restaurant that is receiving undeserved hype.

input:
Great food for the price. 
Tender steak and perfectly cooked shrimp. 
Would certainly come back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Delicious and affordable food, including tender steak and perfectly cooked shrimp. Definitely worth a return visit.

input:
We stopped at Tako due to the positive reviews on yelp. We brought a bottle of white wine with us, the staff did not bring a ice or a chill bucket for us. It took 45 minutes for our appetizers to come out. The edamame was over cooked and mushy while the spring roll did not look appetizing almost like it was frozen. I could buy better spring rolls from trader joes.
Next we moved on to our sushi which was sat on the sushi bar for 15 minutes before it was brought to us. The sushi it self was good, but not the best I have ever had,
If I came here again I would not buy any appetizers. The service was slow
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We chose Tako based on positive Yelp reviews but were disappointed with our experience. We brought a bottle of white wine but the staff didn't provide us with an ice or chill bucket. Our appetizers took 45 minutes to arrive, and the edamame was overcooked and mushy while the spring roll looked unappetizing and possibly frozen. The sushi, though decent, sat on the sushi bar for 15 minutes before being served. Overall, the service was slow, and I wouldn't order any appetizers if I were to visit again.

input: The catfish, chicken, gumbo and mac &a cheese are all to die for. We are the lunch buffet and everything was piping hot and fresh. This place was recommended by a local in the neighborhood we are staying in and it was so worth it!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The catfish, chicken, gumbo, and mac & cheese at the lunch buffet were recommended by a local in the neighborhood we're staying in and they were all amazing. Everything was piping hot and fresh, making it a worthwhile experience.

input:
See's candies is California base bakery reach Florida. I know about this candies when my wife living in California. Their chocolate is very soft and tasty. 

In Tampa, the International Plaza Mall has this temporary store from Thanksgiving to Easter. They located very close to H&M clothing store. You can have samples before you buy it. I got the lollipop candies. I also bought one assorted chocolate candies. They are very good. The store clerk was kind enough to let us try their assorted chocolate other their typical sample candies. 

You can go with chocolate with nut, mint, toffee, milk, white or dark chocolate. All are good. Guilty pleasure with a touch at sweet side. Mail order through the web also available. If you close to the mall, just go to buy one without shipping.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: See's Candies, a California-based bakery, has expanded its reach to Florida. I first discovered these delicious chocolates when my wife lived in California. Luckily, in Tampa, at the International Plaza Mall, they have a temporary store open from Thanksgiving to Easter. This store is conveniently located near the H&M clothing store. The best part is that they offer samples before you make a purchase. On my visit, I tried their lollipop candies and also bought a box of assorted chocolates, which were incredibly tasty. The store clerk even went out of their way to let us try some of their other assorted chocolates, in addition to the typical sample candies. The options for different flavors of chocolate include nut, mint, toffee, milk, white, and dark chocolate, all of which were fantastic. Whether you choose to indulge in their guilty pleasures at the store or opt for mail order through their website, the choice is yours. However, if you are close to the mall, I highly recommend visiting their temporary store and purchasing one without the need for shipping.

input:
Second stop for Center City Restaurant Week:  R2L, dinner for $35 each. 

On the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place is a very fancy-cool restaurant/lounge where you can get a bird's eye view of the city! Group of us went to dinner here together after a day of meetings. Didn't get one of the tables facing the windows, but still had great views of the sunset and city by night. Again, multiple choices for the three courses, but I chose to start with the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls]. Main course was the Butcher's Filet (braised short rib + Steuben bean chili, potato/farm veg slaw and basil), which was quite heavy since there was also meat in the chili as well. The dazzling dessert to finish it off was the milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding served with salted caramel and coffee to melt the chocolate, and candied almonds on the side. A bottle of wine for the table as well. Food was great, waiter was awesome (making sure to warn me that the risotto came in ball form rather than a bowl, for instance), very classy experience.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Visited R2L for Center City Restaurant Week. Dinner was $35 per person. Located on the 37th floor of Two Liberty Place, this fancy-cool restaurant/lounge offers stunning city views. Despite not having a window table, we still enjoyed sunset and night city views. The menu had multiple choices for each course. I opted for the crisp peas/ham/garlic risotto [balls] as an appetizer, followed by the Butcher's Filet with braised short rib and Steuben bean chili, accompanied by potato/farm veg slaw and basil. The dessert was a delightful milk chocolate + hazelnut pudding with salted caramel and coffee, served with candied almonds on the side. Our table also enjoyed a bottle of wine. The food was excellent, and our waiter provided exceptional service, even giving me a heads up about the unique presentation of the risotto. Overall, it was a classy and enjoyable experience.

input: Becca is an awesome bartender. They have awesome happy hour specials including land shark. The food menu is somewhat limited but the service at the bar is great. We hope they can keep up the business and attract more locals.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Becca, an awesome bartender, offers fantastic happy hour specials, including land shark. Although the food menu is limited, the service at the bar is excellent. We hope Becca can continue to attract more locals and thrive in their business.

input: Bummer, just moved to this area and this was my first visit to this location.  I didn't receive my change or receipt,  it was just change but I asked for it and she said she gave it to me, um no. Was in a hurry so I didn't wanna argue.  And no spoon for my chili. Cheese on my burger was old, which means my burger wasn't freshly made. Tasted ok but won't return.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I recently moved to this area and had my first visit to this location. Unfortunately, I did not receive my change or receipt, even though I requested it and was told it was given to me. I didn't want to argue as I was in a hurry. Additionally, I did not receive a spoon for my chili and found that the cheese on my burger was old, indicating that it wasn't freshly made. While the taste was okay, these issues have led me to decide against returning.

input: They have great prices if you order family style. We tried the pot roast and it was just as good carry out as it would have been at the restaurant. They packaged everything nicely and it stayed warm after the 30 min car ride. There was definitely enough for a family of 4. The green beans were amazing! I would definitely recommend. It's nothing special, just a good family restaurant
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: They offer great prices for family-style orders. We ordered the pot roast and found it to be equally delicious as if we had dined at the restaurant. The packaging was excellent as it kept the food warm during the 30-minute car ride. Portions were ample for a family of four. The green beans were particularly outstanding. Overall, it is a recommended family restaurant, not particularly unique but with good food.

input: Ordered Caramel frappe at Drive thru, BIG MISTAKE! Took 30 min and there were only 2 cars in front of me.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Ordered Caramel frappe at Drive thru, waited 30 min, only 2 cars ahead.

input:
This place is amazing! The pizza cookies are a must. It came hot, soft, and crazy delicious. 

We tried the Peanut butter pizza cookie and the Oreo cookies, and both were perfection. I'm very eager to try other flavors. Also, being open until 3am is the smartest decision of any bakery in America. 

The only reason I'm not giving a 5 is because of the prices. But, to be honest, those late nights when all I want is a fresh baked cookie pizza, I'd be willing to pay $50.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is amazing! The must-try item is the hot, soft, and crazy delicious pizza cookies. We tried the Peanut butter pizza cookie and the Oreo cookies, both perfection. Excited to try other flavors and love that they are open until 3am – the smartest decision of any bakery in America. The only drawback is the high prices, but for a fresh baked cookie pizza during late nights, I would still be willing to pay $50.

input:
I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago.  Everybody here raves about the restaurants, but I have yet to find many that deserve five stars, or even four.  This is the best restaurant I have eaten in in Philadelphia.  

Tahini and bread  arrived at the table, and I thought, hum, plain but I'm hungry.  They must put crack in that Tahini.  I wanted to lap it out of the bowl like an uncouth dog.  The bread is excellent too.

I love a menu with many organic meat choices.  How often can you order an organic beef shishkabob?  It was superb.  The meat done perfectly, the onions nearly caramelized but not quite so they still had some substantive crunch.  The purslane salad tasted like I was eating a plant in the middle of a garden.  It is not often that I dream about a salad but I do dream about this one

My husband had a chicken dish with black eyed peas and green peas and fantastic rice.  I won't begin to describe the flavoring; it is beyond my culinary vocabulary.  We asked what spices they use, and in addition to traditional zatar, they use their own blend of spices.  I don't even need to know what is in it just so long as we can keep coming back and ordering it again and again.

I was so full but ate dessert none the less, which I usually don't do.  But when a diner is this good, I had a feeling the desserts would be too and I just needed to find out.  Pistachio creme brulee.  It could have come out over the top, but no indeed.  It was pure pistachio heaven in s super light yet rich custard.  Heaven. Heaven.

Our service was superb.  The squeezed us into a last minute Friday night reservation with the caveat that we would need to get through our dinner in an hour and 15 minutes in order to accommodate a reservation made prior to us.  Given the time constraints they never made us feel rushed and timed the meal perfectly.  Then my husband left to go to the restroom, the waiter picked up his napkin and refolded it nicely on the table.  Do I care about the napkin placement in the middle of a meal?  Not really, but it is a sign that the waitstaff is incredibly attentive and extremely well trained.  

My eating out plan for Philly might just be to skip eating most everywhere most of the time so I can frequent this expensive, though appropriately priced restaurant.  Kudos to the chef.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I moved from Chicago to Philadelphia over a year ago and have been disappointed with the restaurant scene so far. However, this particular restaurant proved to be a pleasant surprise. The tahini and bread were nothing out of the ordinary, but strangely addictive. The menu offers a variety of delicious organic meat options, including a superb beef shishkabob and a mouthwatering purslane salad. My husband's chicken dish was also flavorful, with a unique blend of spices. Despite being full, we couldn't resist trying their dessert and were delighted with the delightful pistachio creme brulee. The service was top-notch, as they accommodated our last-minute reservation and handled the time constraints gracefully. Overall, this restaurant has exceeded my expectations and I plan on making it my go-to spot in Philadelphia, despite its higher prices. Applauds to the chef.

input: They served me a frozen pizza and skunked beer.  'Nuff said.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: They gave me frozen pizza and bad beer. That's all.

input: Whole family got sick after eating here. The frozen yogurt was pretty but did not taste good. Would not go here again or recommend it.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The entire family fell ill after dining at this place, and although the frozen yogurt looked appealing, it lacked taste. Based on our experience, we would not return or suggest it to others.

input:
This is the place for authentic Indian street food. I've been here multiple times ordering different things ranging from bhel puri, pav bhaji, vada pav, deconstructed samosa and aloo tikki, dabeli, kulfi and more. Everything was made exceptionally well.

I regret not having found this place sooner.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Authentic Indian street food is available here, including bhel puri, pav bhaji, vada pav, deconstructed samosa and aloo tikki, dabeli, kulfi, and more. I have visited multiple times and found everything to be exceptionally well-made. I wish I had discovered this place earlier.

input:
Uhhhhh.... Not sure how to quantify or qualify my experience here. Let's start with back story: 

My sister was visiting for the weekend, so I wanted to show her a solid night on the town that lasted till the wee hours of the morning. We started on Frenchmen, but for whatever reason it was dead. 
Deciding to adventure Uptown we proceeded on a respectable bar crawl, including Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes, however, at 3 AM the usual Uptown culprits start to raise their heads. A summary of the following dialogue:

Friends "Let's go to FMs" 
Me: "No, too much broken glass"
Friends: "Let's go to Snake and Jake's"
Me: "Eh...."
Friends: "Brothers 3?"
Me: "I'm afraid I'll hit my head on the ceiling"
Friends: "The Saint!!"
Me: "I suppose I haven't been there before, I'm curious."

After entering the Saint the look on my sisters face was priceless, akin to a deer in headlights look. I kept my countenance, and we ordered a round. Things proceeded as expected ... unwanted dance grinding advances, check! uber drunk guy talking your ear off, check! Big Buck Hunter, CHECK!!! Overall I'm glad I moderately traumatized my sister and sated my curiosity in the same night. 

Helpful hint: They have outdoor seating, surprisingly, which is very good to escape the smoke
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I showed my sister a night on the town starting at Frenchmen, but it was dead. We decided to go uptown and visited Delachaise, Columns, and St. Joes. Eventually, we ended up at The Saint at 3 AM. My sister had a shocked expression on her face. We experienced unwanted advances, drunk people, and played Big Buck Hunter. It was an interesting night, and I'm glad we checked out The Saint. They surprisingly have outdoor seating, which is a good way to escape the smoke.

input: The food here is so great and fresh. I don't shy away from my kids favorite Wonton Soup because i know they take the time to cook it.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food here is excellent and always fresh, including my kids' favorite Wonton Soup, which they take the time to cook.

input: Food was great. But very disappointed with the hospitality. We  entered the restaurant at 9:15 pm but was denied dine in and was told that though the  restaurant closes at 10 pm they won't let us dine in and can give only to go. They saw that there were two pregnant women and a kid with us and I explained that our home is a hour drive from there and yet they denied for no reason. I had to drive back to home and make everyone eat. Very disappointed with such attitude towards customers. Never going back here. Let them try to forgive them self for denying dining for pregnant women.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food was excellent. However, we were extremely disappointed with the hospitality. Despite arriving at the restaurant at 9:15 pm, we were not allowed to dine in. Despite the fact that the restaurant's closing time was not until 10 pm, they refused to accommodate us and only offered takeout. We even explained that we had two pregnant women and a child with us and that our home was an hour away, but they still denied us service without justification. Consequently, we had to drive all the way back home and prepare a meal there. This attitude towards customers is highly disappointing, and we have decided never to return to this establishment. They should reflect on their decision to deny pregnant women a proper dining experience.

input: This place surpassed our expectations!  The steak is far superior to any steak house I have been too.  The staff flows together like a well trained team, the hostess Mallory, our waiter Max, and the busboy all keep things moving smoothly and leave you never wanting for anything.  Honestly the whole experience was amazing and we will be back for more. Love this place!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place exceeded expectations! The steak is the best I've had compared to any steak house. The staff, including Mallory the hostess, Max our waiter, and the busboy, work seamlessly to ensure a smooth and satisfying experience. Overall, it was an amazing experience and we'll definitely be returning for more. Love this place!

input: The service is super friendly! During my exam, Dr. Dinh was very kind and addressed my concerns. Also, I am very picky when it comes to choosing frames so it was a good thing they had a nice selection to choose from. The receptionist was also very helpful and patient with me during the process haha. Overall experience was great and I will definitely come back for my yearly exam.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The service at the clinic was excellent. Dr. Dinh was kind and attentive, addressing all my concerns during the exam. I was pleasantly surprised by the nice selection of frames available, and the receptionist was helpful and patient throughout the process. I had a great overall experience and will return for my yearly exam.

input: When I ordered my pizza for me and my friends , he pizza was so small and this delivery girl took forever and she was rude and didn't want to give me my change back and she said she thought I gave her a tip no ! And she didn't even give me the right change and it was all coins ! This place sucks ! DONT EAT HERE !!!!!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I ordered a small pizza for me and my friends, but it was too small. The delivery girl was extremely slow, rude, and didn't want to give me my change back. She assumed I gave her a tip, but I hadn't. Moreover, she gave me incorrect change, all in coins. I had a terrible experience with this place and strongly advise against eating here.

input: I was told this place is a must for a Sonoran hot dog. I was visiting from out of town and had never had one. It was good, but the whole Sonoran hot dog isn't really my thing (too many components for me) so I can't say it was great. The guacamole on the other hand, was great! I also had the taco combo - the chicken and carne asada were very good but the cabeza was slimy. BK has a salsa bar that allows you to help yourself to your own toppings and I appreciated that. Service was good, food arrived quickly. It was pretty packed during lunch on a weekday.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is recommended for a Sonoran hot dog, but it wasn't my favorite due to its many components. However, I really enjoyed the guacamole. The taco combo was mostly delicious, except for the slimy cabeza. I appreciated their salsa bar and the service was good with speedy food delivery. It was crowded during lunch on a weekday.

input:
Walked into the restaurant, with reservations, and many open tables.  I asked the manager for a window table and was responded with "they are all reserved."  Two hours later, when we left, still many open tables next to the windows.

Overall food was good.
I had the filet and she had the salmon.
The bottle of wine that was recommended was $75 and was not told prior to ordering it, just that it was the last bottle.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Upon arriving at the restaurant with reservations, I requested a window table from the manager, but was informed that they were all reserved. However, when we left two hours later, there were still many vacant tables next to the windows. Despite this disappointment, the food was satisfying - I had the filet and my companion had the salmon. It should be noted that we were unaware of the $75 price tag on the recommended bottle of wine until after ordering, with the explanation that it was the last bottle available.

input: Best Indian I have ever had! The food was fresh and delicious. Staff are very friendly and attentive and restaurant is clean and welcoming. The paleek paneer and briyani were amazing!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This Indian restaurant is the best I've ever been to. The food is incredibly fresh and delicious, and the staff is friendly, attentive, and welcoming. The restaurant itself is clean and inviting. I highly recommend trying their paleek paneer and biryani - both are amazing!

input: Best smoothies in the whole world. And fresh bread is amazing. Very knowledgeable staff.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: World's best smoothies and amazing fresh bread with knowledgeable staff.

input:
I stopped by Bell Meade during a recent visit to Nashville. The best way for me to describe my experience is to say that the next time I go to Nashville I will go out of my way to make sure I return to Bell Meade.

On my travels, I tend to stop from time to time to see if I can find specific bourbons that may be out locally. At this time of year, I did not expect any great finds because many of the items for which I look have their annual release later in the year so it's a surprise to find any of them on the shelf. For example, Elmer T Lee is a favorite of mine so it was one that I asked about.

Despite the fact that I walked away without Elmer T, I still had a great time. I enjoyed a few tastes at the tasting bar and even better I had a great conversation with Max. He is one of the reasons I will return.

I did walk out with a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream that is not sold locally and there was a bottle on the shelf that I have not seen locally that I need to investigate. As I said I will return and a five star rating from me should say at all.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
During my recent visit to Nashville, I made a stop at Bell Meade. I was pleasantly surprised by my experience there and can confidently say that I will go out of my way to return on my next visit to the city. 

As a bourbon enthusiast, I often look for unique finds during my travels. Although I didn't expect to find any rare bourbons this time of year, I still had a great time exploring the offerings at Bell Meade. While I couldn't find my favorite, Elmer T Lee, I thoroughly enjoyed sampling different selections at the tasting bar. Additionally, I had a wonderful conversation with Max, who made my visit even more enjoyable and memorable. 

Although I didn't leave with Elmer T, I did manage to purchase a bottle of Tennessee whiskey cream that isn't available locally. Furthermore, there was another intriguing bottle on the shelf that caught my eye, which I plan to investigate further. Given my positive experience, it goes without saying that I highly recommend Bell Meade and would give it a five-star rating.

input:
I love trying fresh seafood on piers, wharfs and seaside markets. Most of the time, it is a disappointing experience but this place is not. The food is legitimately fresh and prepared well. The gorgeous view is just a cherry on top of nature's beautiful sundae. I have been here before but ordered the "wrong" thing (cioppino). That wasn't very good when I had it a couple of years ago here. 

We came for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday. Even at 4pm,  there was a wait! We waited about 25 minutes and got a table outdoor. While it wasn't ideal that we sat right in the sun with no shelter other than our sunscreen and sunglasses, the view was worth it. 

We got the local crab special which was a steamed 3-lb. crab served with a salad and soup for $26. I thought this was quite the steal because the crab was huge, delicious and meaty. The garden salad was fresh as simple as it was. The lobster bisque we got was pretty good. (The other options were Caesar salad and clam chowder). They topped off the crab with a couple of onion rings and cups of cocktail sauce and drawn butter. Yum!

We also got the fried platter of shrimp, oysters, calamari and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce and cocktail sauce. As greasy of a meal as this made, it was one of the better fried platters I've had anywhere. The seafood was just really fresh including the sometimes-feared fried oyster. :)

The ice in our iced teas melted away in the sun. Our waitress was so cool and brought us lots of extra ice and an extra iced tea in case we needed it (we did because it was hot out!). She was just friendly and good at her job - five stars for her!

By the time we left at about 6, there were so many people waiting. Make sure you sign up for a seat on the clipboard right when you get there. The restaurant is the last one at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes but it looks like a drive that will upset tires. I parked in the large lot south of the pier and walked 15 minutes up and onto the pier. It was free on a Monday late afternoon.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
I love trying fresh seafood at piers, wharfs, and seaside markets. This place stands out from the rest because the food is legitimately fresh and well-prepared. The view is stunning and adds to the overall experience. I had been here before and had a disappointing meal, but this time was different.

We visited for a late lunch/early dinner on a Monday and even at 4pm, there was a wait. After waiting for about 25 minutes, we got an outdoor table with a beautiful view. Although sitting in the sun without any shelter wasn't ideal, the view made up for it.

We ordered the local crab special, which included a steamed 3-lb. crab, salad, and soup for $26. It was an excellent deal considering the size and taste of the crab. The garden salad was fresh and simple, and the lobster bisque was pretty good. Additionally, we tried the fried platter with shrimp, oysters, calamari, and scallops for $12.95. It came with cole slaw, onion rings, tartar sauce, and cocktail sauce. Despite being a greasy meal, it was one of the best fried platters I've had. The seafood was incredibly fresh, even the fried oyster.

Our iced teas melted quickly in the sun, but our waitress was amazing. She brought us extra ice and an extra iced tea without hesitation. She was friendly and provided excellent service.

When we left around 6pm, there were many people waiting. Make sure to sign up for a seat on the clipboard as soon as you arrive. The restaurant is located at the very end of the pier. Parking on the pier is free for 90 minutes, but it can be rough on tires. I parked in a large lot south of the pier and walked for about 15 minutes to reach the restaurant. It was free to park there on a Monday afternoon.

input:
What a disappointment. This place was not good I would suggest you think twice before selecting this option. The manager and wait staff may possibly be the worst I have ever encountered, rude and definitely not focused on customer service.  The manager is a very angry hostile fella I asked if I could get brown rice instead of white and he blasted me...I offered to pay extra and he stormed off? Do not know what the deal was but this is just plain unprofessional and creepy behavior. The waitresses will smack into you while you are eating...man what a mess this place is from top to bottom.
The food just OK at best! I am seriously complimenting them here... you can do better at home than here. Seriously I am not going to go into you have been warned just yuk...OK? these other folks with the positive reviews for this place must burn off their taste buds with adult beverages. (Didn't try the sake it may be the high point of the joint...but why would I want to expose my taste buds to a substandard meal to enjoy some rice wine? I can do this at home.
 Here is something I am not sure of, I have only lived here a few months now, is it customary to charge for each soda every time you get a refill here? I was charged for each I asked why they said "This is how we do it here." So at $2 bucks per 6-8 ounces of beverage you may want to go with water at this place...but smarter yet! Go elsewhere.
I will not be returning to this establishment.

Worst yet.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place was a huge disappointment. The manager and wait staff were incredibly rude and unprofessional, with the manager being angry and hostile towards me when I asked for a simple substitution. The waitresses were also careless and bumped into me while I was eating. The food was mediocre at best, and I believe I can make better meals at home. To add insult to injury, they charged for each soda refill, which I found unusual and expensive. Overall, this place is a mess and I will not be returning.

input: I was happy his was my first experience with Nola food and not my last, started on a low point. First, I understand it was Sunday night before Fat Tuesday and our waitress was working back to back 12 shifts. However, my drink order was forgotten, and my friends plate was mixed up. For my food, I had the po'boy shrimp and was underwhelmed, there was a hardy serving of shrimp but there was minimal lettuce or sauce and the fries were weak, many soggy. Needless to say, we didn't go back. From other reviews seems like we caught them on an off-day but unfortunately the result is a lack luster review.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Although it was my first experience with Nola food and I was initially happy, the restaurant visit had some disappointments. Despite understanding that our waitress was working long shifts, my drink order was forgotten and my friend's plate was mixed up. Moreover, the po'boy shrimp that I ordered was underwhelming; while there was a generous amount of shrimp, the lack of lettuce, sauce, and weak, soggy fries left much to be desired. It seems like we caught them on an off-day, as other reviews suggest, but unfortunately, this experience led to a lackluster review and we didn't return.

input:
Let's be honest, this place needs a face lift. It's starting to feel shady, I wouldn't even feel comfortable taking my small children here (if I had any, which I don't). The service is mediocre and everything looks tired. The comedy club doesn't feel cheerful or fun, it just feels like the back hallway of a banquet room.

Great parking and good location though. Please owners, please put some money into this place. It really needs it.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place desperately needs improvement with its outdated appearance and lackluster service. It doesn't feel safe for children. The comedy club is lacking in charm and feels uninviting. However, it benefits from convenient parking and a favorable location. The owners are urged to invest in renovations as it is much needed.

input:
I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday.

Arrival: I already read plenty of reviews about no signs marking the location therefore, I looked for Starbucks. I parked in a spot in front of the multi business complex. I went inside to find a guard at a desk that said we have been contracted to hand guests their keys and room number and nothing more. He advised me there was a phone that was on the wall that I could make a call to someone if I needed to. He also stated that the very few parking spots in front were free* only on the weekend.

The Room: This wasn't a room, this was an apartment and I absolutely loved it. It was very spacious and had everything I sought* after for that weekend, such as: fully stocked kitchen, a desk, lots of space, king bed, huge table, nice living room, lots of closets. My only complaint is that I could not open any windows for fresh air...they are nailed/screwed shut. There was also a small welcome bag w cookies and water and papers letting you know where all the food delivery locations and numbers.
There wasn't maid service knocking loudly or trying to barge in early in the morning. This place is more of a long term setting and I'm sure the maids come around during the week Monday-Friday if you desire. I was only here for 3 days and I was fine with that. I went shopping at Shoprite and filled my fridge with water and breakfast to cook.

Overall: This place is awesome, I had a huge living room to entertain my guests when they visited, and a nice desk to study my Anatomy notes. I forgot to mention how quiet** this place is. I loved it. I felt as if no one was there except me. Very quiet* which worked for me on Sunday bc I had lots of studying to do and two TV's to watch The Walking Dead on. Lol!  I would most definitely stay here again. Very spacious and updated. Loved it!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I stayed at the Orange St location from Friday to Monday. Upon arrival, I found the location difficult to locate without signs, but eventually found it near Starbucks. Parking was available in front of the multi business complex, with the guard providing keys and room numbers only. He mentioned the limited free parking spots on the weekends. The room was actually an apartment, which I loved for its spaciousness and amenities. However, the windows were unable to be opened. A welcome bag with cookies, water, and food delivery information was provided. Maid service was not intrusive, and it seemed more suited for long-term stays. Overall, the place was quiet and had a large living room and desk, making it ideal for entertaining guests and studying. I would definitely stay here again due to its spaciousness and modernity.

input: Awesome location, good service is why I have been eating there for the past 15 years off and on. Mostly the excuses about the steak is why I have to write the review. I am happy to pay more for good quality steak but don't blame the poor guy that sold it to you !
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I have been eating at this restaurant off and on for the past 15 years because of its awesome location and good service. However, I feel compelled to write this review mainly due to the constant excuses about the steak. While I am willing to pay more for a quality steak, it's unfair to blame the server for the poor quality if it was sold to them.

input: I had the worst experience of my life and it's not over yet.  I made a mistake in purchasing a vehicle that is out of my budget on a Friday afternoon.  By Sunday after review of my budget I realized I was unable to afford the car.  I called the salesman and tried to explain my situation at 11:30am.  He stated he would speak with his manager and call me back.  At 3:30 after no return call, I called him again, no answer. I left a voicemail and still no call at closing time.  Monday morning I arrived at the dealership as they were opening.  I asked Stephen, the salesman what they determined.  He instructed me to have a seat and he would talk to his management team.  One hour + later, I was called into a cubicle and told my loan had been funded and the title had been changed.  Therefore, I would have to sell the car back to the dealership as a used car.  I would lose a lot of money in doing this.  This morning, Bill head of finance advised that the bank had questions about funding the loan.  I received a call from the bank stating the loan had NOT been funded and they would be unable to okay the loan.  I have left numerous messages with the dealership and have yet to receive a callback.  I contacted an attorney and per his review I again called the dealership and asked for a time to return the vehicle and take back my trade.  Still no response!  These people will lie to your face, avoid this dealership!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had a terrible experience with a dealership. I mistakenly purchased a vehicle that is beyond my budget on a Friday afternoon. By Sunday, I realized I couldn't afford it and tried to explain my situation to the salesman at 11:30am. He said he would speak with his manager and call me back but didn't. I called again at 3:30pm, left a voicemail, but still no response. On Monday morning, I asked about their decision, waiting for over an hour to be called into a cubicle where I was told the loan had already been funded and the title changed. I'd have to sell the car back, losing a significant amount of money. Later, the bank called to inform me that the loan had not been funded and couldn't be approved. I've left multiple messages with the dealership but haven't received a callback. I contacted an attorney and tried reaching out to the dealership again to arrange a return of the vehicle and my trade-in, but they still haven't responded. In conclusion, this dealership is dishonest and should be avoided.

input:
I have been a patron of Desi Village in West Philly for years.  After moving the suburbs, we saw the KOP Desi Village and finally tried it.  We were skeptical having also tried Mood Cafe (owned by the W.Philly folks), and it wasn't as good. But the KOP location is actually very comparable to the West Philly location.  

There is no ambiance or atmosphere here.  The strip mall where it's located is pretty depressing.  Desi Village may be the only active store in it.  And its decor is tired and old.  It is a big space and it appears they do a big lunch buffet but I'm curious if it's ever full.  So don't go for the ambiance.

But the food is good.  We ordered some Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani.  All of it was really good.  Perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy.  I have a nut allergy and made them aware of that and they did not screw it up (most Indian restaurants do).  So we'll definitely be back.  It would be great if they moved into nicer digs but the food is what is most important.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I have been a longtime patron of Desi Village in West Philly and recently tried their KOP location in the suburbs. Despite initial skepticism due to trying another restaurant owned by the West Philly folks, Mood Cafe, the KOP Desi Village proved to be just as good. The strip mall it is located in lacks ambiance, with only Desi Village being an active store. The decor is tired, but the restaurant offers a large space and a lunch buffet. However, the food is excellent. We ordered Keema Naan, Samosas, Saag Paneer, and Lamb Biryani, all of which were perfectly seasoned, not too oily, and appropriately spicy. They were also accommodating to my nut allergy, which is often mishandled by other Indian restaurants. Despite the lackluster atmosphere, we will definitely be returning for the delicious food.

input:
What an AMAZING occurrence that we ended up here after another barbecue place ran out of food!

So yeah, we started out at another spot and they were out of food when we got there. Super bummed and still in the mood for barbecue, we started wandering around Mid City and my trusty Yelp app guided me to this place. We were greeted by the super nice woman working the counter and she explained the whole process.

I decided to get the one-meat plate with "wet" pulled pork, grits and potato salad, I also got a medium mac and cheese, because I can. My boyfriend got the two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken with potato salad and fries. The food blew us both away! It was delicious from beginning to end. The pulled pork was perfect and had the perfect amount of sauce without being drenched. I could tell that if I hadn't ordered it wet it still would have been able to stand on it's own. The mac and cheese was incredible, and after the pork, was my favorite part of the meal. The stone ground grits had a different type of flavor (almost smoky) that I enjoyed and the potato salad was served cold and had that nice crunch that I like in potato salad,

We both agreed that the food was excellent, and a good deal to boot, and that we would both make the trip back out to Earhart, just to have more of this delicious food. The owner himself was bringing the food out to folks and he was really friendly and made sure that we were happy with everything. I like when the owners take the time to make sure that everything is okay. The atmosphere is casual and comfortable and the entire process was a breeze. I will definitely return to LA Smokehouse and I'll be adding it to my "BBQ Favorites" list for future reference.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After being disappointed by another barbecue place running out of food, we stumbled upon this amazing spot in Mid City. Guided by Yelp, we were greeted by a friendly woman who explained the process. The food, including my one-meat plate of "wet" pulled pork with grits and potato salad, and my boyfriend's two-meat plate with brisket and pulled chicken, exceeded our expectations. The pulled pork was perfectly sauced, and even without ordering it "wet," it stood out. The mac and cheese was incredible, while the stone ground grits had a unique smoky flavor. The potato salad had a satisfying crunch. We both agreed that the food was excellent and a good value. We would gladly make the trip back to Earhart for more. The owner was friendly and attentive, and the casual atmosphere made the whole experience enjoyable. LA Smokehouse is now on our list of BBQ favorites.

input:
After today's lunch, Iris has moved to the top of my New Orleans favorites lists--no small feat in a city where restaurants are numerous and culinary competition is fierce. Iris excels in every area: food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music and overall graciousness. I made the reservation for 10-15 people, not knowing exactly how many in my party would show up. Iris pulled out all the stops to make sure everyone had comfortable seating and even prepared an overflow table for us. At no time did we feel jostled or rushed, which is a common fine dining concern. 

The layout of the restaurant allowed diners to move freely to and from the table and to exchange seats as needed. The music selection was fun and unique, ranging from the Magnetic Fields to Johnny Cash. It was also quiet enough to be enjoyed while allowing conversation to flow unimpeded. Our waiter had excellent timing and anticipated our every need. 

Though they don't have a full drink menu for lunch (I hear they have an amazing mixologist for the dinner hour) they do offer a selection of martinis and wines. One of the guests has accounts with several high-end bars in the Quarter, and the drink list passed his muster. Our table settled for Chardonnays, Perseco and chilled shots of Chartreuse, though I hear they have several types of absinthe as well. 

Our group began with slices of warm, heavenly bread that Iris bakes in house. We continued with an assortment of salads--I had the Hollygrove arugula with warm goat cheese, niçoise olives and balsamic vinaigrette. It was fresh perfection. A few of us opted for the mussels, which I heard were delicious. For my main course, I had a wonderful drum with onions prepared in a tangy soy reduction, which was an elegant complement for the fish. I also heard rave reviews about the gnocci and chicken. 

All the entrees were creatively arranged and selected, and at no point did I feel overwhelmed or that any fuss or pretense had gone into the food. I also appreciated that the portions were European-sized (it always makes me laugh when other Americans list too-small portion size as a complaint even when the food is well-prepared!). Iris prepares a lot of their basic ingredients in-house, and I appreciate that the kitchen makes a point of incorporating gulf fish and produce purchased from local, farmer-friendly markets. 

We settled on the prix fixe menu, which was $20 a person for appetizer, main course and the dessert of the day (the best strawberry sorbet I have had yet). With the added drinks and tip it came out to under $35 a person, which is an excellent price for such a delicious white-linen lunch. No matter the size of my group, I will definitely be returning!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After an impressive lunch at Iris in New Orleans, the restaurant has quickly become one of my top favorites in the city. Despite the strong culinary competition, Iris excels in all aspects including food, drinks, service, atmosphere, location, music, and overall graciousness. They effortlessly accommodated my reservation for a group of 10-15 people, providing comfortable seating and even preparing an overflow table. The restaurant's layout allowed us to move freely and the music selection added to the enjoyable ambiance without hindering conversation. The waiter's impeccable timing and attentiveness further enhanced our dining experience. Although the lunch menu didn't offer a full drink selection, their martinis and wines were sufficient, earning approval from one of our guests who has experience with high-end bars. We began with delectable house-baked bread and proceeded to enjoy various salads and mouth-watering entrees like mussels, drum with onions, gnocchi, and chicken. The presentation and portion sizes were pleasing, and I appreciated Iris' emphasis on using locally sourced ingredients. Opting for the prix fixe menu at $20 per person, which included an appetizer, main course, and a delightful strawberry sorbet dessert, our total bill, including drinks and tip, amounted to under $35 per person. With such a wonderful experience, I will definitely be returning to Iris regardless of the size of my group.

input:
Great atmosphere and decor. Super friendly staff seat you right away. I stopped once for lunch and one time for dinner. They have some lunch specials one of which was Pad Thai. I order with chicken as the protein but they have the typical options for this .  The portion was good for lunch and had good flavor.

For dinner I ordered the chicken satay to start and the Panang Curry with chicken for main course. I was very disappointed in the satay being that you only get two small skewers. The flavor and peanut dipping sauce were very good but they give a few more skewers.  The Panang was good and you get a good size portion of rice.

On a side note, I was disappointed they do not have Pad See Ew. Still some other options on the menu I will return to try.

The staff and manager really know customer service.  Look forward to returning soon!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
Great atmosphere and decor, with super friendly staff who seat you right away. They have lunch specials, including one with Pad Thai. I ordered it with chicken, but they offer other protein options. The portion for lunch was good and it had great flavor.

For dinner, I had the chicken satay as an appetizer and the Panang Curry with chicken as the main course. The satay was a bit disappointing as you only get two small skewers, but the flavor and peanut dipping sauce were really good. The Panang was enjoyable and came with a good portion of rice.

I was disappointed that they don't have Pad See Ew, but there are other options on the menu that I will return to try. The staff and manager provide excellent customer service. I look forward to going back soon!

input: We randomly decided to look for middle eastern food. Came up with Petra Restaurant near our home. Tried it with my family and liked it quite a bit. Try their Friday and Saturday special rice (it actually test like Indian fried rice) with lamb. Really tasty. Other things are very good too. Don't be discouraged with the location of the place, but food is good and inside of the restaurant is quite nice. Service is good too.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We randomly tried Petra Restaurant, a Middle Eastern eatery near our home, with my family and found it to be quite enjoyable. The Friday and Saturday special rice, which tastes similar to Indian fried rice, paired with lamb, is particularly delicious. Despite its location, the food is excellent and the interior of the restaurant is pleasant. The service is also commendable.

input: I went to the pearl for my birthday and every detail of the experience was awesome!  The food, the wine and the service were all impeccable!  We didn't realize the time and were chatting away after closing time and the staff never made us feel rushed.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had an amazing birthday experience at the pearl. The food, wine, and service were impeccable. Even after closing time, the staff never made us feel rushed and allowed us to chat away.

input: I stopped in because I was hungry for some snacks.  Browsed the store since I had some spare time and found it to be clean and well stocked.  Wide isles, good selection of bakery stuff, flowers and all your usual groceries. I like that they had some locally made snacks too like California Kettle Corn and Taco Works (out of SLO).  Found the semi-unusual chips I wanted that other stores don't always carry, grabbed a Diet Coke by the checkout and I was happy.  Convenient parking lot and the staff was friendly and helpful.  Thanks Albertsons!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I stopped by because I was hungry for snacks and wanted to browse the store when I had spare time. I found it clean and well stocked, with wide aisles and a good selection of bakery items, flowers, and usual groceries. I was pleased to see locally made snacks like California Kettle Corn and Taco Works (out of SLO). I easily found the semi-unusual chips I wanted, which are not always available at other stores. Lastly, I grabbed a Diet Coke at the checkout and left happy. The convenient parking lot and friendly, helpful staff made my experience even better. Thank you, Albertsons!

input: New owners turned it into a double threat: Bad food AND bad service. Shame. I loved this place.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Under new ownership, this place unfortunately became a double threat with both bad food and bad service, which is a shame because I used to love it.

input:
We see Dr. Gloudemans, and she's a wonderful doctor. Friendly, upbeat, up on the most recent research, and pro-vaxx (hooray!!). She's proactive about problems after making sure things are worth worrying about-- "let's keep an eye on this, and if there's still a problem in a month or two, come back in and we'll see about a referral to a specialist."

As others have mentioned, we've had a few billing hiccups. We received a bill saying we were past due on 3 appointments' fees, despite paying all copays in the office. Luckily it was all straightened out after a phone call, but it's been frustrating on that front.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We love Dr. Gloudemans - she's a friendly, upbeat, and knowledgeable doctor who stays current with the latest research. She strongly supports vaccinations, which is great. She takes a proactive approach by closely monitoring any concerns before considering referrals to specialists. However, we have experienced some billing issues. We received a bill stating that we were overdue on fees for three appointments, even though we had paid all the copays at the office. Thankfully, a phone call resolved the issue, but it has been frustrating to deal with.

input: I attended a meeting for the homebuilders Association of New Orleans here. The food was good and they took good care of the patrons. I had a mimosa which was good. I had a small cup of corn and crab soup which is fantastic but the portion was quite small. I had the grits and grillades and it was fantastic! The portion same grade on this one. The price was around $10. I've included a photo of the menu for your convenience. I didn't get a chance to test the Wi-Fi but I would say given the ambience and the quality of the food it's a repeat
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I attended a meeting for the Homebuilders Association of New Orleans. The food was good and they took good care of the patrons. I had a good mimosa and a small, yet fantastic, cup of corn and crab soup. The grits and grillades were also fantastic, with a similar portion size. The price was around $10. I have included a photo of the menu. Although I didn't test the Wi-Fi, considering the ambiance and food quality, I would definitely come back.

input: I work at the Frist and I don't eat at the cafe much, since I like to leave the building and go home for lunch. But once in a blue moon on a really dreary day like today, I stay in and have the Cobb Salad. It's a go-to for gluten free noshers like me. Add an extra egg for extra protein punch (as if all the meat wasn't enough already) and oil and vinegar dressing and i'm doing ok. A lot of museum visitors and local employees come for the cheap prices and quick bites. Beware of Senior Mondays (every 3rd Monday of the month) and weekends at lunchtime- it's usually busiest at 1130-noon.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I work at the Frist and rarely eat at the cafe. However, on occasion, like today, I have the Cobb Salad as a gluten-free option. I add an extra egg for more protein, along with oil and vinegar dressing. The cafe is popular among museum visitors and local employees due to its affordable prices and fast service. On Senior Mondays (every 3rd Monday of the month) and weekends during lunchtime, it tends to be busiest between 11:30 am and noon.

input:
The food at Ghini's is just delicious. Everything for French breakfast imaginable, and more. I highly recommend the eggs provencale, not something you can get anywhere else. Two eggs basted with a sliced hot house tomato, thyme, garlic and herbs de provance. Get the baguette toast and add the great hashbrowns for a mere dollar.
My personal favorite are all the crepes, both sweet and savory. Especially recommend the spinach and swiss.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Ghini's serves delicious food, including a variety of French breakfast options. Highly recommended is the unique and exclusive dish called eggs provencale, consisting of two eggs basted with a sliced hot house tomato, thyme, garlic, and herbs de provence. To complete the meal, try the baguette toast and add the tasty hashbrowns for just a dollar. Additionally, Ghini's offers a range of crepes, both sweet and savory, with the spinach and swiss crepe being a personal favorite.

input: This was such a unique spot, from the graffiti style art on the walls to the delicious food options and special hummus flavors. Good prices, great portion size. I had the greek steak pita with guac hummus. Will definitely be back!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Unique spot with graffiti style art on walls, delicious food options, and special hummus flavors. Good prices, generous portions. Tried the Greek steak pita with guac hummus, definitely going back!

input:
I really like Prep & Pastry - we have been twice in the last two months on a Sunday.  The best trick I learned is to put your name on the waitlist BEFORE YOU ARRIVE.  As long as you are within 5 miles of the restaurant, you can be added.  It is a great service.

I have tried a number of things for brunch and all have been excellent - even their sweets. I think my favorite is the breakfast sandwich.  I am not a big drinker, so I usually order the ice team and it really is better than almost anything else I have tried. 

Staff is really, really nice.  I highly recommend a visit if you are in town.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love Prep & Pastry! We've been twice in the last two months on a Sunday. The best trick I learned is to put your name on the waitlist before you arrive. As long as you're within 5 miles, you can be added. It's a great service. Their brunch options are excellent, including their sweets. My favorite is the breakfast sandwich. I'm not a big drinker, so I usually order their ice tea, which is better than almost anything else I've tried. The staff is really, really nice. I highly recommend visiting if you're in town.

input:
Another great annual festival Edmonton has to offer.

The Fringe is over two weekends and the joining week full of performances. There's a variety of venues and plays to watch, street performers and musicians. There's a schedule online to find show times, buy tickets and learn more about the artists. 

Half of 104th closes down to add space for a variety of food vendors and artisan vendors (art, jewelry, clothing, etc.).

Good tip: there's a gourmet mini donut truck off behind the farmers market a bit tucked away. Amazing!

It's nice to take an hour or two before or after a show to walk around and casually stumble on other street performances. Or even go without seeing a play just to snack and shop at the vendors.

The location is absolutely fabulous.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Edmonton's annual festival, The Fringe, is a must-see event held over two weekends and a joining week, showcasing a wide range of performances from various venues and plays. Attendees can enjoy street performers, musicians, and explore the schedule online to plan their show times and purchase tickets. Furthermore, a portion of 104th Street is closed to accommodate an assortment of food and artisan vendors, offering art, jewelry, clothing, and more. Don't miss the hidden gem of a gourmet mini donut truck located behind the farmers market. The festival's location is absolutely fabulous, making it perfect for leisurely strolling and stumbling upon other street performances, or simply indulging in snacks and shopping at the vendors.

input:
Wow have things changed at this location. I used to come here on a regular basis with a friend. I haven't been back in over a year and so couldn't wait to have lunch today. I was surprised at the deterioration in customer service...,.our server didn't smile, was unwilling to give a recommendation and didn't offer us a tea to go. When I used to come, every server was friendly, gave suggestions and always offered a tea to go. 

The food was okay and probably would have been better if we had been treated better.  I noticed there was tape on the benches where the leather/vinyl is wearing out; this looks tacky.

This used to be my favorite lunch spot; this is no longer the case. I will not be back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I'm disappointed with the changes at this location. I used to frequent it regularly with a friend, but hadn't returned in over a year. Today, I was surprised by the deterioration in customer service. Our server was unfriendly, unhelpful, and didn't offer us a tea to go, which used to be a standard practice here. Even the food, though okay, could have been better if we had been treated better. Furthermore, I noticed tape on the benches where the leather/vinyl is wearing out, which looks tacky. This place used to be my favorite lunch spot, but it's no longer the case. I have no intentions of returning.

input:
Got an estimate but went with another plumber as this was the highest quote of the 3 plumbers we interviewed for the job.
Very prompt communication though.

Will re-consider for future jobs.  Seems reliable (and often you get what you pay for!)
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Obtained an estimate but selected a different plumber due to their higher quote compared to the other two interviewed. However, their communication was impressive. We will reconsider hiring them for future projects, as they appear reliable (and quality usually comes with a higher price).

input: Only the best Mexican food in Florida!!!!  Since the first day I tried it I love it I keep coming back!!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Best Mexican food in Florida! Kept coming back since my first try, absolutely love it!

input: Real Thai food and they'll make it spicy if you ask for it pet pet. I really like both their soups. The curries have excellent flavor but they can seem runny if you're not used to Thai curries. I'm not super thrilled with the eggrolls but my girlfriend always gets the veggie ones. Perhaps the meat ones are better.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Authentic Thai food with the option to add spice upon request. Their soups are particularly enjoyable. Though the curries are flavorful, they may appear watery to those unfamiliar with Thai cuisine. The vegetable eggrolls are preferred by my girlfriend, but the meat ones might be an improved alternative.

input:
Last May, my wife and I used Jump on the School Bus to take our wedding guests on a winery and brewery tour. They were just amazing, the perfect choice for our pre-wedding wine and beer tour and for wedding transportation between Goleta and the Circle Bar-B Ranch for our guests who stayed in town. Darin and Sierra did a wonderful job communicating with us in Washington, DC as we planned our wedding itinerary. They were flexible about trip times and made last minute adjustments when the number of in-town guests changed suddenly. 

Darin and Sierra have such attention to detail and quality that Darin even stopped by one of the wineries to meet us and to ensure that everything was as expected. Our driver was also extremely knowledgeable about the area and had many good suggestions throughout the day.

We couldn't have picked a better choice for a winery, brewery day tour and wedding day transportation than Jump on the School Bus! I highly recommend them to everyone!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
Last May, my wife and I had an amazing experience with Jump on the School Bus. We used their services for a winery and brewery tour during our pre-wedding activities and for transportation on our wedding day. Darin and Sierra, the owners, were great at communicating with us from Washington, DC as we planned our itinerary. They were flexible with trip times and made last minute adjustments when the number of guests changed. 

Darin went above and beyond by personally visiting one of the wineries to ensure everything was perfect. Our driver was also knowledgeable and provided helpful suggestions throughout the day. Overall, we couldn't have made a better choice than Jump on the School Bus for our tour and wedding transportation. I highly recommend them to everyone!

input:
A great spot to take out-of-town guests. I take all my Chicago friends here and they fall in love. The burgers are incredible and the boozy shakes are like no other. The first time I had horchata shake I honestly had dreams about it for like a week. It's also super centrally located, a quick walk from Wash Ave and other downtown attractions. Great vibe, although I always prefer to get a table upstairs than sit at the community tables on the ground floor.

The burger selection is really, really great. You can pretty much get whatever your heart desires. I've had mac n cheese patties on my burger, you can get a bison burger, turkey burger, literally anything. I have tried a ton and have never been let down by the flavor combinations. The waiters are always super honest, in a good way. If you ask them what's better, X or Y, they're not going to jerk you around and say they're equally good. They'll give you their honest opinion. LOVE that. 

Another unique aspect about Bailey's Range is that they have a burger showdown (can't remember their technical term for it) where last week's featured burger goes up against a new burger recipe. It's a cool call-out that you don't see at a lot of other restaurants. 

The only reason I gave it a 4/5 star instead of 5/5 is because I've had a couple of instances (out of MANY visits, so it's really not alarming or anything) where I requested my burger medium or medium-rare and it turned out a little well done. I still ate it, but it wasn't really what I expected.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Bailey's Range is a must-visit spot for out-of-town guests and Chicago friends. The incredible burgers and unique boozy shakes make it a favorite. Its central location near Wash Ave and other downtown attractions is convenient. While the community tables on the ground floor are okay, I prefer getting a table upstairs for a better vibe. The burger selection is extensive, allowing you to customize your burger with various options like mac n cheese patties, bison, or turkey. The flavor combinations never disappoint. The honest waiters are a plus, providing genuine recommendations. One distinctive feature is the burger showdown, where last week's featured burger competes with a new recipe. The only drawback is that, on rare occasions, the requested medium or medium-rare burger may turn out slightly overcooked, which I experienced a few times. Overall, it's a 4/5 star experience.

input: Possibly the best breakfast sandwich EVER.  On a biscuit!  Oh my gosh, it was so good!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The best breakfast sandwich ever, on a biscuit! It was unbelievably delicious.

input:
This place sucks! The one up on oracle and wetmore is where I usually go, however, I moved and the university location is closer. Sorry Silver mine you have lost my business forever.

First, I ordered two sandwiches a large homesteak  with no green onions. I accidentally typed onions instead of peppers that come on the sandwich. These bozos still proceed to put the greens on it and the manager laughs it off like no big deal. 
Second, my hot homesteak sandwich was as cold as if had been sitting out for an hour. You guessed right it took an hour to get my food and then the hot sandwich was not wrapped in the proper wrapping to keep it warm.
Lastly, the employee got rude with me when I was checking to see what time my order would be done. He proceeded to scold me about how he only got it two minutes ago and it will be done when its done. Not how you talk to a customer buddy!

Goodbye Silver mine!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had a terrible experience at the Silver Mine location on Oracle and Wetmore. I usually go there, but I moved closer to the university location. I ordered a large homesteak sandwich without green onions, but they still put them on. The manager didn't seem to care and laughed it off. Additionally, my hot homesteak sandwich was cold, as if it had been sitting out for an hour. It took an hour to get my food and it wasn't even wrapped properly to keep it warm. To top it off, an employee was rude to me when I asked about the status of my order. I won't be going back to Silver Mine again. Goodbye!

input: My first time here! Grace did my hair....and it's FABULOUS! (And my hair is very difficult---super long and super thick). Great atmosphere, too--modern and clean, and no snobbiness.  Totally reasonable pricing! Highly recommend!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: First time at Grace's and she did a fabulous job on my difficult hair (super long and super thick). Great modern and clean atmosphere without any snobbiness. Pricing is totally reasonable. Highly recommended!

input: Food was good, we took advantage of the Sunday Buffet it included fried chicken, greens, smother steak, corn, cabbage.  It was so much more  It was very,very cozy. You would actually think you were eating at your grandmother's house.  This is not a fine dining establishment.  The price was fair, was highly recommended by locals. It's was worth any wait. This place exceeded my expectations.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food was delicious, especially the Sunday Buffet which had various dishes such as fried chicken, greens, smother steak, corn, and cabbage. The cozy ambiance made it feel like dining at your grandmother's house. Despite not being a fancy restaurant, the fair prices and high recommendations from locals made it worth any wait. Overall, this place exceeded my expectations.

input: Ordered a Passion Passport, I love the name! It contains Passion Fruit Juice Blend, Bananas, Pineapple Mango Juice Blend, Papaya Juice Blend, and Raw Cane Sugar. It was delicious and refreshing!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I ordered a Passion Passport, which I loved for its name. This delightful drink is made with a blend of Passion Fruit Juice, Bananas, Pineapple Mango Juice, Papaya Juice, and Raw Cane Sugar. It was incredibly delicious and refreshing.

input: Thoroughly enjoyed our private tour today with Carrie (it was very rainy so not too many visitors).  Her knowledge and passion about the Civil War was captivating. The Battle of Franklin deserves such a memorial.
