Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I highly recommend Jenna Moore for hair services. She listened to my goals and delivered. My hair has been a work in progress for over a year, but today, Jenna successfully gave me the A-line bob I desired. She is amazing and ensured we were on the same page throughout the process. I have confidence that Jenna will help heal and grow my hair to achieve my desired results.

input: Fast.  Fresh.  The carne was very good.  So was the guacamole.  Wish there was the ability to customize taco toppings.  The tortilla chips were too thick.  The dulche de leche  soft serve ice cream was amazingly delicious.  Wish that there was more seating.  Wish that table clean ups were more timely and more thorough.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Fast and fresh, the carne and guacamole were excellent. Would like the option to customize taco toppings. The tortilla chips were too thick. The dulche de leche soft serve ice cream was incredibly delicious. More seating would be appreciated. Table clean ups could be more timely and thorough.

input:
Would it be weird if I wanted to move in and permanently live here!? The style of this salon is impeccable. The color palette and decor they chose makes it feel like you're in a Restoration Hardware magazine...in France...surrounded by heirloom antiques. I didn't know what to expect when arriving but I was pleasantly surprised with their upscale polish options like Chanel and many others I actually didn't know I needed in my life until I arrived. 
Service was prompt and I especially enjoyed the extended massage. Most importantly the tools she used were brand new/ had been sterilized. I watched her open the fresh package up, that made me feel good about cleanliness and safety. I don't know if all nail salons have cute gold tips on their nail trimmer tools but now I want them for my own collection. 

I picked a gray color for my toes and did OPI Funny Bunny gel on my nails. So far I'm loving both! 
So nice to see a high end nail salon finally making its way to Nashville. I've gone to others in Nashville that seem to be high end, but it just ends up like a VIP club on the Vegas strip with loud music and sparkles just waiting for a Justin Bieber song to come on. 
CURED was not only high end, but it was classic. Like The Hamptons type of classic but with a comfortable low key brunch with girlfriends mimosa type of vibe. I think it would be amazing for a bridal party with so many photo opportunities. I felt comfortable with their prices, competitive to anywhere else I've gone in Nashville worth mentioning. 

I didn't know where to park so I parked on the side in a random parking lot. Looks like there's a lot of up and coming businesses beside them under construction. So I'm assuming once those are complete, parking will be pretty straight forward? 

When my Mom & Sister come into town next I'm going to take them here & go to Local Honey for lunch since it's so close. 

Can't wait to go back. Welcome to the neighborhood!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Is it strange if I want to move in here? This salon has impeccable style, with a color palette and decor that makes it feel like a page from a Restoration Hardware magazine in France, surrounded by heirloom antiques. I was pleasantly surprised by their upscale polish options like Chanel, which I didn't know I needed in my life until now. The service was prompt and the extended massage was great. The tools used were new and sterilized, which made me feel good about cleanliness and safety. The gray color on my toes and OPI Funny Bunny gel on my nails are both looking great. It's nice to finally have a high-end nail salon in Nashville that is elegant and classic, without the loud music and sparkle of a Vegas strip club. The pricing is competitive and parking may improve once the neighboring businesses are completed. I'm planning to bring my mom and sister here when they visit, and we'll check out Local Honey for lunch since it's nearby. Can't wait to go back! Welcome to the neighborhood!

input: I've been coming to this place for years now, and even though I now live in Colorado, I come back here every time I'm in Philadelphia for work (which is often). I've tried many items on the menu and many were great, portions are generous, and prices are low. My go to item - Indian Mee Goreng, I can eat that every day of the week if I could, it's that good. Maybe one day I can get the recipe from the manager so I can actually do that on days I'm in CO.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Despite now residing in Colorado, I have continued to frequent this place for several years. Each time I am in Philadelphia for work, which happens frequently, I make sure to return here. The menu offers a variety of excellent options, with generous portions and affordable prices. Personally, I highly recommend the Indian Mee Goreng – it is so delicious that I could eat it daily. Perhaps one day, I will convince the manager to share the recipe with me, allowing me to enjoy it even when I am in Colorado.

input: not impressed!..... the service was great but the pizza i ordered was not good. i love Stella and Trenos pizza so i wast expecting the same type. no desire to return again

input: This has fast become one of my favorite New Orleans gems! Enter over at the bridge on Peters near Elysian Fields or a little way up on Piety, either way, if you like breezes and city views, your efforts will be rewarded. The path stretches about a 1.25 miles from close to Elysian Fields over to the area near the old Navy installation. Along the way are various art installations, a dog park, and a wonderful walk along the mighty Mississippi River. If you time it just right, you might catch one of the spectacular sunsets. A beautiful way to end any day in NOLA!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This is one of my favorite New Orleans gems! Enter at the bridge on Peters near Elysian Fields or a little way up on Piety. The path stretches about 1.25 miles from close to Elysian Fields to the old Navy installation, with various art installations, a dog park, and a wonderful walk along the mighty Mississippi River. input: Yelp doesn't allow to leave 0 star review, so that is why you see one star. Me and my wife are moving from NY to South California, and we contacted 5 different moving companies. input: I really enjoy this theater! input:
4-5 stars, this is just after one visit so far, worth a try if you're a thai fan. I liked the food, but you always have to have the first visit to see "how they do things" and figure out what your preferences will need to be.

I did use their living social deal so I brought my dad in when he came in from out of town to try it out with me. I like the set up, the quaint house is cute (and well, quaint), but I can see how it wouldn't be ideal it if was jam packed. I imagine you could potentially do family style for some of the pub height tabletops. I did call ahead to make sure that I didn't need to print out the coupon and it could be used from my ipod and to make sure they were open, as the website said to just double check.

We started with shrimp spring rolls, probably the best I've had, the ingredients seemed fresher, and crispier. No shredded lettuce here. Simple and loosely wrapped, but you could taste the individual components. The peanut sauce was tasty too, though they don't have sirracha (spelling?) to add to it, just dried pepper flakes. 

We then got the tom yum (gai?) with shrimp. I know it is hot (because of the name, duh), I usually prefer it a little less spicy (I am white), though I still got a good sour flavor (for instance at Thai chili it's too hot for me, I don't taste any sour). I usually get my tom yum without meat or seafood because I feel the meat gets dried out, but the server assured me the shrimp wouldn't be overcooked, and they weren't. I think they are making sure to use fresh ingredients, but I do prefer straw mushrooms (I think they are usually canned) over the button mushrooms they used. Next time I am probably going to try out a veggie version (i love the soup with the cabbage, and broccoli). The owner did tell me they are trying to be authentic and so maybe button mushrooms and less veggies is more authentic?

We then got shrimp pad thai and chicken pad keo mao (drunken noodle) minus the red pepper. Both were tasty, the portions were probably a little less than other places in Reno (not sure if just lunch sized portion now that I think about it).

Like Ernie said, the pad thai noodles were a little soft, overdone, and its not the 'orange-y' sauce like other pad thai's, but there was still flavor there. The shrimp were also tasty in this dish. The drunken noodles was done exactly how I like them, lots of baby corns and the noodles covered in the sauce and of course spicy. 

My dad and I talked outside for a while and the husband did come out and talk with me about the food, and asked if I was happy (we were outside a while). I hope the living social deals bring in some business, and I do plan on coming back, it is just hard because I don't live in the area. I also asked about the cooking classes (they are a steal at $65), and on facebook it said they are looking to improve and give some focus to that side of the business. The owner did say that they use just a regular kitchen so no woks or anything like that (meaning what they teach us can actually be done at home), I wonder if that is why the pad thai noodles are that way? Regardless, they seem to pride themselves on authentic and quality food and service.

I did include pictures. Oh I did try a thai iced tea for the first time too, pretty tasty, reminded me of chai tea. 

I didn't get to see the bill closely, but it was $24 and some change after the living social deal (takes $20 off), I didn't think that was too bad for 2 for lunch (the total cost), with an appetizer and soup and a drink.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: 4-5 stars, worth a try for Thai food. Good experience on first visit. Used a living social deal and brought my dad. Quaint house setup, might be crowded. Called ahead and had a pleasant experience. Started with delicious shrimp spring rolls. Tom yum soup was a little too spicy, but still had good flavor. Pad Thai and drunken noodles were tasty, but portions were slightly smaller. Owner talked to us outside and seemed passionate about the business. Planning on coming back, even though I don't live nearby. Asked about cooking classes. Bill was $24 with deal, reasonable for two people with appetizer, soup, and drink. Overall, enjoyed the experience and even tried Thai iced tea for the first time.

input:

They've got lululemon, Jacob, Danier, Gap, Club Monaco, American Eagle, and a variety of other shops that work for me, and it's never so busy you have to brush past people in the halls.

The food court has a ton of seating. It's never completely full. There's a Zellers and a dollar store and a Sears. I just wish they had a Bay and a movie theatre to round it out a bit. Otherwise, Kingsway is as good a mall as I need.

I often go to Kingsway instead of West Ed for shopping. They have stores like lululemon, Jacob, Danier, Gap, Club Monaco, and American Eagle. It's not too crowded, so you don't have to push through people.

input:

Sorry to say this curry was not great, the sauce was very heavy on the salt and tomato and the goat was tough as an old boot, the naan bread was below mediocre. Only nice thing was the rice.  Very Very dissapointed
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: My favorite Indian restaurant in St. Louis is Spice and Grill on Olive. However, my husband suggested trying out Indias Kitchen for a change. We ordered a portion of goat curry, but unfortunately, it was not great. The sauce was overly salty with a strong taste of tomato, and the goat was tough. input:
Yes, it's a little pricey, but it was darned near worth it. 
It certainly didn't seem a priority to get us our menus, but once they did, the service was pretty on point. The bread was good. I ordered a chopped salad and a crab cake, and the hub got a crab cake sandwich with fries. We had water to drink, no appetizers-walked out for $45 with tip. The food came quickly.  My food was great-and I'm no salad eater. The crab cake was quality, fries were good. 
Another drawback is that we had to sit in the bar area bc it was after 9. The table was the size of a chair, 3 plates were too much.

P.S. i used my bank card, and noticed that I was charged significantly more than I agreed to, so I called the restaurant. The manager said it's a banking glitch, and should correct itself before the money comes out of my account... It better.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Although expensive, the overall experience was almost worth it. Initially, the service was slow but improved after we received our menus. The bread was enjoyable and our main dishes - a chopped salad and a crab cake for me, and a crab cake sandwich with fries for my partner - were satisfying. We didn't order any appetizers and only had water to drink. The total bill, including tip, came to $45. The food arrived quickly and my salad, despite not being a salad person, was excellent. The crab cake and fries were also of high quality. However, one downside was being seated in the bar area due to our late arrival, resulting in a small table that couldn't accommodate all our plates. Moreover, there was an issue with overcharging on my bank card, but the restaurant manager assured me it was a banking error and would be resolved prior to the money being deducted from my account.

input:

input: My partner and I split the vegetarian platter and left stuffed! Delicious food, very kind and attentive staff.  Will help you make decisions on ordering and certainly won't take advantage of you. Will definitely be back.

input:
i enjoyed the experience eating here and will definitely go back.

first of all, there are vegetarian options on the menu. we started with the veggie spring rolls which were hot, crisp, and delicious. my husband had the duck and rice vermicelli soup which we both agreed was great in a yummy, savory broth. i had the beef pho which i didn't care for because the meat was a bit grisly and i'm not a fan of tripe. i've not eaten a lot of pho and wasn't sure what to order, though. they offer several different beef cuts and i should have picked a different one. next time. also, the regular serving size was way more than enough. i don't think either of us could have come close to finishing the largest bowls.

the restaurant was clean and quiet with a sparse, yet very 80s decor. the server was quick and attentive.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I enjoyed dining here and will return. They offer vegetarian options on their menu. We had delicious veggie spring rolls to start. My husband loved the duck and rice vermicelli soup, which had a yummy, savory broth. I, however, didn't like the beef pho because the meat was a bit grisly and I'm not a fan of tripe. I should have ordered a different beef cut. The serving size was also generous. The restaurant was clean, quiet, and had a sparse, 80s decor. The server provided quick and attentive service.

input:
3.5 stars.

Chickie's and Pete's is a friendly sports bar, particularly for women, and it has lots of seating for Sunday games. I appreciate the sound booth in the sky, as it means that (admittedly bad) music is played during the commercials, along with special themes for Eagles fans. And, the place seems to be smoke free.

But, I am not impressed by the famous crab fries, which are crinkled, lightly fried, and seasoned with garlic, chili pepper, and salt. Something about the congealed cheese sauce detracts from the entire experience, and I also prefer my fries to be piping hot. However, there are towers of beer available (complete with taps), which is pleasantly tacky. 

With loads of space, booming sound, cute servers, and rowdy fans, Chickie's and Pete's is a perfect place to catch a game.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Chickie's and Pete's is a friendly sports bar with lots of seating for Sunday games. They have a sound booth in the sky playing music and special themes for Eagles fans. The place is smoke free. However, the famous crab fries with congealed cheese sauce are not to be impressed with and the fries are not piping hot. They have towers of beer available. With ample space, booming sound, cute servers, and rowdy fans, it is a perfect place to catch a game.

input: Pancake Pantry is an institution in Nashville. A place to see country stars and have a great breakfast. Pancakes are good. It's a thing to do in Nashville. Plan to stand in line and enjoy the conversation.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Pancake Pantry is a renowned Nashville institution where you can enjoy a delicious breakfast and spot country stars. The pancakes are particularly noteworthy, making it a must-visit destination in Nashville. While a wait in line is expected, it provides an opportunity to engage in pleasant conversations.

input: I have been a loyal customer at Magasin Cafe for years, it's what made me fall in love with Vietnamese food. Since Magasin Cafe has closerd for renovations I came to Magasin Kitcheb to curb my weekly pho cravings. The food and service were good- even the chopped was seasoned better than the other location. However, paying more money for the same meal and the restaurants atmosphere deters the ranking. Quality food and service will continue to keep me a loyal customer.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I have been a loyal customer at Magasin Cafe for years and it's where my love for Vietnamese food began. Since they closed for renovations, I have been coming to Magasin Kitchen to satisfy my weekly pho cravings. The food and service here are good, and even the chopped is seasoned better than the other location. However, the higher price and less appealing atmosphere of this restaurant affect my overall ranking. Despite this, I will still remain a loyal customer as long as they continue to provide quality food and service.

input: I love this place...stop whenever I can; either at this location or the Philadelphia one. I could eat the cumin style lamb every day of the week. But honestly, all of their food is good. I'm definitely a fan of their rabbit appetizer. People can argue about how authentically Sichuan it is...whatever. The only place I've actually had Sichuan food taste exactly like they serve in Sichuan Province was when I went to Chengdu. This place is well worth eating at.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love this place and visit whenever possible, whether at this spot or the Philadelphia branch. The cumin style lamb is my absolute favorite, I could eat it every day. However, all of their food is excellent. Their rabbit appetizer is also a personal favorite of mine, despite debates about its authenticity. The only place where I've tried Sichuan food that truly matched the flavors of Sichuan Province was in Chengdu, but this place is still highly recommended.

input:
A quasi political rant and a store review all wrapped in one, so enjoy. 

Ever since Target hit the scene I really have to ask, "Who even goes to Kmart anymore?" I asked this to myself out loud the other day as I had to get my meds filled due to a sinus infection. No one looked at me odd, as there seemed to be several people talking to themselves. I now go here because of the stolid contractual war between Express Scripts and Walgreens. Thanks you two....idiots.....qausi-political rant over.

This store is harshly bright, rather dingy, and the selections, especially in the electronic section, are on the cheaper end.  On top of that, I've found the mainstream DVD and Blu-Ray movies are overpriced.  I laughed at the men's area, especially the young man's department, as they had a tv with music videos playing. I laughed because it just seemed a lame attempt to be cool and creating a shopping experience that you will find at a department store like Macy's or Dillard's. This is hard to create when everything is whitewashed. You will feel like you are in that August Burns Red's "Whitewashed."  The best WTF moment is discovering the opportunity to purchase Joe Boxer male thongs. Who knew that Kmart cared about male panty line?

One great tip is you can find patio furniture cheap during the off season and clearance days. I bought a great patio table for under $50. So, keep that in mind.

The extra star is for the pharmacy, as they filled my prescription out efficiently and with the greatest of ease. The hours are little later than Target.  No problems there and credit when credit is due!

The later 80s quote, "K-Mart sucks", remains as true as ever and who knows, you may even bump into someone who still dresses from that Tom Cruise era who cares about male panty line. One never knows?
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Target has made me question why anyone still goes to Kmart. The store is poorly lit and the selection, especially in electronics, is cheap. The prices for mainstream DVD and Blu-Ray movies are also too high. The attempt to create a cool shopping experience falls flat, and everything feels whitewashed. However, I did find good deals on patio furniture during clearance days. The pharmacy deserves credit for efficient prescription filling, though the store's hours are not as convenient as Target's. Kmart remains lackluster and outdated, attracting even people who care about male panty lines from the Tom Cruise era.

input: The Tuck Special. So good I would drive all the way back out to Nashville from TX just to have it again. It's a mix of strange ingredients- brisket, egg, pimento cheese but combined they are an amazing flavor combination. My husband didn't care for the BBQ sauce on the table, but meat was pretty good. I can see how this place gets crowded, but if you have patience and look up the menu ahead of time, it should be manageable.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The Tuck Special is an incredibly delicious dish that is worth driving all the way from Texas to Nashville just to have again. It combines unusual ingredients like brisket, egg, and pimento cheese, resulting in an amazing flavor combination. While my husband wasn't a fan of the BBQ sauce provided, the meat itself was quite good. The restaurant tends to get crowded, but with a bit of patience and checking the menu beforehand, it should be manageable.

input: The restaurant smelled like a toilet.  I couldn't stand it.  My daughter and I got the meals to go and the guy put them in the same box.  She doesn't eat fish and that is what I got.  I know it's a sushi restaurant but she likes the California rolls.  I got the spicy tuna roll.  It was mediocre.  My daughter did enjoyed hers.  Will not be going back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The restaurant had a strong unpleasant odor, which was difficult to tolerate. To avoid the smell, my daughter and I decided to order takeout. Unfortunately, the server packed both our meals in a single box, resulting in my daughter receiving a dish with fish, which she doesn't eat. Despite it being a sushi restaurant, my daughter specifically prefers California rolls. I ended up with a mediocre spicy tuna roll. Although my daughter enjoyed her meal, this experience has made me decide not to return to this restaurant.

input:
Love the food. Big portions, interesting and ever changing menue. The only issues i have are that the seating is cramped, too loud for conversation and the coffe is not as good as Sabrina's.

The latkas are always perfect and the bacon is the best I ahve had in Philly.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Great food with big portions and an interesting, ever-changing menu. However, cramped seating and excessive noise make conversation difficult. Additionally, the coffee doesn't quite meet the standards set by Sabrina's. Nonetheless, the latkas are consistently perfect, and the bacon is the best in Philly.

input: This is a must get when you come to Reno is Yellow Subs. Ask for the sprouts on your sub and you won't regret it. It is way better then  anywhere I've ever been. The people are totally down to earth and always are nice and Stack your sub with only the best. Only the best and I recommend this to anyone who loves subs and loves food. Oh and there Tank Tops and T-shirts, priceless, I have a tank myself and represent it anywhere I go. Will be going there again in the future. 5 stars because the service was fast, people were nice, food was amazing, seating made you feel closer to your peers with more conversation movement back and forth and a great environment.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Yellow Subs in Reno is a must-visit spot. Their sprouts on the sub are exceptional and superior to any other place I've tried. The staff is friendly and genuine, providing excellent service. You can stack your sub with the finest ingredients. I highly recommend this place to any sub and food enthusiast. They also have Tank Tops and T-shirts, which are a cherished possession. I will definitely be returning in the future. Overall, I give it a 5-star rating for its fast service, amazing food, welcoming atmosphere, and the opportunity for engaging conversations with fellow diners.

input: Tina I believe was our waitress.. I'm not sure if I want to give 3 or 4 stars. Its just that the initial wait was kinda long. But it was my first time eating the food and I thought it was pretty good. I liked my side salad too!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Tina was our waitress. Unsure about giving 3 or 4 stars as the initial wait was long. However, food was good and I enjoyed the side salad.

input: Love!! Our new favorite local spot. We've gone a few times since they opened and it's always a good ambiance, and great food. The drinks are great, the salsa is super yummy, and the salads are very much entree sized. Bring your friends, sit outside, grab a margarita and enjoy!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Love is a fantastic local spot we've been frequenting since they opened. The ambiance is always enjoyable and the food is delicious. The drinks, including their yummy salsa and entree-sized salads, are top-notch. Bring your friends, sit outside, and savor a margarita while having a great time!

input:
Great service, food was ok..  Wish the soups were served warmer, and my steak was cooked well done, when requested medium. 

However the service was excellent.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Service was great. Food was okay, but soups should have been served warmer and the steak was overcooked, requested medium.

input:
Despite it's great reviews by other Yelpers, I was not that blown away by Nippon Tei. 

My roommate and I were craving sushi and were recommended to come here by Yelp and a friend so we decided to give it a shot. 

First off, they get bonus points for serving FREE edemame as an appetizer. I usually pay $4 to $5 for it at other sushi restaurants. The mango sake drink I have was alright, but not worth the price I paid for it. 

On to the main event...SUSHI! We had the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. They were all yummy, but I would have to say I have had better. Actually, out of the hand-full of sushi restaurants I have tried, this was the worst sushi I have tried, but I cannot say the sushi was bad by any means. Don't get me wrong, it was still tasty. 

The other big thing was that the rolls were actually falling apart. I have never had this happen. Therefore, I can say that the presentation and the ability to get the sushi from the plate to my mouth without falling apart did make me unhappy. 

I am willing to come back to Nippon Tei, but I have to say I already have my other favorites. The prices were average compared to other sushi bars, so that won't really help them out either when it comes to bringing me back. We will see!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Despite its positive reviews on Yelp, Nippon Tei did not impress me. My roommate and I decided to try it based on recommendations, but I was underwhelmed. On a positive note, they served complimentary edamame, which is usually an extra cost at other sushi places. However, the mango sake drink I ordered was not worth the price. As for the sushi, we tried the philly roll, tempura roll, tuna roll, and california roll. While they were tasty, I've had better sushi elsewhere. In fact, out of the sushi restaurants I've tried, this was the worst. The rolls were also falling apart, which was disappointing. While I may return to Nippon Tei in the future, I already have my preferred spots. The prices were average, so that won't be a deciding factor either. Only time will tell if I give it another chance.

input: Went to see Star Wars Rogue One yesterday in 3D.  Buying the tickets was a breeze, and the atmosphere was inviting.  Found the comfortable seats with no problem and ordered right away before the movie began.  I ordered pretzel sticks - food was hot, prompt & delicious.  I was excited for the movie to begin.  Once the advertisements were done and the movie started, that's when I noticed something wasn't right.  The entire screen was so dark that I was not able to make out the faces of the actors on the screen.  I kept lifting up the 3D glasses to see if it made a difference - nope.  The two people seated next to me were noticing the same and complaining.  I thought that maybe this is how the movie was filmed?  Then it got worse.  Even with the 3D glasses on, the shadows in the background on the screen were double and there was no discerning most actors' faces at all.  I got up and went to the lobby and asked for the manager.  The gentleman wore a blue shirt, middle age with a beard, said that this was the 3D experience, it was a "closed-system" and there was nothing he could do.  I simply asked him to come with me into the theater to see with his own eyes how dark it was.  He would not and did not.  I suspect this wasn't the first time he's heard this from a customer.  I've seen normal movies at this location before, but this was my first, and last experience with their 3D in room #1.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Yesterday, I went to see Star Wars Rogue One in 3D. Buying tickets was easy and the atmosphere was welcoming. I quickly found comfortable seats and placed an order for pretzel sticks, which arrived promptly and tasted delicious. Once the movie started, I noticed that the entire screen was too dark, making it difficult to see the actors' faces. Even lifting the 3D glasses didn't help. The people sitting next to me were also experiencing the same issue and expressing their dissatisfaction. The shadows in the background were double, further obscuring the actors' faces. Concerned, I approached the manager in the lobby, who explained that it was the intended 3D experience and there was nothing he could do. I asked him to come and see the darkness for himself, but he refused. This disappointing 3D experience was my first and last in room #1 at this location.

input: Overpriced for average food served warm (not hot) by servers who had trouble saying the names of the dishes and seemed in a rush to give us our bill when the place was more than half empty (on a Saturday night). When one of the servers came over to check on the $23 pork chop (which was not listed in the menu - $18 price was), my spouse commented there was a lot of fat....she seemed baffled by his comment, then walked away! The "ropa vieja" dish was good, but overpriced for being served in moderate portion. The menu prices did not reflect the ambiance (random plastic container boxes placed on a nearby table nor the sagging knitted item hanging over our table - it looks like there should've been a lamp in it).
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Overpriced average food served warm by servers who struggled with dish names and hurriedly gave us the bill despite a half-empty restaurant on a Saturday night. The $23 pork chop, not listed on the menu, had excessive fat and the server seemed confused by our comment. The "ropa vieja" dish was decent but overpriced for the portion size. The menu prices did not match the ambiance, with random plastic container boxes and a sagging knitted item hanging over our table, which appeared like it should have had a lamp.

input: Should have listened to other reviews--we were kind of disappointed.  The layout of the restaurant is interesting in that it's made to look sort of like the inside of a chicken coop (made for people).  However, the food was overpriced and underwhelming.  We ate from the Sunday brunch menu--only decent value on the menu is the chicken strips and fries.  My wife ordered the seasonal salad, which was comically small and was way short on the actual lettuce (and not cheap either).  Chicken was good, but nothing better than Raising Canes in my opinion.  Service and food seemed on the slow side, especially with the small crowd.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Should have listened to the reviews, we were disappointed. The restaurant has an interesting layout like a chicken coop, but the food is overpriced and underwhelming. The only decent value on the menu is the chicken strips and fries from the Sunday brunch menu. My wife's seasonal salad was comically small with very little lettuce, and it was expensive. The chicken was okay, but not better than Raising Canes. Service and food were slow, even with a small crowd.

input: Wow. I am not a vegetarian, nor am I a health-food nut (except for my random "diet" binges) but this place is awesome. A co-worker talked me into trying it out one day (by going there and getting me something and putting it in front of me) and she created a monster. I may not order every day but I sure do think about them. And their delicious salads! Every time I go there I am greeted with a smile and there are tons of other people waiting for their food, as well. Good company =)
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I'm not a vegetarian or health-conscious, but this place is amazing. A co-worker introduced me to it and now I can't get enough. Their salads are delicious and the service is always friendly.

input:
Only giving a 1 because there is nothing lower!!! Angie
Gave me the worst haircut I've ever had!!! I came in with 2 photos of the cut I wanted came out with my hair looking NOTHING like the photos!!  Even when pointed out to her she didn't not pay attention to what she was doing.  Came out basically having a mans flattop!  Would never go to this place again!!! Nothing like going into the Holidays with a crappie haircut. Thank you!! Angie and Regis Hair salon!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I am extremely dissatisfied with my experience at Regis Hair salon. I requested a specific haircut, providing two photos for reference, but the stylist, Angie, completely ignored my instructions. I ended up with a haircut that looked nothing like what I wanted, resembling a man's flattop. Despite my attempts to communicate my dissatisfaction, Angie paid no attention to what she was doing. As a result, I am left with a terrible haircut right before the holidays. I will definitely not be returning to this salon. Thank you, Angie.

input: Perfect place for a date night. The sweet potato nachos and the "breakfast" we're to die for! Really everything we tried was delicious...I can't wait to go back again.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Great spot for a date night! The sweet potato nachos and "breakfast" were absolutely amazing. Everything we tried was delicious. Can't wait to return!

input: We had dinner at Convivio right after it opened and we will definitely go back. There were a few minor quirks with the service and with wine being out of stock, but I'm chalking it up to the fact that it just opened and they were working out the kinks. The owner visited our table and he could not have been nicer or more gracious. The food was excellent...nothing to change there! I had the tortelloni pansotti, and i think it was the best pasta I've ever had. I'm sure we will be frequent diners .
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We had dinner at Convivio right after it opened and despite a few minor service quirks and wine being out of stock, we plan to return. The owner visited our table and was incredibly gracious. The food, especially the tortelloni pansotti, was excellent and I believe it was the best pasta I've ever had. We will definitely become regular diners.

input: After driving pass all the seafood restaurants around Clearwater Beach, I knew wanted seafood right there and then. I wasn't familiar with the area and did not do any yelping before hand, so was pretty hesitant to just blindly pick a restaurant.  Finally, after a long day at the beach, we made a quick walk across the street to all the restaurants and thats when we stumbled into Crabby Bill's. We ordered the $25 bucket of steamed seafood. It was decent, not necessarily the best fresh seafood. This was just a quick snack that I shared with one other person to keep us going before our big dinner at Bern's Steak House that we had reservation for a couple hours later.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After passing numerous seafood restaurants around Clearwater Beach, I craved seafood and felt unsure about which restaurant to choose. Eventually, after a tiring day at the beach, we stumbled upon Crabby Bill's, conveniently located across the street from all the restaurants. Opting for the $25 bucket of steamed seafood, we found it to be decent but not the freshest. Nevertheless, it served as a quick snack to sustain us before our planned dinner reservation at Bern's Steak House a few hours later.

input:
Just finished a State Street Kitchen, Grilled Chicken, Spinach, Swiss and Honey Mustard Sub.  To kick it up a notch I stuffed in Jalapeno Chips for a spicy crunch. 
It was great on an afternoon when autumn is starting to assert itself with bluster.  

This excellent local establishment continues to turn out first rate creative dishes thanks to the ever-present Micha, and her friendly staff.  It has become my most constant breakfast companion, and often my lunch date, as well.  

If you have not been in for a taste of home cooking with a Korean flare, you don't know what you are missing. 

Find a way to get there.  Sit down and become part of the family.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Just had a delicious State Street Kitchen grilled chicken, spinach, Swiss and honey mustard sub with a spicy kick from jalapeno chips. The autumn atmosphere added to the enjoyment. The local establishment run by Micha and her friendly staff consistently serves creative and top-notch dishes. It's my go-to for breakfast and lunch. Don't miss out on their Korean-flavored home cooking - make sure to visit and feel like part of the family.

input: awesome place.  good food. nice people.  rotating specials.  all home made.  what else do you want?  Chicken salad is a great pickup to make sandwiches at home.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The place is awesome - great food, nice people, rotating specials, and everything is homemade. Plus, their chicken salad is perfect for making sandwiches at home. What more could you ask for?

input: I'm rating this based on the service and not the food. I am a sales administrator at a hotel. Typically, many places offer a hospitality discount because we do refer guests different places. Front desk told me I should try this place as they give a decent discount. I called to place my order and wasn't really able to say what I liked b/c the girl who answered would cut me off to finish my statement.(she wasn't in the best mood) We get to the end of the order and she asks me am I a guest or an employee. I told her an employee. She asked my title. I told her. She gives me a total and I asked her about the discount. She says it's only for front desk. I'm shocked that this is a departmental thing 1 and 2 I'm thinking to myself, "I'm in sales. I get groups of people here. They ALWAYS asked for recommendations." I said well should I hang up and have front desk place my order? She huffed and puffed and then said "well i'll give it to you this time but please dont abuse it." I was so shocked at how rude she was. So when I finally got my food, I tipped the driver and gave him their menus back and said we will no longer be doing business with you guys. She didnt know SALES is in charge of who the front desk can recommend. Her name was Neisha.The food was good though.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I am a sales administrator at a hotel and recently had a poor experience with a restaurant's service. Upon a referral from the front desk, I called to place an order and experienced interruptions and rudeness from the employee who answered. I mentioned being an employee myself and asked about the hospitality discount, only to be informed that it was exclusive to the front desk. Shocked and disappointed, I considered having the front desk place the order but was reluctantly provided the discount. When my food arrived, I decided to discontinue doing business with the restaurant due to the unprofessional behavior of the employee.

input: Always the sweetest ladies! Appointments never take forever and barely any wait time!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Sweet ladies, quick appointments, minimal wait time.

input: We won't be back. We got the Brussel sprouts and they tasted like pure salt. Our server sent them back and we got another batch and they tasted exactly the same. My husband got the burger and it was okay but the fries that came with it tasted like pure salt also. Maybe the cook working this night was just a little heavy handed on the salt, I don't know. I got the flank steak and it was okay. I wouldn't rave about it or ever get it again. Our cocktails were good and the atmosphere was nice, but we were really disappointed with the food :(
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We were disappointed with our recent dining experience. The Brussels sprouts and fries were both overly salty, despite being replaced once. The burger was okay, but the flank steak didn't impress us either. However, our cocktails were good and the atmosphere was nice. Overall, we won't be returning due to our disappointment with the food.

input: I love going to Phillies games sooo much and this stadium definitely adds to the experience. I was never a big baseball fan until about a couple of years ago, when my bf introduced me to the wonder that is the Phils- instant love. Sure,my first Phils game was the 10, 000 loss but whatever. The places has a open feeling, and never feels clausterphobic. The only time i've felt that I had bad seats was when we sat right under neath the scoreboard, and I had to keep on looking up.  I like how you can wander about and watch the game from the lower levels, and that despite it's a sold out game, it never feels cramped or you're really aching to get around the stadium. They have a lot of great food (lots of variety) and the facilities are always clean- both are numerous, so I'm never waiting in line.  I am missing baseball season and I cannot wait until April! Go Phillies!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love going to Phillies games and this stadium enhances the experience. My passion for baseball started a couple of years ago when my boyfriend introduced me to the team, and I instantly fell in love. Despite my first game being their 10,000th loss, I still enjoyed it. The stadium has an open atmosphere, which never feels crowded. The only time I had less-than-ideal seats was when we were right under the scoreboard, constantly having to look up. I appreciate the ability to wander and watch the game from the lower levels, even during sold-out games when it never feels cramped. There are plenty of great food options with a variety to choose from, and the facilities are always clean and numerous, minimizing wait times. I'm eagerly awaiting the upcoming baseball season in April. Go Phillies!

input: My boyfriend and I decided to stop by for lunch yesterday, and I am so glad we did. I ordered a side of beans, chips and salsa, and guacamole. He ordered two steak tacos and a side of rice. The beans are hands down my favorite I've had from a mexican restaurant.  My only complaint is that, unfortunately you do not get a very big portion. The salsa is so fresh tasting and delicious-very cilantro forward, and the chips were nice, thick and crunchy without being oily at all. Take note though, chips and salsa are not included with your purchase and must be bought separately. Now let me get to the best part-the made to order, chunky guacamole. The hardy chips would definitely withstand this heavy duty guac, but I opted instead for tortillas as my vessel to stuff it with along with my beans and salsa. The hot sauces were anything but, though admittedly my tolerance to spices may be higher than the average persons. While I had a great eating experience, my boyfriend did not. He said the meat was of low quality and quite flavorless. He did say he would give it another shot though!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: My boyfriend and I stopped by for lunch yesterday. I ordered a side of beans, chips and salsa, and guacamole. He got two steak tacos with a side of rice. The beans were my favorite, but the portion size was disappointing. The salsa was fresh and cilantro-forward, and the chips were crunchy without being oily. Note that chips and salsa are sold separately. The chunky guacamole was the best part, and I used tortillas instead of chips to enjoy it with beans and salsa. The hot sauces were not spicy enough for me. While I had a great experience, my boyfriend found the meat flavorless and low quality, but he's willing to try again.

input: I love this place. It's been in La Cumbre Plaza for I don't know how long now. If you are looking for a good sandwich look no further. All of the ingredients taste fresh, and their bread rolls are amazing. They are nice and soft, not with that cut the roof of your mouth crust. Being born and raise in Santa Barbara, actually just down the street, I have been coming here for some years now. I've tried probably over half of their sandwiches and all have been good, so good it's hard to pick a favorite.  In addition, I cannot forget to mention their awesome soda selection, so awesome I cannot hesitate to try something different with every visit. You won't find anything super fancy or exotic, like a roasted duck pastrami sandwich here, but if you're a local or just passing through and feel like having a great sandwich with good fresh ingredients swing by Plaza Deli and grab a bite.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Plaza Deli in La Cumbre Plaza has been a local favorite for years. Their sandwiches are made with fresh ingredients and delicious bread rolls that are soft, not crusty. As someone who grew up in Santa Barbara, I have tried many of their sandwiches and they are all fantastic. They also have a great selection of soda. If you're in the area and craving a tasty sandwich, make sure to stop by Plaza Deli. Don't expect anything fancy or exotic, but their sandwiches are top-notch.

input: I think this Nordstrom's shoe department is better than other locations.  There was a lot of variety and they carry some higher end lines here.  The sales professionals were very good.  A gentleman named Erwin helped me locate two pairs of shoes throughout the Nordstrom's network AND price matched them to Bloomingdale's clearance sale price.  And no charge for shipping and handling.  Nordstrom's has won my loyalty due to the very high level of customer service!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I find Nordstrom's shoe department to be superior to other locations due to the great variety and inclusion of higher-end lines. The sales professionals, particularly Erwin, were extremely helpful in locating two pairs of shoes across Nordstrom's network, and even price matched them to Bloomingdale's clearance sale price. Additionally, there was no charge for shipping and handling. Overall, the exceptional customer service at Nordstrom has earned my loyalty.

input: A small aquarium that is interesting mainly for kids.  They have a shark feeding show and stingrays that you can pet and buy food to feed.  It is not the first place i would go in Tarpon Springa, but it is ok, small children seem to like it.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: A small aquarium in Tarpon Springs offers various attractions for kids, including a shark feeding show and the opportunity to pet stingrays. Although it may not be the top choice for adults, it is enjoyable for young children who seem to find it appealing.

input: Nothing extraordinary, but if you want some simple Chinese takeout, this is the best place around. The food seems less greasy than you sometimes find and the people are super nice.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Best place for simple Chinese takeout - not extraordinary, but the food is less greasy than usual and the staff are super nice.

input: Quaint place with great ambience, food and service. I had the Shrimp Po Boy. It was delicious. The fries and cole slaw were perfect side dishes. This was my first visit. Definitely not my last.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Quaint place with great ambience, food, and service. Loved the Shrimp Po Boy - it was delicious. The fries and cole slaw were perfect side dishes. First visit, but won't be my last.

input: Broussard's was pretty good when I went there a few weeks ago. I had a Groupon that was about to expire so I took my parents out to dinner.  I knew going in that Broussards is a very old skool New Orleans restaurant, and it is very nice when you walk in to see the old tile on the walls in the foyer of the building. The courtyard is beautiful and I just had to turn into a tourist and take a picture in front of the fountain with my mom. We were seated and very promptly greeted by the drink guy.  He brought us our water and told us about the extensive wine list, but they were of course out of the Pinot Grigio that I ordered.  He successfully suggested a Chardonnay for me instead and I was happy. The head waiter came out and explained with great detail the specials for the night, but I went for menu regulars, the maytag blue cheese salad and the pecan crusted drum. I wanted more salad, it was so good, I ate it up so fast. The drum was excellent too. It had this soy butter sauce on it that was so good and topped with crawfish. I was definitely happy with my meal and glad I had the experience. What makes me knock off two stars is that though the foyer's vintage appeal is nice and the courtyard is beautiful, I feel like the dining room needs an upgrade.  The chandeliers on the walls in the main dining room are very reminiscent of the hallways of my grandmother's assisted living home. I think its just one of those places I am glad to say I've been to, but I don't think I will choose to go there again.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Broussard's was a good dining experience with old skool New Orleans ambience. The beautiful courtyard and vintage foyer were impressive. Despite being out of the Pinot Grigio I ordered, the drink guy suggested a satisfying Chardonnay. The head waiter provided detailed specials but I opted for their regular menu, enjoying the maytag blue cheese salad and pecan crusted drum. However, the outdated chandeliers in the dining room detracted from the overall experience. While glad I went, I don't plan to return, resulting in a two-star deduction.

input:
Service is excellent. Atmosphere is great. The raw bar was fantastic. Those were the best Alaskan crab legs I've had. Well worth splurging for them. 

My friends were drawn in by the awesome looking burger they had, and indeed the burgers were all they hoped for. It came with a generous portion of crispy fries. But if you want anything else besides the $17 burgers, expect to spend over $30 for your entree. While the ambience feels and looks casual, it is fine dining.

Unfortunately, the waiter did sell the shrimp and grits with the additional crab as "heaven in his mouth", but that it was not. I've had better shrimp and grits in Atlanta, and there is no reasonable way you should be paying $30 for shrimp and GRITS. Without the crab, it was still over $20.

But everything else was great. Drinks were delicious. Everything came out pretty quickly. Oh, when we mentioned we were visiting from out of town, the waiter was nice enough to give us a complimentary appetizer of the cool pizza to start. It was great but the name is hard to say or remember. And the rabbit and chicken liver pate was super worth since it comes in a huge mason jar.

I recommend sticking to the drinks, appetizers, and burgers and you'll be a pretty happy camper.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Great service, excellent atmosphere, and an outstanding raw bar with fantastic Alaskan crab legs make this restaurant worth splurging for. The burgers are also impressive, served with a generous portion of crispy fries. However, be prepared to spend over $30 for any other entree besides the $17 burgers. The casual ambiance is deceiving, as it is actually considered fine dining. Unfortunately, the shrimp and grits with additional crab, touted by the waiter as "heaven in his mouth," did not live up to expectations and were overpriced at $30. Overall, the drinks are delicious, and the food arrives quickly. Mentioning you're visiting from out of town may even get you a complimentary appetizer, such as the cool pizza. Stick to the drinks, appetizers, and burgers for a satisfying experience.

input: I love Doan's. It's the kind of place you have a "usual" and every time you have it, it's just as good as the last time. They staff is friendly and speedy so if you don't have a long lunch it's a great place to go.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love Doan's because it never disappoints. It's the kind of place where you can have a "usual" and each time you order it, it's consistently delicious. The staff is friendly and efficient, making it a perfect choice if you're in a hurry during lunchtime.

input: This amazing brick oven pizza joint gets better every time I go. The last I time I went I got a Rotolo and a prosciutto pizza. The Rotolo is dough wrapped around mortadella and ricotta cheese and topped with pistachios and oil. It is so good. I order it every time. It's about the size of a bun and cost $5. The pizza was amazing. The prosciutto was incredibly tasty. The dough is divine. The service is always great and the beer selection is good. Definitely one of the best pizza places in Philly.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This brick oven pizza joint in Philly continuously improves with each visit. During my last trip, I ordered a Rotolo, which consists of dough wrapped around mortadella and ricotta cheese, topped with pistachios and oil - an irresistible choice that I consistently order at the cost of $5. Additionally, the prosciutto pizza was incredibly delicious - the divine dough paired perfectly with the exceptional taste. The restaurant offers excellent service and a good selection of beers. Without a doubt, it is one of the top pizza places in Philadelphia.

input:
Amazing pizza. AMAZING! After my first bite, I felt like that Oprah Winfrey meme, where her head is thrown back, her mouth is agape and her arms are open wide, and she's screaming, "You get a car!" Except it's not Oprah, it's me. And I don't get a car -- I get a pizza. But I felt that excited.  

This is basically the pizza I have been looking for since moving to the Indianapolis area. It's a whole lot of nothing: It's not cut into square pieces. It's not crispy and thin. It's not redolent of oregano. It's thick and chewy, cheesy, greasy, wonderful -- it tastes the way pizza is supposed to taste! I have found my new pizza home.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This pizza is absolutely amazing. From the first bite, it reminded me of that Oprah Winfrey meme where she's ecstatically shouting, "You get a car!" But instead, it was me feeling that same excitement over a pizza. It's the pizza I've been searching for since moving to Indianapolis. Unlike the typical square pieces or crispy and thin crust, this one is thick, chewy, cheesy, and delightfully greasy. It simply tastes exactly how pizza should taste. I've finally found my new pizza haven.

input: Waited 27 minutes for three teas (no one else was in the store when we came in and ordered). NO tea is worth that long of a wait, especially in Chinatown.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Waited 27 minutes for three teas with no other customers in the store when we placed our order. No tea is worth such a long wait, especially in Chinatown.

input:
I grew up eating beef sandwiches in Chicago, and this place makes the best beef I've ever had outside of the city. 

Couple of suggestions: Offer a third sandwich size option (bigger!), get sweet peppers, serve fries(!!!), keep the main location off of Mass Ave open year-round, and have longer hours!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Chicago native, impressed by the delectable beef sandwiches here. Suggested improvements: introduce larger sandwich option, add sweet peppers, serve fries, maintain year-round operation at main location off Mass Ave, and extend business hours.

input:
We came here for an early mothers day celebration as we were on the quest to find a nail salon that could accommodate 4 pedicures at the same time. They were very friendly and even though they didn't have 4 pedicurists on the schedule that day they added one to accommodate us. That was really nice of them as they could have easily told us no. 

The place itself is decorated very modern and offers a very clean, minimalist atmosphere. Upon walking in we were immediately greeted and after we checked in with the front desk we were asked what we wanted to drink. They had complimentary mimosas, wine and champagne, the perfect way to begin to unwind. Once we picked out our polish colors we were well on our way to getting our pedicures. Everyone was so nice and made us feel comfortable and welcomed. My polish never chipped the whole time I had it on. I will definitely be back. 

The only downside is that its street parking only, which isn't something that they can control. They told us most of their business comes from people who work in the CBD so parking probably isn't an issue for their regular customers. Aside from parking being an issue I would definitely go to Buff again.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We came here for an early Mother's Day celebration, searching for a nail salon that could accommodate 4 pedicures simultaneously. Despite not having enough pedicurists scheduled, they kindly added one for us. The place has a modern and minimalist decoration, creating a clean atmosphere. Upon arrival, we were warmly greeted and offered complimentary mimosas, wine, and champagne. After selecting our polish colors, we received excellent pedicures from friendly staff. My polish did not chip throughout the entire time. The only downside is the street parking, but it is not within their control. Overall, I would definitely return to Buff.

input: Great spot for pho! Broth is very good. I ordered No. 51 (small) and it was filling. Would definitely come back again when I'm in Philly.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Excellent pho spot! Delicious broth. Tried the No. 51 (small) and it was satisfying. Will definitely return when in Philly.

input:
I love the concept of this place. One half of it a café that serves different types of coffees and teas, and breakfast type items, and the other world where it serves bar type apps, salads, and sandwiches,  Can't forget that they also serve a wide variety of beers that they serve on tap, bottled, or in can.  

This place is pretty darn casual, and one can hang out here for hours with their friends.  Reminds me of the good ol' college days when no time could pass especially on a chill out Sunday Fun day.

Bring your four legged friend too.  They are totally welcome.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love this place! It's a concept that combines a café serving different types of coffees, teas, and breakfast items, with a bar serving appetizers, salads, and sandwiches. They also have a wide variety of beers available on tap, bottled, or in cans. The atmosphere is casual and perfect for hanging out with friends for hours, reminiscent of the carefree college days. Plus, they're pet-friendly so you can bring your four-legged friend along too!

input: My husband reserved a Corolla-sized car over the internet ten days ahead of time. When we arrived at Avis Rent A Car at the Reno airport I asked if the rental could be upgraded to a Camry-size vehicle. They offered us two different kinds of cars and finally we got the Camry we wanted. The man was very professional and in the end told us the rental would be $800.00 for five days. I felt the price was very high, however we had gone through most of the paperwork. I had already selected to get the $25.00 a day insurance which came to $150.00 with tax. We were very happy with the car and had no problems with it. During our vacation I decided to talk to an Avis representative when we dropped the car off. I asked her if a weekly rate would be less expensive. She said it would be $15.00 more. She said the upgrade cost an extra $20.00 a day. I will not rent from Avis any more. Next time I will go to Hertz or Dollar and make the reservation over the phone. Looking back, i would not have gotten the extra insurance. My personal insurance covers everything.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: My husband reserved a Corolla-sized car online for our trip to Reno. When we arrived at Avis Rent A Car, I asked to upgrade to a Camry. After considering two options, we received the desired Camry. The total rental cost was $800.00 for five days. Despite finding the price high, we proceeded with the process. I had already opted for the $25.00 per day insurance, totaling $150.00 with tax. The car performed well during our vacation. Upon returning the car, I inquired about a weekly rate, but it was $15.00 more. Additionally, the upgrade costed an extra $20.00 per day. Based on this experience, I have decided not to rent from Avis again, preferring Hertz or Dollar with phone reservations. In hindsight, I realize the extra insurance was unnecessary as my personal insurance provides adequate coverage.

input: Great customer service! Love my new car! Highly recommend to anyone who's trying to buy a new used car in good shape! Talk to Andy if you want some good help!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Highly recommended for great customer service and purchasing a new used car in good condition. Andy provides excellent help and assistance. Love my new car!

input: After moving to the area, Jungle Prada Tavern was one of the first places a friend took me.  The bartender made a great recommendation based on a beer I told her I liked and I loved it!  Now for the food- I LOVE seafood, so I am leary of ordering from places that don't do it justice, but alas, they impressed me thoroughly with all the seafood options I chose!!  The scallops prosciutto app, del mar pizza with crab and scallops, and crab stuffed portabella app (comes with a crab and lobster bisque- YUM) are all delicious!!  I also love the roasted portabella app- for a vegetarian option, it is delicious and was recomended by someone who isn't. I've actually gone back several times since then just to eat (obviously, I also drank ;) and took my sister when she was in town visiting (and is a seafood fanatic).  So all in all, give this place a chance!!  You will not be disappointed with the options!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After my move to the area, a friend introduced me to Jungle Prada Tavern. The bartender there impressed me by offering a great beer recommendation based on my preferences. The seafood options at the tavern surprised and pleased me, as I typically hesitate to order seafood from places that don't do it justice. However, Jungle Prada Tavern exceeded my expectations with their delicious scallops prosciutto app, del mar pizza with crab and scallops, and crab stuffed portabella app, accompanied by a mouthwatering crab and lobster bisque. Their roasted portabella app, although a vegetarian option, was also delectable and came highly recommended. I have returned to the tavern multiple times since then, mainly for the scrumptious food but also for the drinks. I even brought my sister, a seafood fanatic, when she visited town. Overall, I highly recommend giving Jungle Prada Tavern a chance, as their menu will not disappoint in terms of options and taste.

input: This is one of my favorite bead stores in Nashville, walls and walls of seed beads and glass strands!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This is a top bead store in Nashville, featuring an extensive selection of seed beads and glass strands.

input: Went here for dinner on opening day and was SO HAPPY I DID!! Great atmosphere, lovely staff, and food on fleek!! Green tea (PHO PHREE) was so satisfying, summer rolls and spicy peanut sauce were DELISH, and pho was PHONOMENAL! Definitely making this one of my regular hot spotz as I eat my way through Fairmount!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Had an amazing experience at this new restaurant on opening day! The atmosphere is great, staff is lovely, and the food is absolutely delicious. The Green tea (PHO PHREE) was satisfying, while the summer rolls with spicy peanut sauce were mouthwatering. The pho was absolutely phenomenal. This will definitely become one of my go-to places as I explore Fairmount through its food scene.

input:
Don't let the outside fool ya or even the initial impression when you walk in because they food here is really good! When ya walk in this place it's like stepping back into the 1950's.  It's kinda awesome.  Definitely a small-town, homey feel that serves good ole family cookin'.  They had a iceskates up on the wall and a Christmas tree in the corner.  How precious.   
Don't come here expecting the best food in the whole wide world.  It is great for grandma's greasy cooking.  I've only eaten breakfast here but it's been amazing everytime.  I got pancakes and they are so fluffy and light and awesome (esp if you add a little butter).  The bacon was nice, thick, large slices; slightly overcooked maybe but super good cuz I love bacon! :)
The prices are reasonable and the service is great.  This is a great place for a quick delicious home cooked breakfast!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Despite its unassuming exterior and initial impression, the food at this place is really good. Stepping inside feels like going back to the 1950s, giving off a small-town, homey vibe. The place is adorned with ice skates on the wall and a Christmas tree in the corner, which adds to its charm. While it may not offer the best food in the world, it is excellent for grandma's greasy cooking. The breakfast options, particularly the pancakes, are consistently amazing, with fluffy and light texture. The bacon, although slightly overcooked, is still enjoyable for bacon lovers. The prices are reasonable and the service is great. For a quick, delicious, home-cooked breakfast, this is a fantastic choice.

input: Tried this place out after many suggestions from friends.  We went in one night about an hour or so before closing just to find that they were only serving a partial menu - we're not talking that late, it was like, 9:30 on a weekend.  There was no mention of going down to a bar menu on the website so I was a bit annoyed by that.  Something about 'surprise disappointments that could be totally avoided' really bother me.  So, the dish I had picked out online wasn't available and I ordered a burger instead.  The server seemed to have a very hard time understanding my burger and suggested that modifications couldn't be made?  I told him I'm sure removing a single topping wouldn't cause the kitchen staff any issues...  The rest of the meal we were generally ignored and the service wasn't great.  I found the food to be overpriced for the quality.  Unless there is a special reason to attend, I don't think we'll be going back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After multiple recommendations from friends, we tried this place one night about an hour before closing. However, to our disappointment, they were only serving a partial menu. It was not that late, around 9:30 on a weekend, and the website did not mention any change in menu. This unexpected occurrence bothered me as it could have been easily avoided. Consequently, the dish I had selected online was unavailable, and I ended up ordering a burger instead. The server had difficulty understanding my request for modifications and initially claimed it couldn't be done. I insisted that a simple topping removal wouldn't cause any issues for the kitchen staff. Throughout the rest of the meal, we felt generally ignored and the service was subpar. Furthermore, considering the quality, we found the food to be overpriced. Unless there is a compelling reason to return, I doubt we'll be going back.

input:
Second visit even better than the first!!  Loved the butternut squash and goat cheese Rangoons, and the delightfully filling mushroom yakisoba. Amazing flavor, and a smoky , meaty feel though it is meatless. Then came the coconut curry ramen. Heaven in a bowl. 
My only complaint is when you have to wait for seating there is no way to hang by the bar without constantly feeling you are in The servers' way as they breeze by with deliciousness in bowls and plates. So worth the wait before heading to the theater. Plus, food comes out very quickly so we made the curtain, just barely, but with really happy tummies.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Second visit even better than the first!! Loved the butternut squash and goat cheese Rangoons, mushroom yakisoba with amazing flavor and a smoky, meaty feel despite being meatless. Coconut curry ramen was heaven in a bowl. Only complaint is the lack of seating near the bar, constantly feeling in the servers' way. Worth the wait before heading to the theater, as food comes out quickly and we made the curtain with happy tummies.

input: I cannot comment on the food as I had only a couple beers. I did have the white IPA and a red ale which were good but not blow me away. I might be spoiled having 2 friends who brew professionally but the beers were good, not outstanding. The location is kind of far from other stuff which normally wouldn't bother me but everything around is seriously industrial and scenery does make a better place. They do discount the beer $1 when a train comes by and maybe that's the best they can make of a meh location. Probably give it more like a 3.5 stars. It does say something that there was a loyal following at 4pm on a Sunday.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I cannot comment on the food as I only had a couple of beers. The white IPA and red ale were good, but not exceptional. I may be biased since I have friends who brew professionally. The location is far and surrounded by industrial scenery, which detracts from the overall experience. They do offer a $1 discount when a train passes by, perhaps to compensate for the lackluster location. I would rate it around 3.5 stars. However, it is worth noting that there was a loyal following at 4pm on a Sunday.

input:
I first found out about this adorable little salon here on yelp while looking for a place to get a manicure downtown/ CBD.  I visited on 3/8/13 and got their "Mini Manicure"- it's only $15!  I chose an OPI polish and the nail technician did a GREAT job!  So great in fact, that today on Monday, 3/18/13- I did not have ONE CHIP!  This is amazing for polish!  My nails looked fabulous!  The technician was friendly, as were the other stylists.  I'm not sure if it was the manager or the owner that was working the front desk- but she came over as well and was super friendly and welcoming.  The salon looks amazing, trendy, and peaceful.  It has a great vibe.

I was so happy with my first appointment- that I went back today, and left disappointed.  I went to the same nail techinician- and we talked as she worked on my nails.  The person working the front desk (seemed like an owner/ manager- although different from my first visit) was SO  nice, welcoming, and talkative.  This time though I needed a gel manicure, in french- as I am in a wedding this weekend.  I explained that I was in the wedding, assuming the technician would know that this more special than just an everyday manicure  The technician stated after she started my nails, that she did not have the proper brush that she needed in order to do the manicure.  So like most places- they paint the white, and then go back later with a brush to create the crisp, perfect line.  Since she did not have the brush to do that- she used a q- tip.  So obviously the lines are not perfect or even.  Along with the lines being uneven- some are thicker than others, and the edges go up, instead of down.  My nails are not at all filed and shaped pretty either.  For $40 (+ a tip)- I really expect them to look right.  I went during my lunch hour, and it was supposed to be 30 minute appointment, but the appointment took a little bit over an hour.  I understand that french takes a little extra time- but this seemed like quite a bit extra.  I was late for work, and had to hurry out of there when she was finished and did not want to be even more late to work to stay there to make a complaint.  I wish I would have- but I also felt bad because the technician was trying so hard- but they are just not up to par.

I'm conflicted, but I don't know that I'll return.  I loved it to so much the first time, I even sent friends over there.  But after this time- I am not happy with the product.  I wish it wasn't gel- because I can't even take the polish off myself.  So I'm forced to have nails that I am unhappy with, or go to somewhere else and pay to have this taken off, and then pay to have them re done- all before a 6am flight on Wednesday morning, and it's Monday afternoon....
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
I discovered this salon on Yelp while searching for a manicure place downtown. I visited on 3/8/13 and got their affordable "Mini Manicure" for $15. The nail technician did an excellent job using an OPI polish. Surprisingly, the polish lasted without a single chip until Monday, 3/18/13. The nails looked fabulous and the technician and other stylists were friendly. The salon had a trendy and peaceful vibe.

However, my second visit left me disappointed. I requested a gel French manicure for a wedding, assuming the technician would understand the importance. Unfortunately, she didn't have the necessary brush and used a q-tip instead, resulting in uneven and thick lines that went up instead of down. The nails were also not filed or shaped nicely. The appointment, which was supposed to be 30 minutes, took over an hour, making me late for work. I didn't have time to complain and left feeling unsatisfied. I wish I had made a complaint, but I felt guilty because the technician was trying her best despite the subpar outcome.

I'm conflicted, but I'm unsure if I'll return. Though I loved my first visit and even recommended the salon to friends, this experience left me unhappy. Since it's a gel manicure, I can't easily remove the polish myself. I'm now stuck with nails I'm not satisfied with, and I have limited time before an early flight on Wednesday to find another salon to fix them.

input:
A bit off the beaten path for most tourists, as it is in the Marigny, but worth the trip. Sure, the place is not perfect, but there are ultra-expensive restaurants in the FQ that are also not perfect. Look, cheap food, especially food this good, gives "wiggle" room for imperfections.

Breakfast served all day is a bonus. Sometimes you just got to have a lox omelet (under $10) late in the day. The restaurant boasts vegetarian and *gasp* vegan dishes, but someone needs to tell them that cheese doesn't fit into either of those categories. That aside, the french fry poboy, and the mac 'n cheese sandwiches are amazing. So is the Saturday Blue Plate of BBQ Chicken legs. 

Every entree is under $10, well except for the Friday Blue Plate, but why quibble? And who can argue with $5 Bloody Mary's, especially ones that are this good?
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Located in the Marigny, this restaurant may not be as popular with tourists, but it is definitely worth the visit. While it may not be flawless, even high-end restaurants in the French Quarter have their imperfections. The affordable prices allow for some room for minor flaws, considering the quality of the food. One of the highlights is that they serve breakfast all day, perfect for those craving a lox omelet for a late-day meal at just under $10. The restaurant offers vegetarian and vegan options, although it should be noted that cheese is not included in either category. Despite this, their french fry poboy, mac 'n cheese sandwiches, and Saturday Blue Plate BBQ Chicken legs are all fantastic. The best part is that every entree is under $10, with the exception of the Friday Blue Plate. Additionally, they offer delicious $5 Bloody Mary's that are hard to argue with.

input: Awesome sangria.  Rotating craft beers. Pizza and calzones keep me coming back
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Delicious sangria and rotating craft beers, alongside irresistible pizza and calzones, are the reasons I keep coming back.

input: First off, it is a bar through and through. The alcohol selection is good and the drinks well mixed. It is also a casino bar, so you'll be paying higher than average prices. There is a small food menu, but the selection isn't that great. To add insult to injury the food made me ill. The reviews about service aren't exaggerations. We, too, practically had to tackle our server to order food and drinks many of times. Not my preferred place to go when there are so many better options in Reno.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This bar is primarily known for its drinks and casino atmosphere, but the prices are higher than average. The food menu is limited and disappointing, and the quality made me sick. The service has also been consistently poor, with difficulty in ordering both food and drinks. Overall, there are much better options available in Reno, making it not my preferred choice.

input: Rude and unprofessional staff. I called today to find out if they had availability over the Thanksgiving holiday and the staff was short and basically said no then hung up the phone. I will take my business elsewhere.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The staff I spoke to today regarding Thanksgiving holiday availability was rude, unprofessional, and abruptly ended the call without providing any further assistance. As a result, I have decided to take my business elsewhere.

input: Went there due to having a gc, and was suprised at the great food!  Had the sauteed stirfry over spinach, and my gf had the abundant pile of nachos.  They have a pretty decent selection of other delectables, and the day time bartender was very pleasant.
