It's not a hot breakfast (I've had so many mass-produced bad ones, so I'm not complaining) but greek yogurt, a huge croissant, an orange and some cranberry juice hits the spot! They leave it at your door though, instead of ringing your bell to wake you. So if you ask for it to be delivered at 7 a.m., check outside your door; by 7:01 it WILL be there. 

Coffee, a variety of teas, cold and hot water, as well as ice and a bowl of assorted fruit are available 24/7 in the lobby. There are doorbells for each room, and the hotel can only be accessed after hours if you have a key card. Floors are acessible with a keycard as well, for extra protection. The staff is very polite: one of the few places in Philly where someone will actually say "good morning" to you (No, seriously. I lived there for 5 years, so trust me on that). They're also extremely helpful. When I checked in the night before, the gentleman at the reservation desk called to make sure I had a cab waiting for me at 8:15 the next morning so that I could make my speaking engagement on time. While I was getting my clothes ready, my iron was making more wrinkles than it was taking out, so I asked them for a new one and within 30 seconds, I had a brand new model with all the bells and whistles.

I've read a few reviews talking about the noise level of this place. My room was closest to the reception desk and I never heard a peep. There were people out and about, but I didn't hear a thing. And I'm a very light sleeper...

A few things to note:
Its location on a tight, one way street can cause a little difficulty if you're traveling solo, but if you have one person to unload the car while someone else parks, you should be fine. The parking garage they use is about half a block from the hotel, but you have to drive in a big rectangle to get there. 

There's a stand-up shower instead of the traditional bathtub/shower combo. It fits one comfortably enough... provided that you're not too far from average height and build. (My boyfriend is 6'2 with a football player build and he made out okay.)

Don't expect much of a view. The view from our room was of the side of another building. But that's what the city is for... go out there and see something!

Overall, this was an excellent trip and a great find. I highly recommend this hotel to anyone.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This hotel in the heart of Philadelphia is a cozy gem. The rooms are spacious, modern, and beautifully decorated, resembling a friend's apartment rather than a hotel. They offer a free breakfast with items like greek yogurt, croissant, orange, and cranberry juice delivered to your door at the specified time. The lobby provides 24/7 access to coffee, tea, water, ice, and fruit. The staff is polite, helpful, and ensures that guests have a smooth stay. Despite some reviews mentioning noise levels, the room I stayed in was peaceful. Note that the hotel's location on a one-way street may be challenging for solo travelers, but parking is available nearby. The bathroom has a stand-up shower, and the view from the room may not be impressive, but the city offers plenty to explore. Overall, this hotel was an excellent find, and I highly recommend it to anyone visiting Philadelphia.

input:
Was taken here today by a Colombian friend who needed to satisfy a craving for something cheap and delicious. This place reminds me of Nanzhou, a Yelp favorite, because of the heaping helpings you get for next to nothing. 

I got the oxtail soup (Sancocho) with extra rice and plantains to see how it would differ from the Korean-style stuff I was used to at home. Aside from a thicker, stew-like broth and beefier potatoes, it was just as delicious. My friend got a flat steak (Carne Asada) that I think he ate in just under 10 seconds. 

Remember Yelp, you're missing out on a lot if you don't visit NE philly once in a while, especially this place.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
Today, a Colombian friend brought me to this place to satisfy their craving for something cheap and delicious. It reminds me of Nanzhou, a popular spot on Yelp, because of the generous portions you get for a low price. 

I ordered the oxtail soup (Sancocho) with extra rice and plantains to compare it to the Korean-style soup I usually have. Apart from a thicker, stew-like broth and heartier potatoes, it was equally delicious. In under 10 seconds, my friend devoured a flat steak (Carne Asada). 

Don't forget, if you don't visit NE Philly occasionally, especially this place, you're missing out on a lot according to Yelp.

input: My friends and I all got one of each that were available to try out. I love the many fun donut flavors they have there. The thing that stood out to me was their fried chicken. I got the chicken sandwich and it was SO GOOD. I highly recommend it.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: My friends and I tried all the available flavors of donuts. They offer a wide variety of fun flavors, which I really enjoyed. However, what impressed me the most was their fried chicken. I tried their chicken sandwich and it was incredibly delicious. I highly recommend it.

input: Pricey ( a ham and cheese croissant was $5.50)  as with anywhere in Santa Barbra but very delicious. Cute space ( a bit hard to find ). The green eggs and ham  breakfast biscuit is to die for.  ($10 I think) The Santa Barbra tri tip sandwich was excellent! Cold brew coffee was good. Lots of good choices in the grab and go section, and our salami and pesto sammy was also great. I'd go back!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The prices are high in Santa Barbara, including a ham and cheese croissant for $5.50, but the food is delicious. The space is cute but a little hard to find. The green eggs and ham breakfast biscuit is amazing, priced at around $10. The Santa Barbara tri tip sandwich is excellent. The cold brew coffee is good too. There are many good choices in the grab and go section, and the salami and pesto sandwich is also great. Overall, I would definitely go back.

input: The food is delicious but the service has always been pretty slow if not bad which would be understandable if it was busy it's just usually it's not .
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food is delicious, but the service is consistently slow or unfavorable, which is surprising since it's usually not busy.

input:
One of my most favorite Indian restaurants. Nothing fancy but absolutely delicious meals.

Never an issue being seated promptly. A casual dining experience awaits. Service is pleasant. Ambience a bit blahh but still enjoyable.

Now onto the real reason to come here... the FOOD:
Naan is soft. Garlic is tasty but I usually like the original best.  Regardless of your entree of choice, you really cannot go wrong. And although it does not appeal to my level of spiciness preferred (I like it HOT HOT HOT), it has great flavor and is great for the average spicey food eater. My recommendations are the Masala or Vindaloo (Chicken, Shrimp, Lamb... option is yours). Room for dessert? Order the Rice Pudding  and Gulab Jaman, mix together and enjoy the creamy sugary treat.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This Indian restaurant is one of my favorites. The meals are absolutely delicious and the service is prompt. It offers a casual dining experience with a pleasant atmosphere. The naan is soft and the garlic flavor is tasty, though I prefer the original. Regardless of your entree choice, you can't go wrong as everything has great flavor. While it may not be very spicy, it is still enjoyable for those who prefer milder spice levels. I highly recommend the Masala or Vindaloo options (Chicken, Shrimp, or Lamb). For dessert, try the Rice Pudding and Gulab Jaman mixed together for a creamy and sugary treat.

input:
I can say this is the best burger of my life!

You sit outside and Goleta holester Ave is nothing special.   But the burger is the best
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The burger is the best I have ever had, even though the atmosphere at Goleta Holester Ave is nothing special.

input:
To the other reviewers 
You are reviewing the god damn stadium, not that your a Philly fan, and OMG your team won the world series in 08. 

-The food sucks, they do not have enough vendors, So if your enjoying the game, you pretty much have to get up to buy yourself a pretzel or soda. 
-Point out the worst food, the "Hoagies" or whatever are Terrible. Aren't they suppose to be like really good (Believe I'm in Philly). The french fries are mad greasy and no crunch or anything. They were soggy, greasy fries!!!! 
- They have cheap small TVs, that are blurry as hell, so there goes the idea of watching the game while your on line waiting for your food. 
- I would love to understand how the game has just started (3rd inning), and I find empty beer containers everywhere.. 

This is not part of my judgement, but for other people to be aware and be careful 
Philly fans are the RUDEST and NASTIEST people. They are very drunk people, they get in your face, they will spill things on you. Even if your a girl, they have no respect. 

This stadium SUCKS, visit it, knock it off your list, see cheap home runs, since the stadium is built for hitters... 
but we advised...Bring your own food and beware of Philly fans. 
PS: There still are nasty even if you aren't a mets fan...they are just rude people.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
To the reviewers, 
Focus on the stadium, not your team allegiances or past victories. 

- The food options are lacking, with limited vendors requiring fans to leave their seats to purchase refreshments. 
- The "Hoagies" or sandwiches are particularly disappointing, not living up to their reputation. The french fries are overly greasy and lack crunch. 
- The small, blurry TVs make it difficult to watch the game while waiting in line for food. 
- Empty beer containers can be found scattered throughout the stadium, even in the early innings. 

Note: Philly fans can be extremely rude and disrespectful, often intoxicated and prone to spilling things or getting in your face, regardless of your gender or team affiliation. 

This stadium is not recommended. Expect cheap home runs due to its hitter-friendly design, but bring your own food and be wary of Philly fans who can be unpleasant.

input: I cannot say enough how much I loved this place!! It has a great old school diner vibe. The workers there were so so nice. I had never had gumbo and they make it to order but they made us 2 little tasters, and I usually don't even like shrimp but I ate every last bite!!! We also had the grits, fried chicken and the split pea soup was the best freaking split pea soup I have ever had in my life and I am not kidding. And the prices are insanely affordable, between the 2 of us we ordered a lot of food and beers for only $25. Great deal!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I absolutely loved this place! It has a fantastic old school diner vibe, and the workers were incredibly nice. Even though I had never tried gumbo before, they made us two little tasters upon request, and I was pleasantly surprised to find that I loved it, despite not usually liking shrimp. We also tried the grits, fried chicken, and let me tell you, the split pea soup was the best I've ever had. I am not kidding. Additionally, the prices are unbelievably affordable. Between the two of us, we ordered a lot of food and beers for only $25. What a great deal!

input:
If you want stunning and unique pieces of jewelry, this is the place for it! The two marvelous owners, Ali and Albisia, are such sweet people. They create amazing jewelry that you really will have a hard time choosing from! I have a necklace, two bracelets, and a ring and am already hankering for more... There's also great music to add to the decor and general ambience of the store... and you get offered wine as you peruse! What can be better than that? 

Hope to visit Tampa again soon and see you guys soon!! :)
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place offers stunning and unique jewelry created by the marvelous owners, Ali and Albisia. They have a wide selection that will make it difficult to choose. The store also has great music and a welcoming atmosphere. To top it off, they offer wine while you browse. Can't wait to visit Tampa and see you guys again soon!

input: Good menu, solid ingredients, but these folks are not sandwich artists.  I had a Turkey and Brie Wrap one day and the Spinach Florentine Wrap the next.  Both "wraps" could have more fittingly been called "crumples" because that's how they were assembled.  While watching the sandwich line I kept thinking, "Thank god they're not trying to fold burritos!"  Everyone in the sandwich line either looked befuddled by anything other than a plain bagel or like they were supposed to be somewhere else ten minutes ago.  Also, can we please hang a few signs like "order here", "pick-up here," "pay-here" to direct traffic instead of the east coast "If you don already know, then leave!" attitude?
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The menu is good and the ingredients are solid, but the staff lacks expertise in sandwich making. The Turkey and Brie Wrap and the Spinach Florentine Wrap were poorly assembled, resembling more of a crumpled mess than a wrap. Observing the sandwich line, it was evident that the staff struggled with anything beyond a basic bagel and seemed either confused or in a rush. Additionally, it would be helpful to have clear signs directing customers where to order, pick up, and pay, instead of adopting an unfriendly attitude towards those who are unfamiliar with the process.

input:
This place is absolutely amazing. A cute little bakery and the employees are super attentive. I walked in and was bouncing around from one dessert to another deciding if I should make a purchase. The employee offered me a sample of the banana puddings - definitely try some! And you know how sometimes when they give you so small of a sample to taste, you can't really make a proper judgment because there isn't enough to judge from? Not the case here!

I got the salted caramel banana, the strawberry banana pudding and the upside pineapple cake.

Thoughts: OMG!! I never crave banana pudding and never really thought anything of the dessert. But man after this, I wanted to go home and make my own banana pudding (Although I highly doubt that I could make it half as good)! Their desserts are crafted perfect - three/four layers depending on what you get. The bottom layer the the pudding, second layer is the nilla wafers or they might even use some sort of pound cake(whatever it was - it was AMAZING), third layer, the strawberry and then the top layer is pudding with a nice whipped creme and topping. The creme has so much flavor and the texture is so smooth. Everything just comes together so nicely! 

The upside pineapple cake was BOMB. the cake wasn't too fluffy but was dense to the perfect amount to Taste like what it's suppose to. The pineapple flavor isn't overwhelming but just right. My only problem was that the pineapple bottom got a little too carameliZed with brown sugar and was a bit hard to chew.

Definitely go to this place! I was so sad that there was no option to leave them a tip. (They use an iPad to ring you up). The service/help was so great and I would have left a tip but I had no cash. Any ways, highly recommend this place for desserts!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is amazing! It's a cute little bakery with super attentive employees. They offer samples of their delicious banana puddings - definitely try them! Their desserts are crafted perfectly with layers of pudding, nilla wafers or pound cake, strawberry, and whipped cream on top. The flavors are amazing and everything comes together nicely. The upside pineapple cake is also great, with the perfect density and pineapple flavor. The only issue was that the caramelized pineapple bottom was a bit hard to chew. Overall, I highly recommend this place for desserts.

input: I visited the new Paoli location. BIG selection of tasty donuts. It's about time--the cardboard impostors found at Dunkin are so lame compared to these beauties. Salted Caramel, Bacon Maple, Lemon--now you're talking my language. Breakfast sandwiches, muffins, and bagels, oh my.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I visited the new Paoli location which offers a wide variety of delicious and flavorful donuts. Unlike the disappointing options at Dunkin, these donuts are superior in taste and quality. They have an impressive selection including Salted Caramel, Bacon Maple, and Lemon, which I absolutely loved. Additionally, they also serve breakfast sandwiches, muffins, and bagels.

input: So our most recent visit earlier this month was very disappointing, however we received an email from the company's guest service, followed by a call from the Hermitage O'Charley's manager Chris who was very professional and apologetic about our experience and asked that we give his location another try on them. So I convinced my husband to do so. Here's how this 2nd chance went:: Absolutely wonderful. Chris asked that we let him know when we wanted to give the restaurant a second chance, but we decided not to. We didn't want any special attention. We wanted real unreviewed service.  We were seated in the bar because it was a very  busy night, regardless of that the server was very attentive and had a great personality. Our food came out in a timely manner, well prepared and delicious. We have since then been back several times and service continues to remain great.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After a disappointing visit earlier this month, we received an email and call from the company's guest service, followed by an apologetic call from manager Chris at Hermitage O'Charley's. He asked us to give his location another try on the house. We decided not to ask for any special attention and were seated in the bar on a busy night. Despite this, the server was attentive and had a great personality. Our food arrived promptly, well prepared and delicious. We have since returned multiple times and the service remains consistently excellent.

input: In love with my haircut! Very reasonable prices as well. This is my second time here. The first time the cut and style were amazing but the color was a little off from what I wanted but it still looked good. I will definitely continue to be a returning customer.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Love my haircut! Reasonable prices, second time here. First time, amazing cut and style, color slightly off but still looked good. Will definitely be a returning customer.

input: So much care is given to healthy, delicious food (ex. Japanese squash rather than white potatoes in curry). Thay have nice touches like a welcome snack and straw wrappers twisted in a rose. The sauces are amazing, menu has so many options, they accomodate special dietary needs easily since everything is made from scratch; even the desserts have that extra touch using both white and black sticky rice. This is our go-to for Thai from now on!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place offers a lot of care for healthy and tasty food. They use Japanese squash instead of white potatoes in their curry. They also have nice touches like a welcome snack and straw wrappers twisted in a rose. The sauces are amazing, and the menu offers a wide variety of options. They easily accommodate special dietary needs since everything is made from scratch. Even the desserts are exceptional, using both white and black sticky rice. From now on, this will be our go-to place for Thai food.

input:
Great grocery store in the Mid-city neighborhood. It had great deli, soup, hot bar, and salad bar options. It was like a waaaay less expensive Whole Foods. On the weekends they had crawfish or lobster boils by the lbs. This would be my go to store if I lived here for sure. Big plus it's LOCAL!!!

* Fried Chicken was BOMBlicious!!!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Amazing grocery store in Mid-city neighborhood with excellent deli, soup, hot bar, and salad bar offerings. Comparable to a more affordable version of Whole Foods. They host weekend crawfish or lobster boils by the pound, making it a top choice for residents. Additionally, it's a local establishment. Not to mention, their fried chicken is absolutely delicious.

input: I made my Yelp account for the soul purpose of reviewing this place; I think that very much speaks to how I enjoyed the experience. It's exactly what you would expect from a local cafe/coffee shop and then some. The food and coffee were great and the atmosphere was very friendly and casual. The architecture of the dining room was very cool as well - it had a very Victorian feel, which I personally love. The service was a bit slow, but the barista was the only person working behind the counter and she was also very personable, so for that we can forgive her. When I go to a coffee shop I usually go to stay and relax, often reading or sketching. It is the perfect place for that, with both indoor and outdoor tables, a booth, and a counter. I also appreciated the dog-friendly policy but that's definitely a personal preference and isn't right for everyone. The location is also great, being situated in the French quarter. My only complaint is that I could only visit once on my trip to New Orleans.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I created a Yelp account solely to review this place, which speaks to how much I enjoyed it. This local cafe/coffee shop met my expectations and more. The food and coffee were excellent, and the atmosphere was friendly and casual. The Victorian-style architecture of the dining room added to its appeal. Although the service was a bit slow due to limited staff, the barista was personable. It was the perfect spot for me to relax, read, or sketch, offering both indoor and outdoor seating options. I also appreciated the dog-friendly policy, although I understand it may not be for everyone. Located in the French quarter, the only downside was that I could only visit once during my trip to New Orleans.

input: High pressure tea sales!  Good teas but outrageously expensive.  Try Republic of Tea or even good old Twinings.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: High pressure tea sales! Affordable options: Republic of Tea and Twinings.

input:
oh Millers, how i wanted to like you.  You are close to my house, have ample parking, and large spacious tables.  you even have a fireplace in the back for a little ambiance. 

friends and i tried to come here 2 or 3 times for a quick/inexpensive* bite to eat and every time there was a 30-60 minute wait. we thought this must mean they are really good.  perhaps it just means that people in Springfield are willing to settle for a less than average dining experience.  *side note- this place is not inexpensive. 

hubby and i ordered apps- he got zinger boneless wings, and i got the guacamole. portion size was ENORMOUS on the guac - it could have served 8 people, seriously.  flavor was meh. apparently the wingz were good.  hard to tell what hubby enjoyed more, the wingz or the scantily dressed hostesses. 

our server was great, attentive and pleasant.  When something went wrong she did her best to fix it. That was much appreciated.   Side salad came out wilted and gross. management offered to take it off the check, would have rather had a decent salad in the first place but i digress.  Dinner was not very flavorful - at all - and portion sizes were okay. i got the quesadilla appetizer (which was plenty for an entree) but it was very sloppily put together and had no seasoning at all.  I have had food that is presented better and tastes better at fast food restaurants, where i am happy to pay $5 for a meal.  

At the end of the meal, i badly wanted dessert but didnt want to risk another poorly flavored dish.  Not to mention, all the dishes were like lunch tray plastic, and i felt that a $50-60 dinner for two was at least worth a nicer presentation. who knows, it may have even made up for the bland flavors. 

perhaps i was let down by the fact that there always seemed to be a wait and i had over hyped it in my head.  Never have i wanted to send back everything i ordered at a restaurant before this night.  i will never be back.  my husband says he will order the wings, but takeout only. no more dining in at this place.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
I wanted to like Millers because of its close proximity, ample parking, and spacious tables. They even have a fireplace for ambiance. However, on multiple attempts, my friends and I experienced a 30-60 minute wait, leading us to believe it must be popular despite the less than average dining experience. Additionally, the prices were not inexpensive as expected.

My husband and I ordered appetizers - he enjoyed the zinger boneless wings, while I found the guacamole portion size enormous but the flavor mediocre. Our server was attentive and pleasant, resolving issues promptly. The side salad was wilted and unappetizing, but management offered to remove it from the bill. The dinners lacked flavor and portion sizes were average. My quesadilla appetizer was sloppily made and lacked seasoning. I have had better-tasting and better-presented food at fast food restaurants for a fraction of the price.

I wanted dessert but was hesitant due to the risk of another disappointing dish. The cheap plastic dishes used for a $50-60 dinner for two were underwhelming. The overall experience may have been colored by the constant wait and inflated expectations. This was the first time I felt compelled to send back everything I ordered. I have no plans to return, though my husband may still order the wings for takeout.

input: Came back again bc I am stuck with a membership... The facilities are nice but they do NOT do a good job. Been coming here for 6 months because of the membership I bought. Every time I have to have them re-vacuum or wipe everything down again. They don't clean out the cup holders or wipe the door kick panels. So frustrating. Some of them on the vacuum side do not seem to speak English so it's even harder to have to explain I need it re-washed :( too bad... The location is perfect for me, if only the quality was
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I returned to this membership-based facility again because I am stuck with it, and while the facilities are nice, they consistently fail to meet expectations. Despite coming here for 6 months due to my membership purchase, I constantly have to request that they re-vacuum and wipe down everything. Moreover, they neglect to clean out the cup holders and wipe the door kick panels, which is incredibly frustrating. Additionally, communication is a challenge as some of the staff on the vacuum side do not seem to speak English well, making it even more difficult to convey my needs for re-washing. It's disappointing because the location is perfect for me, if only the quality of service matched.

input:
I am sort of a simple man, so I had never been to a liquor bar before. I have been to The Libertine twice and had a good experience both times. They use fresh ingredients all the way down to the crushed ice, which they crush with a mallet right at the bar. 

The biggest problem I ran into was figuring out which restroom was the men's. You have to look at the hair on the dimly lit pictures that indicate which is which, all the faces look the same.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: As a novice to liquor bars, I had a positive experience at The Libertine on both my visits. They impressively use fresh ingredients, including their crushed ice which is prepared at the bar using a mallet. However, I faced difficulty in distinguishing the men's restroom as the dimly lit pictures had similar-looking faces but required identifying the hair to determine the correct one.

input: Came with the family based on a recommendation and was not disappointed.  I consider myself to be a bit of a Pizza connoisseur and this was right up there.  The staff was friendly and the food came out quick.  Solid experience across the board.  I would come back and recommend it to others.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Came with family on a recommendation, not disappointed. As a Pizza connoisseur, I was impressed. Friendly staff, quick service. Solid experience overall. Would return and recommend.

input: We tried these at the Collingswood Art Festival this weekend. they are a bit pricey, but worth it. The flavor is perfect. they aren't greasy. I will be seeking them out. Once you try them... you will want to have them again. they are a light cheddar curd, battered and friend. You don't taste grease or batter. the flavor of the cheese is delicious, and so stringy and melty. The sauces are a delicate compliment to the curd. Well worth the splurge.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We tried these at the Collingswood Art Festival – pricey but worth it. The flavor is perfect, not greasy. I'll be seeking them out again. They are light cheddar curds, battered and fried without a greasy or batter taste. The cheese is delicious, stringy, and melty. The sauces complement the curd delicately. Definitely worth the splurge.

input:
Yats rocks. You walk in and they've got 4-6 cauldrons full of your choices...which are written in sidewalk chalk on a blackboard. There's always something vegetarian, and a plate full of any of it costs five fitty. Add a buck and you can get a split plate of 2 delectable cajun creations with rice. But the best part is the ridiculously awesome garlic bread...which you can get a bowl of for like a buck.

Not only is the food awesome, but the owner (Joe Vuskovich) is a local celebrity. He's a famed restaurateur from New Orleans that sells his secret spice to restaurants everywhere. Everybody in town knows him (despite the fact that there are two other locations) and he's highly supportive of local bands and kids that most older people stay away from.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Yats is a fantastic restaurant known for its variety of choices displayed on a blackboard. They have 4-6 cauldrons filled with delicious options, including vegetarian dishes. A plate of any food costs only $5.50, and for an additional dollar, you can enjoy a split plate of 2 tasty cajun creations with rice. The standout feature is the incredibly tasty garlic bread, which is available in a bowl for just a dollar. The owner, Joe Vuskovich, is a local celebrity and renowned restaurateur from New Orleans who shares his secret spice with restaurants across the city. He is well-known in the community and actively supports local bands and unconventional youngsters whom most older people avoid. Despite having two other locations, Joe remains a beloved figure in town.

input:
Today after our Ethiopian food fiasco (see Selam review), we literally RAN into Pi after waiting hours to be served at the prior restaurant. We must have looked like a pack of hungry wolves so we told the hostess what had just happened. She seated us right away and sent us two orders of garlic bread (which we later found out were comped!). 

We ordered two pizzas and scarfed it all down. Pi has been consistently good on every visit I have made since I've moved to STL. Service is always excellent. Both the deep dish and thin crust are amazing every time.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After a disappointing experience at Selam, we coincidentally stumbled upon Pi while famished. The hostess promptly seated us upon hearing what had occurred, generously treating us to two complimentary orders of garlic bread. We devoured two pizzas from their menu and found them consistently delicious, just like every previous visit since relocating to STL. The service at Pi is consistently excellent, and both their deep dish and thin crust options are consistently amazing.

input: I went here to get my wisdom teeth out and they did a great job. The only complaint I have is that I never see the same dentist. I've been going here for 5 years.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The dentist did a great job removing my wisdom teeth, but my only complaint is that I have never seen the same dentist in the 5 years I have been coming here.

input:
After hearing about this place from a fellow Yelp Elite, my SO and I decided to try this place! We were warned of possible waiting times so came here on a Saturday around 10:45, and a line was already forming! 

For apps, we ordered the takoyaki and fried octopus. The takoyaki are delicious-an order comes with 5 balls that were perfectly cooked and topped with sauces. Takoyaki are little circular doughs with squid in the middle, topped with sauces and squid flakes (?). I definitely recommend this app. As for the fried octopus, it was just fried without sauces on top and came with mayo on the side, but it didn't come with enough mayo to dip the octopus in.

For ramen, I got the red spicy tonkotsu ramen and my SO got the black garlic tonkotsu ramen. For both ramen, the thin noodles were mushy/overcooked and just didn't quite fit with the ramen. That was the flaw with the dishes, and it tasted like the noodles were overcooked in a pot of flour-y water so it wasn't as clean (which explains the mushy feeling). They should use more bouncy noodles for this.

Now let's talk about the broth. The broth is flavorful, but the red chili broth was a bit too spicy for me and covered up the depth of the broth. I prefer the black garlic tonkotsu broth for that reason.

Overall, delicious food and pricing is reasonable. The decor is very nice as well, but screaming kids that were running around didn't make our meal pleasant.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Based on a Yelp Elite recommendation, my SO and I decided to try this place. We arrived on a Saturday around 10:45 and found a line already forming. We ordered takoyaki and fried octopus for appetizers. The takoyaki was delicious with perfectly cooked balls topped with sauces. The fried octopus lacked enough mayo for dipping. Moving on to the ramen, I had the red spicy tonkotsu and my SO had the black garlic tonkotsu. The noodles in both were mushy and overcooked, detracting from the overall dish. The flavor of the broth was good, but the red chili broth was too spicy, overshadowing its depth. The black garlic tonkotsu broth was preferred. The food was tasty and reasonably priced, and the decor was nice. However, the presence of screaming, running children affected our dining experience.

input: Hands down best breakfast in Philly!  I've only been here for four months, but I have tried nearly every "Best of" spot in town.  I'm a breakfast fanatic so I get little over critical.  However, this small cafe has managed to create incredible flavor while keeping their dishes fresh and simplistic.  While the actual space is "cozy," this menu could easily keep a place as big as Parc overflowing with patrons.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This small cafe in Philly offers the best breakfast in town. Despite being critical of breakfast spots, I have tried and tested almost all the "Best of" places here. This cafe stands out with its incredible flavor and fresh, simple dishes. Although the space is cozy, the menu is so outstanding that it would attract a large crowd even in a bigger establishment like Parc.

input: If I could give this place 6 stars I would. Don't let the looks deceive you, great diner food. Biscuits and gravy were incredible. Portions were more than I could eat.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place deserves 6 stars! Despite its appearance, the diner serves amazing food, especially the biscuits and gravy. The portions are huge and I couldn't finish everything.

input:
This place is hip.  Perhaps too hip for many over 35 but if you can tolerate the boisterous and extremely casually attired youth--I haven't worn a suit in 20 years either but even 20 year olds should have something besides skinny jeans and T-shirts with borderline obscene slogans in their closets--the food is worth it and the staff copes well.   

I had a 6:00 reservation (obtained the day before) but the sky seemed threatening a downpour so I came early to avoid it and was seated 20 minutes or so before the appointed time.  I often don't even make reservations and have no trouble getting seated at popular places by being there when they open or, for those open all day, coming before the popular dinner hour, but that didn't work the day before at Lüke.  Even at 4:30 the place was packed so I did make one for the following day.

My meal started with the crispy Brussel Sprouts.  Even if you hate Brussels sprouts (I like them), don't be afraid to try this dish--if no one told you you might not know what you were eating.  They are in some sort of sweet/sour sauce/dressing and fried both slightly blackened and crispy as advertised . . . tossed with almond slices, small bits of jalapeño and sprinkled with shavings of cheese on top.

Then I had pork schnitzel and "pommes frites" (that's shoestring fries to the Galliphobes).  It came with whitish gravy in a pitcher, I suppose to make it "Southern".  The gravy was good but I skipped eating it, doing that the usual way with a squeeze of lemon.  It was excellent and the fries were fine too.

I finished with some excellent decaf and a glass of Kahlua--I had had iced tea with the meal so some alcohol was not an excess.

A lady who was some sort of hostess dropped by my table while I was eating to make sure everything was OK and when told I needed ketchup (for the fries), went and got me some (in a dainty little single-serve Heinz bottle).  My waiter also checked several times but didn't hover.

I am giving it 4 stars.  The 5th star is withheld because of the crowded dining room and noise level . . . nothing to do with the food which I greatly enjoyed.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is popular among younger crowds and might not be as appealing to those over 35. The food is worth it though, despite the boisterous and casually dressed clientele. I made a reservation for 6:00 but arrived early due to bad weather and was seated ahead of time. It's usually easy for me to find a seat without a reservation, but that didn't work at this restaurant. The Brussels sprouts appetizer was surprisingly delicious, even for people who don't typically enjoy them. The pork schnitzel and shoestring fries were excellent, although I skipped the gravy. I ended the meal with decaf and a glass of Kahlua. The staff, including a friendly hostess and attentive waiter, ensured everything was satisfactory. I rate it 4 stars due to the crowded and noisy dining area, but the food was highly enjoyable.

input: Beers were amazing! I got the porter, the double IPA and the table gutt and they were all fantastic. Food was also killer if you like Russian cuisine. They had a special when I went with a sausage and sauerkraut which was tasty. I also got the pickled everything appetizer, great choice. This place rules.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The beers at this place were fantastic, including the porter, double IPA, and table gutt. The food, especially the Russian cuisine, was killer. I highly recommend trying their special sausage and sauerkraut dish, as well as the pickled everything appetizer. Overall, this place rules.

input: There are a ton of good sushi places in Reno and I have tried them all, but it always seems like Rickshaw has the freshest fish. I'm not a big fan of rolls and sauces, and opt mainly for Nigiri or sashimi. You can get some dressed up roll anywhere, hell you can buy them in the store, but if you are a true fan of sushi, just fish is where its at and Rickshaw has some of the freshest in town.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Rickshaw in Reno has the freshest fish among all the sushi places I've tried. I prefer Nigiri or sashimi over rolls and sauces, as the focus on just fish is more appealing to true sushi fans. Dressed up rolls can be found anywhere, even in stores, but for the best sushi experience, Rickshaw is the place to go.

input: This was my 1st visit here.  Overall, not that impressed!  To start with parking was really bad!  There are good choices of beer on draft.  The food was ok.  We split a few appetizers.  The fried olives were very tasty & different!  The rest of the appetizers were ok: the blue cheese chips, calamari, & meat/cheese platter.  I would try this place again, but overall not thrilled!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: First visit here, not impressed. Bad parking. Good beer selection. Okay food, split appetizers. Fried olives tasty, rest okay (blue cheese chips, calamari, meat/cheese platter). Would try again, but not thrilled.

input: Really not sure what the hype was when it opened. It's fine, the ambiance was nice, but the menu is limited and food is nothing to write home about. They are in a nice location so at least if you decide to wait, then you have things to see...
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The opening of this place didn't live up to the hype. The ambiance is nice, but the menu is limited and the food isn't outstanding. However, being in a good location gives you something to do while waiting.

input:
This place was amazing! I only tried their ice cream I really wanted to try the hot chocolate but didn't get a chance :(. Well the ice cream was great! The first night I came here I got a brownie sundae all for myself, brownie on the bottom and three scoops of ice cream topped with whipped cream and nuts. I finished it all happily! I chose pumpkin cake flavor which was delicious and smooth. I also got pralines and cream that was better than other praline ice creams. The Tennessee fudge was vanilla with fudge swirled it was good not too special. 

The next time I came I got nutter butter ice cream that was really good had cookie pieces in it! I got the hot fudge topping over it and that was a great combination. 

The service was great the workers were really nice and patient with me haha indecisive! They would joke around with me and let me sample all I wanted. Also no judgement for eating all the brownie sundae alone :) lol
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
The place was amazing! Although I only tried their ice cream, I really wanted to try the hot chocolate but didn't get the chance. The first night I had a brownie sundae with a brownie on the bottom, three scoops of ice cream, whipped cream, and nuts. I happily finished it all and loved the delicious and smooth pumpkin cake flavor. The pralines and cream flavor was better than other praline ice creams. The Tennessee fudge flavor was good, but nothing too special. 

The second time I visited, I had their nutter butter ice cream with cookie pieces, topped with hot fudge. It was a fantastic combination. The service was great, with friendly and patient workers who joked around with me and let me sample as much as I wanted. They also didn't judge me for eating the entire brownie sundae alone.

input:
My dad and I were here for lunch and after reading some of the reviews, I was excited to check out this restaurant located where an O'Henry's once stood.

The place was fairly empty at 1 on a Friday and we were lead upstairs. Honestly, there's not much going on up there and it was a bit warm, but we decided to stick it out. Everything on the menu looked great and I decided to get the Catfish Acadian, which is catfish topped with crawfish and sauce with a side of vegetables. My dad got the pork chop.

My dish was great! I have no idea what was in the sauce but it was delicious and it was a perfect pairing with the fish. The vegetables were also really good; they were nicely cooked and fresh. My dad wasn't overly blown away by his pork chop, so if you find yourself here you might want to stick to the seafood.

Bria was our waitress and she was wonderful! She was attentive, kept the fresh iced tea coming and she was extremely personable. She was probably the highlight of the visit.

I'm not sure if I would go back. The food was good, but the atmosphere left something to be desired and I feel like I can get good catfish at plenty of places without going out of my way. I might go back at dinner, when the weather is cooler, and sit on the balcony outside as Harry suggested.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: My dad and I had lunch at this restaurant, which is located where an O'Henry's once stood. The place was fairly empty at 1 on a Friday and we were taken upstairs. Although there wasn't much happening up there and it was a bit warm, we decided to stay. The menu had great options and I ordered the Catfish Acadian, which was delicious. The sauce paired perfectly with the fish, and the vegetables were nicely cooked and fresh. My dad wasn't impressed with his pork chop, so seafood might be a better choice. Our waitress, Bria, was attentive, friendly, and kept our iced tea refreshed. Overall, the food was good, but the atmosphere could be improved. I might consider going back for dinner on the balcony as Harry suggested, when the weather is cooler.

input:
Well, well.... Where do I start with this place? First time experience, went in with my partner.

Walking in at about 7:30 on a Friday night (st paddys day weekend even)  and the  place had about 4 customers. That should have been my first clue as to what our experience was going to be like.

We seated ourselves and the waitress, an older gal maybe mid to late 40's who had greasy stringy unwashed hair and rotting teeth came up and took our drink order. My girlfriend got a Dr. Pepper and I got a water. She brought out Coke instead of DP. No biggie. We let it go, assuming it was an honest mistake. After about 10 minutes she returns and we order a 12 piece "jumbo" wing basket ($11.99), a 6 piece($7.99), and a beer batter sampler($11.99). 20 minutes pass and finally here comes our appetizer. The waitress throws the basket of appetizers on the table  and says "here's your food." Very flat with a big attitude and walks off. The beer battered mushrooms were doughy and undercooked. We had a single half full ranch cup to share between us for the big platter and she avoided our table when she saw we needed more.
***let me note that this waitress is giving the customers at the 3 tables surrounding us WAY better customer service. Even brought their food out in a timely manner with no attitude whatsoever.
I decide to let the mushrooms slide for the moment. I used to work in a restaurant and I understand that mistakes happen, however this far into the experience I'm being mighty generous since it's a first time experience.
We finish our appetizer and we wait and wait and wait and finally she comes by and takes the platter returning 10 minutes later with our wings. She makes no inquiry about the broken open, clearly undercooked, mushrooms still sitting on the platter.
I got the 12 piece with a single half full ranch. Again. Food on the table, doesn't ask if we need anything else which is something she is doing for other customers. at this point we have been here for about 40 minutes.

I got half regular and half thai flavor. The wings were NOT jumbo. They were puny. The flavor was good for the thai, and the waitress even stopped by to check up on us, though I wouldn't consider walking by quickly and saying in your flat attitude tone "youguysdoingalright?okaycool." Really all that helpful since she came and went so fast it took me a second to understand her. I had to reiterate for my girlfriend.  When I started on the regular I bit into my drumstick and had to fish a feather out of my mouth. DISGUSTING. It was that point that the entire experience was completely and thoroughly unacceptable.  The wings were soggy because they batter them or something on top of all that.  At first I had no plans other than to pay for the meal and leave the waitress 2 pennies and be on my merry way. But when the waitress came and asked if we needed a box I said no with 6 wings still on my plate, OBVIOUS SOMETHING WAS WRONG, again. She was going to take my stuff and make no inquiry to right the situation. I asked for the manager. Took a minute but finally the manager came over (mind you it is still pretty dead, what are these people doing I wonder?) I explained the food issues but blew off bringing up our treatment by the waitress. Normally I give the benefit of the doubt on this one but it was blatantly obvious that we were being treated differently with a different attitude than other patrons because we are a same-sex couple. Like our table had a contagious disease that prevented us from getting food in a timely manner, and getting drink and condiment refills too, regardless of the *empty* cups on the edge of the table. It wasn't like we were off in the distance. She had to walk by our table every time to communicate with the surrounding tables.

Anyways. The manager experience wasn't the greatest, but I wasn't going to pay for that meal after the feather thing, and she comped everything. BUT only after slightly arguing with us about the undercooked mushrooms, which by the way come frozen which  makes the fact that they weren't cooked all the way acceptable I guess? Don't know. Don't care. I WILL NOT BE GOING BACK!!!

2 stars because they did comp the meal, the waitress got lucky. If I would have had to pay for anything she wouldn't have gotten a tip due to the attitude but we left her $4 anyway since we didn't have to pay for the meal.  THAT IS THE ONLY REASON.
1 star though for the overall experience. Same-sex couples, steer clear. You aren't welcome there and it's obvious.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: First time experience at this place on a Friday night. The place was not busy, with only 4 customers. The waitress had poor hygiene and brought the wrong drink. We ordered appetizers and had to wait a long time for them to arrive. The mushrooms were undercooked and the waitress did not provide enough ranch dressing. Our wings were not jumbo-sized and one had a feather in it. We had to ask for the manager to address the issues. The manager comped our meal but argued about the undercooked mushrooms. We will not be going back due to the overall experience. We gave 2 stars because the meal was comped but the service was poor. We left a small tip. It was evident that same-sex couples are not welcome at this establishment.

input: Why don't we have a Target?  I thought K-Mart was going out of business.  Well not this one, this miserable son of a bitch refuses to die.  They had the audacity to try to update it.  It reminds me of Jack Palance its old, tired, and smells funny, but it ain't going know where.    I wish a shiny new Target would come along and stab this relic of a store through the heart with its superior retail sword.  I have experienced on no less than 5 occasions of a product being labeled as on sale only to be charged full price at the counter.  Then I have to stop the line to back to the aisle and grab the sign to show it to the cashier.  Once I bought a beach chair here, well my wife saw the dopeness of said chair and wanted to copy me.  I return to the store the next day (happened to be 80 degrees and sunny) and those SOB's raised the price of the chair $10.  I was pissed yo.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Why don't we have a Target nearby? I thought K-Mart was going out of business, but this particular store seems determined to stay alive. They attempted to update it, but it still feels old and not in a good way. I wish a new Target would come and replace this outdated place. On multiple occasions, I've found products labeled as on sale, only to be charged full price at the counter. It's frustrating to have to go back and show the sign to the cashier, halting the line. Another time, I bought a beach chair only to find out that they had raised the price by $10 the very next day. It made me really angry.

input:
Don't let the outside fool you-this place is much cuter and nicer inside than you would expect! 

Food is good and reasonably  priced. We ordered papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. Papaya salad is always refreshing, but this place overdoes it on the fish sauce. Anything triple flavor is always a safe but delicious choice. I would say their king soup, with choice of protein, is a winner. 

And also, BYO!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place may not look impressive from the outside, but it is surprisingly cute and pleasant inside. The food is both delicious and reasonably priced. We tried the papaya salad, triple flavor duck, and king tofu soup. The papaya salad is refreshing, although they use too much fish sauce. Anything with triple flavor is a safe and tasty option. The king soup, which allows you to choose your protein, is definitely a winner. Another bonus is that you can bring your own beverages.

input:
I feel so comfortable with the Mazzoni Center.  I, and many others, am incredibly lucky and grateful that these services exist.  Going through all sorts of life challenges can be painful and frightening when you know you're assumed to be a certain way.  Here, there are no assumptions.  They know who they're working with, and they are sensitive without the need to pry for information.  If you're in need of gynecology and you're not a woman, for example, they know exactly how to handle your needs while prioritizing respect for your identity.

My biggest concern is the physical space in which the Mazzoni Center clinic exists.  I feel sort of exposed in the waiting room.  I hope that they someday have the funds to upgrade to a larger, more private space.

If you visit during youth drop-in hours rather than making an appointment, you will probably wait a very long time to see someone.  This is completely understandable, in my opinion.  They'll advise you regarding what time you should show up if you call.

Occasionally, I've noticed lapses in communication; I have been kept waiting in the exam room before with no one around and no idea how much longer I would have to wait.  This is not a common issue, and I find that, overall, I receive more attentive service here than at any other clinic I've visited.

Be aware that the doctor you want to speak with may not always be available over the phone.  Don't be afraid to leave messages with reception.  You'll always receive quick assistance.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I appreciate the comfort and gratitude I feel at the Mazzoni Center. They provide valuable services and create a welcoming environment without assumptions. However, the physical space of the clinic's waiting room makes me feel exposed, and I hope they can upgrade to a larger, more private space in the future. If you choose to visit during youth drop-in hours, expect a long wait time, but they can advise you on the best time to arrive if you call ahead. Occasionally, there have been lapses in communication, with no one available in the exam room and uncertainty about waiting times. However, overall, I receive attentive service at this clinic compared to others. It's important to note that the desired doctor may not always be available over the phone, but leaving messages with reception will provide quick assistance.

input:
If I could give half a star I would, I'm from Tx, and anyone that thinks this is BBQ, I am willing to apologize to you for being led to believe that this is what BBQ is like.
I ordered the sample platter, horrific, the chicken looked and tasted like frozen pressed meat, the ribs.... All cartilage, the sausage, bland.... The sauce.... Walmart basic sauce with cups of sugar thrown in.... Extremely overpriced for ummm.... A child's plate (what it seemed like). I would never recommend this place to anyone.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I would give half a star if I could. Being from Texas, I feel compelled to apologize to anyone who thinks this is BBQ. I ordered the sample platter and it was horrible. The chicken tasted like frozen pressed meat and the ribs were all cartilage. The sausage was bland and the sauce was just basic sauce from Walmart with cups of sugar added. It was excessively overpriced for what seemed like a child's plate. I cannot recommend this place to anyone.

input:
Really great place for wine!

Came here with my dining group, there was about 20 of us on a Friday, for their Happy Hour. Excellent wine happy hour where all glasses are $5 or you can take $5 off any bottle of wine, which is a great deal if you're sharing with a few people...great way to try a few bottles.

The food was also great! Cheese plates are the way to go here! Excellent selections! Several of my foodie friends ordered sandwiches, which looked & smelled amazing! They all raved about them!

The ambiance is very warm and inviting! They do a great job decorating, especially around the holidays! My favorite space is the enclosed patio area, adjacent to the main dining area. Super warm and romantic on those cold winter evenings! 

The service is great as well!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is a really great spot for wine. They have an excellent happy hour where all glasses are $5 or you can take $5 off any bottle of wine. The food is also great, especially the cheese plates. The ambiance is warm and inviting, especially during the holidays. The service is also great.

input: Rude staff. Can't even get a salad order right. Overpriced by the slice. When we sat down to wait for our food I thought wow this is taking a long time given the fact we were the only people in there. I guess it should stay that way. Don't waste your money.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Staff rude. Salad order wrong. Overpriced slices. Long wait despite being only customers. Save money, avoid.

input: Really good, really authentic! This is some of the BEST Mexican cuisine I've tasted since my nana cooked for me; I'm from California so I would know. The enchiladas w/mole are awesome and the carne asada tacos remind me of Rosarito Beach, yummy!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Authentic and delicious! This Mexican cuisine is truly some of the best I've had since my nana's cooking. As a California resident, I know good Mexican food, and these enchiladas with mole and carne asada tacos are reminiscent of Rosarito Beach - absolutely yummy!

input:
You need a Cinnamon Roll from the bake house.  You probably need two; life would have just a little less happiness and light without their Cinnamon Rolls.
The coffee and salads are also excellent, a lovely Saturday morning breakfast treat.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Get a Cinnamon Roll from the bake house for a delightful breakfast. Two would be even better, as their absence would diminish the joy and brightness in life. Additionally, their coffee and salads make for an excellent Saturday morning meal.

input: I had the carrot cake.... Very disappointed tasted like licorice and baking soda cooking powder. It's too bad because everything looks so delicious :( also didn't like the chocolate chips in it either.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had the carrot cake and I was very disappointed. It tasted like licorice and baking soda cooking powder. It's unfortunate because everything else looked delicious. Additionally, I didn't enjoy the chocolate chips in it either.

input: You can't beat the prices for the unlimited food, but I've had better. The sushi is delicious, the salad was subpar and the crab Rangoon was probably the worst I've had. I've been twice and would definitely go again.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Prices for unlimited food are unbeatable, but the quality varies. The sushi is delicious, while the salad falls short and the crab Rangoon is the worst I've ever tasted. Despite this, I've been there twice and would go again.

input: Best chicken you could ever hope for in bourbon st. The chicken is good. The sauce is good. Everything is goof
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Best chicken on Bourbon St. Chicken and sauce are both excellent. Overall, everything is fantastic.

input:
Reviewing the food.
Hard to justify $16 for a burger and fries BUT wowow this burger was so delicious. I'm not sure if I was just starving but ordered the Lama burger and the patty size is quality. They also have random ingredients thrown in that you probably haven't seen before like gruyere stuffed in a pepper on your burger. Fries came out nice and crisp vs. soggy and the bun on that burger was great. You order inside by the Nook and then can sit around. They have tons of craft beer to choose from and I could see this place getting packed on the weekends.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Though expensive at $16, the burger and fries at this restaurant were incredibly delicious. I had the Lama burger, and the patty was of high quality and sizable. The surprising addition of gruyere stuffed in a pepper on the burger was unique and noteworthy. The fries were crispy and the bun was excellent. The dining process involved ordering inside near the Nook and plenty of seating options are available. Additionally, their wide selection of craft beers suggests that this place can become quite crowded on weekends.

input: Stopped in for breakfast on 12/2/17 I used to like it here for breakfast.  Service was slow coffee was not hot, grits were only warm and twenty minute wait for cinnamon biscuit after breakfast was brought to table then ten minutes to pay at counter to get out of the place there are better places to get breakfast in the area.  Should have went with my first choice instead of here.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: On 12/2/17, I had breakfast at this place which I used to enjoy. However, the service was slow, coffee was not hot, grits were only warm, and there was a twenty-minute wait for a cinnamon biscuit after my breakfast was served. Additionally, it took ten minutes to pay at the counter before leaving. There are better breakfast options in the area, and I regret not choosing my initial preference.

input: simply the best! everything from here is good! I come from a very Italian family and whenever there is a family event, there is always Termini brothers dessert trays! Their cannolis are amazing! Highly recommend.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Termini Brothers dessert trays are simply the best! Coming from a very Italian family, we always rely on them for all our family events. Their cannolis are absolutely amazing and I highly recommend them.

input: It's a nice place. Really nice! Great service and awesome restaurants in the hotel. Clean rooms
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is really nice with great service, awesome restaurants in the hotel, and clean rooms.

input:
After our recent trip to New Orleans, I came back to Reno appreciating this place even more than before! 
The shrimp po boy is my favorite thing on the menu! And their corn bread is amazing as well!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: After visiting New Orleans, I returned to Reno with a newfound appreciation for this place. The shrimp po boy and their incredible corn bread are definitely my favorite items on the menu.

input: People in this place are generally friendly, but do not make the mistake of going to Katie.  She went through my hair like a bulldozer-- slapped colour on it in less than 5 minutes and cut it in even less time.  I think she was in a rush to get out of there (it was late in the day), but then she shouldn't have agreed to take me on.  The whole thing cost me close to $200, and I was shaken up by the experience.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Generally friendly people here, but avoid Katie. She rushed through my hair in less than 5 minutes, applying color like a bulldozer, and cutting it even faster. It seemed like she wanted to leave early, but she shouldn't have agreed to take me. Spent nearly $200 and was left shaken by the experience.

input: Favorite place in Nashville for breakfast!! This is a must go to spot!! Near Vandy and always busy...park in the back lot and be sure to get the parking ticket from the machine so you won't be charged...its free parking for a specified amount of time. My favorite is banana pancakes...think banana bread only in a pancake!! Perfection!!!! I don't leave Nashville until I go here to eat my pancakes!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Must-visit breakfast spot near Vandy in Nashville. Park in the back lot, grab a parking ticket to avoid charges - it's free for a limited time. Try the delicious banana pancakes, a must-have! I never leave Nashville without indulging in them.

input:
Yes, there are vegan options in University City, you just have to know where to look for them. MexiCali has a number of great options.

Many options here can be made vegan by holding the cheese. I absolutely adore the marinated tofu burrito. The tofu has a wonderfully chewy texture, and along with the black beans, the meal packs a protein-filled punch that will leave you full well past dinner-time, should you choose to finish it.  The sweet potato and plantain burrito is purportedly dairy-free, and it's another delicious, filling vegan option. The veggie tacos come with a spicier version of the sweet potato, the marinated tofu and some cabbage on doubled corn tortillas. The tacos are not as filling as the burritos, but they're a delicious lighter option. Finally, a fourth option for vegans: the guacamole burrito. They homemade guac is to-die-for delicious. 

I end up at MexiCali about once a week. I've been going since they were just a lunch truck 8 years back. There's often a line at the restaurant, but this place has been around for years and they have a great system to get you your burrito in a very timely manner.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Vegan options are available in University City, particularly at MexiCali where you can find a variety of delicious options. By holding the cheese, many menu items can be made vegan. The marinated tofu burrito offers a satisfying, chewy texture with black beans, providing a protein-filled meal. The sweet potato and plantain burrito is another filling, dairy-free choice. The veggie tacos feature spicier sweet potato, marinated tofu, and cabbage on double corn tortillas, while the guacamole burrito is a must-try with its homemade, tasty guac. MexiCali has been a favorite spot for the writer, who has been visiting since their days as a lunch truck. Despite often having a line, the restaurant's efficient system ensures quick service.

input:
Great breakfast fare and all. Eggs provençale was pretty good; all kinds of herbs and seasonings, but cooked inconsistently. Tomato on the side was awesome.

Omelets were executed well, and the pastries were pretty impressive.

But the coffee was horrendously bad. And without good coffee, what's the point of breakfast?

And I still can't trust restaurants that have misspellings on their menus. Even if the misspelling is from another language.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The breakfast had great options including delicious Eggs provençale with various herbs and seasonings, although they were cooked inconsistently. The tomato side dish was excellent. The omelets were well-prepared and the pastries were impressive. However, the coffee was extremely poor, which was disappointing. Additionally, there was a lack of trust in the restaurant due to misspellings on the menu, even if they were related to another language.

input: Another Yelper hit it -- this is a noisy, crowded restaurant with big screen TVs.  I wouldn't call it a sports bar.  Nothing wrong with the place.  Cool location, good beer selection.  The food - delicious, but eliminates itself as a "sports bar". My sons and I wanted to catch some pub grub and the hockey game.  Got the game.  The grub-- eclectic.  Do go here if you want a busy, bustling, energetic, tasty, flavorful, thumping music-beat experience.  Don't go here if you want  a burger, a beer and a hockey game amidst sports conversation.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This restaurant is noisy and crowded with big screen TVs, but it wouldn't be considered a sports bar. The location is cool and they have a good selection of beer. The food is delicious, but it doesn't fit the traditional "sports bar" menu. If you're looking for a lively and flavorful experience with thumping music, this is the place to go. However, if you want a simple burger, beer, and the ability to watch a hockey game while having sports conversations, then this may not be the right spot for you.

input: Fabulous, quick, stress free windshield repair. .. didnt cost a penny out of pocket. I would definitely use this company again and would recommend to anybody!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Fast, hassle-free windshield repair that's absolutely free! Highly recommended and definitely a company worth using again.

input: I was so excited about this meal, I came home to review it immediately. The service was outstanding and the food I'd say was some of the best in New Orleans. Even the freshly made bread was piping hot and delicious. We started with the oysters good enough, which were four fried oysters with bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon- a must get. Then we both got scallops and swine with a butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. All of the entrees sounded phenomenal, but we both couldn't resist getting that dish. The best part I have to say was the dessert. We got cafe au lait panna cotta with mini glazed donuts, which reminded us of beignets at cafe du monde. Finally, I sampled their house made 'cellos, including ginger and limecellos, and they were unique and delicious. An amazing experience!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I was thrilled with this meal and immediately came home to review it. The service was outstanding and the food was among the best in New Orleans. The freshly made bread was piping hot and delicious. We started with the must-get oysters, four fried oysters with bearnaise sauce and Benton's bacon. For our main course, we both had scallops and swine with butternut squash purée and balsamic vinegar. The dessert, cafe au lait panna cotta with mini glazed donuts, was the highlight. It reminded us of beignets at cafe du monde. We also tried their unique and delicious house made 'cellos, including ginger and limecellos. Overall, it was an amazing experience!

input:
Absolutely amazing!!! My girlfriend and I went on a Wednesday night for Restaurant week and didn't know what to expect but we were overly satisfied. We ordered blood orange margaritas and they were strong and delicious. For our appetizers we had meatballs and let me tell you they weren't your average meatballs. They were veal and beef meatballs that melted in your mouth. Our other appetizer was some sort of grilled cheese that was amazing as well. For our entree we had the fishermen stew that was full of flavor and well balanced. Initially I did not think I was going to like it but it was to die for. Every element of the stew had it's own flavor and it was properly cooked. My girlfriend ordered the steak that came with cauliflower puree and a vegetable medley that was delicious as well. This was the first time we had ever ordered our steak to be medium-well and ever since we've been hooked. The steak was so juicy, tender and seasoned so eloquently and the puree was seasoned beautifully as well. 
The service there was amazing!! I forget the waitors name but he was great with the menu. He helped us order and came back frequently to check on us. 
Overall I think BARRA is amazing. It's not expensive and it is very intimate.  If you are looking for good food and great service at a reasonable price, BARRA is the place to go!!!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: My girlfriend and I had an absolutely amazing experience at BARRA during Restaurant week. We were pleasantly surprised by the delicious blood orange margaritas and the exceptional appetizers, including veal and beef meatballs that melted in our mouths and a fantastic grilled cheese. The entrees, a flavorful fishermen stew and a perfectly cooked steak with cauliflower puree and vegetable medley, exceeded our expectations. The service was outstanding, with a knowledgeable waiter who helped us navigate the menu and frequently checked on us. Overall, BARRA offers delicious food, great service, and an intimate atmosphere at a reasonable price. Highly recommended!

input:
We went here hoping for a good breakfast,  and we weren't disappointed.  We went on Valentine's Day, not because we wanted to, but because we had to.  In doing so,  we knew the wait would be long, which it was (an hour and a half), though i hear there's always a wait. 

The place is buzzing with servers and busboys. The tables around the edges of the room are a bit close to one another,  so seating is tight.  The service was though, considering how busy it was.  I ordered the famed cornmeal pancakes with a side of hash browns and a fried egg.  My girlfriend ordered the banana pancakes with a side of bacon.  Everything was amazing.  The pancakes were hearty but fluffy... The side of bacon only comes with three pieces which is disappointing,  but it was cooked to her liking.  The cornmeal pancakes had just the right amount of everything... Bacon,  peppers... Salsa, sour cream,  syrup... Yes,  all of that.  If you're looking for good coffee,  this is not the place, which was surprising. 

The only question is do you go with the homemade syrup or the maple.... Or both
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We hoped for a good breakfast and weren't disappointed, despite going on a busy Valentine's Day. The wait was long, as expected, but the service was good considering the crowd. I ordered cornmeal pancakes with hash browns and a fried egg, while my girlfriend had banana pancakes with bacon. The food was amazing, with the pancakes being hearty and fluffy. The bacon portion was a bit small, but cooked to her liking. The cornmeal pancakes had a great combination of flavors with bacon, peppers, salsa, sour cream, and syrup. However, the coffee wasn't great, which was surprising. The only question remaining is whether to choose the homemade syrup, the maple syrup, or have both.

input: Went on a Monday to have a daiquiri and watch a little bit of the NBA basketball game.  Asked the young lady working if she would be willing to turn on the game and was told she was watching Netflix.  I guess customer service is not important anymore.  Won't ever go back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Went to have a daiquiri and watch NBA basketball on a Monday. Asked the young lady working to turn on the game, but she declined as she was watching Netflix. Disappointed with the lack of customer service, I won't be returning.

input: There  aren't  enough  stars  to  review  The  Pearl ! Food , service  and  ambiance . I  enjoy  every  minute  of  every  visit ! Not  just  dinner , a genuine  dining  experience  ! Pamper  yourself !
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The Pearl has outstanding food, service, and ambiance. Every visit is enjoyable, not just for dinner, but for a truly exquisite dining experience. Treat yourself and indulge in everything The Pearl has to offer.

input: Pretty good bagels, be sure to ask for extra cream cheese if you like a lot. The people are always pleasant which is unique to Dunedin. The bad thing is the guy doesn't wash his hands or wear gloves. He took a previous customers money, my money,  used the phone and wiped his nose, then he made my bagel. I won't go back. If this doesn't bother you, the bagels are pretty good.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Decent bagels, but request extra cream cheese if desired. The standout aspect is the friendly staff, a rarity in Dunedin. However, a concerning issue is that the employee doesn't wash hands or wear gloves. Observing this, he handled money, used the phone, and wiped his nose before making my order. Due to this, I won't return. If hygiene isn't a concern, bagels are still tasty.

input: Had great reviews. Tried someone new..my husbands cut looks great. My sons cut does not.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: New stylist, great reviews. Husband's cut looks great, son's cut needs improvement.

input:
Good, but expensive. 

We both had steak, and it was pretty darn good. 

The guacamole is nothing special. Yes, it gets made in front of you, but it gets made wrong in my opinion.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
Good steak, but pricey. 

Steak we had was delicious. 

Guacamole is mediocre – made in front of you, but not to my liking.

input: I've been to New Day Meadery quite a few times, and every time I come I'm never disappointed! Normally when I come here I order the South Cider or the Shelby Blue Ribbon, but on my last trip I decided to taste one of their seasonal items. I tasted the Paulding Light which has cranberry, honey, and a touch of lime. It was pretty good, but was not as sweet as Shelby Blue Ribbon in my opinion. But that is what I like about New Day, they always have a variety of meads and ciders that everyone can enjoy, not just sugar fans like myself. All in all it is one of my favorite places in Fountain Square! Their service is always prompt and their staff always friendly.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love New Day Meadery and have been there multiple times. I have never been disappointed with their offerings. My go-to drinks are usually the South Cider or the Shelby Blue Ribbon, but on my last visit, I tried their seasonal option, the Paulding Light. It had a pleasant combination of cranberry, honey, and lime, although it wasn't as sweet as the Shelby Blue Ribbon in my opinion. However, I appreciate that New Day Meadery caters to a variety of tastes, not just those who prefer sweet drinks like me. Overall, it's one of my favorite spots in Fountain Square due to their prompt service and friendly staff.

input: I think this is better than the Philadelphia location. Nevertheless, Szechuan house in Hamilton, NJ is still the best.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Szechuan House in Hamilton, NJ remains the best option, surpassing even the Philadelphia location.

input: The food and service is fantastic.  Everything is fresh and bursting with flavor. I will come back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Fantastic food and service, with fresh and flavorful dishes that will make me want to come back.

input:
Recently went to Make Up For Ever at KOP. Initially had a great experience and bought $75 worth of products. After trying them for 5 days I didn't really like them. I went to return and was told I couldn't because they were opened. Thankfully they let me exchange but I ended up having to shove more money out! Then they stamped a big FINAL SALE on my new receipt. Overall, still not in love with the products and definitely won't be buying from there again.

The Sephora in KOP sells the same Make Up For Ever products and their return policy is unopened or gently used can be returned, so I'll just keep shopping there.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I recently visited Make Up For Ever at KOP and initially had a positive experience, purchasing $75 worth of products. However, after using them for five days, I was not satisfied with the results. When I attempted to return the items, I was informed that I couldn't due to them being opened.
