input:
When giving friends from out of town a tour of the French Quarter, one can only expect they want some classic New Orleans dishes. I've been here a couple of times, but they were the ones that wanted to go, due to their lunch special. It's a nice, well know restaurant that offers a 17.00 lunch special that includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a 4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. I got the Bloody Mary and it was a great size for the price. It was spicy and hit the spot.
They text message you when your table is ready, so were able to walk around the quarter while we waited. Thank god a lot of restaurants are getting rid of the those buzzers that make you feel like you are under house arrest. 
We sat down to a beautiful table right by the open shutters. The servers, were ok. They were busy, but forgot a couple of things we asked for. It was still a great experience though!
I got the pork chop with red beans and the turtle soup. The turtle soup was one of the best I have had. The pork chop was cooked to perfection and the read beans were seasoned very well. It came with cornbread, but it was very dry. After this lunch at noon, I didn't find myself hungry till it was basically time for bed. It was a very generous portion and well worth the money.

Muriel's is a great way to get a classic, good quality New Orleans meal at a decent price. The location is spectacular, and the history behind the restaurant made for great conversation at the table.
Definitely check it out if you are in the Quarter!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: When showing friends around the French Quarter, it's expected that they would want to try classic New Orleans dishes. We went to Muriel's, a well-known restaurant with a $17.00 lunch special that includes a soup or salad, entree, and the option for a $4.00 Bloody Mary or martini. The Bloody Mary was spicy and a good size for the price. They texted us when our table was ready, allowing us to explore the Quarter while we waited. Our table was beautiful and by the open shutters, although the service was a bit forgetful. I ordered the pork chop with red beans and turtle soup. The turtle soup was excellent and the pork chop was perfectly cooked, but the cornbread was dry. The portion size was generous and I didn't get hungry until bedtime. Overall, Muriel's is a great place to get a classic New Orleans meal at a reasonable price. The location is amazing and the restaurant's history makes for interesting conversation. Definitely worth visiting if you're in the Quarter!

input: We stopped here's on the recommendation of our shuttle driver.  The red velvet ice cream is wonderful!! Pieces of cake. Creamy goodness.  Yum!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We came here based on our shuttle driver's recommendation and tried the red velvet ice cream. It was absolutely delicious, with cake pieces and a creamy texture. Yum!

input:
I ate here for the first time today.  The woman that works behind the counter is really friendly and offered to waive the minimum credit order amount ($7), since I work nearby.

The food itself is pretty average for American-Chinese food.  Nothing great, but not bad either.  My sauce was greasy, but the food in general doesn't seem to be (e.g. fried rice).  They do have some vegetarian options which are of the tofu variety as opposed to fake meat. 

I would go back since they have lunch specials that come with rice and either a drink, soup, or egg roll ($5.75).

EDIT: I got super sick after leaving this review, and I'm 99% sure it was food poisoning.  Will not be returning.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I tried this restaurant for the first time today. The counter woman was friendly and waived the minimum credit order amount for me. The American-Chinese food was average, neither great nor bad. The sauce was greasy, but overall the food seemed fine, especially the fried rice. They offer tofu-based vegetarian options. Their lunch specials for $5.75 include rice and a choice of drink, soup, or egg roll. However, I got food poisoning after my visit and will not be returning.

input:
Delicious! 

I wish they took reservations, but my friend and her fiance go there nice and early so that we could snag a seat inside (it was cold out!). 

We ordered the bianco salad ( to share between 2) and the western addition (to share between 4).

I thought the salad was tasty but nothing special, despite the white chocolate shavings. Cute idea, but not enough crunch or pizazz to make the salad seem really fabulous.

The pizza, however, was pretty darn good. We ordered it deep dish to try their special cornmeal crust and were pretty impressed. 
The crust tastes a little bit like cornbread, a little bit like pizza dough, a tiny bit like grease (the good kind) and a lot like YUM!

I don't know if it was the best pizza I've ever had, but it was very good. It would be even better if it were a tad cheaper, and didn't get so crowded! But definitely worth a visit if you're in the area!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Delicious! The restaurant doesn't take reservations, but my friend and her fiance arrived early to secure a seat inside. We shared the bianco salad (for 2) and the western addition (for 4). The salad was tasty but unremarkable despite the white chocolate shavings. However, the deep dish pizza with its special cornmeal crust was pretty darn good. The crust had hints of cornbread and pizza dough, a touch of grease (in a good way), and was overall very enjoyable. While it may not be the best pizza I've had, it's definitely worth a visit if you're in the area, though it could be better priced and less crowded.

input: A downtown without a bookstore is like a downtown without... I don't know I lost the metaphor. It's just sad is what it is. You need books, you need a place to browse, talk with other book lovers, and listen to book readings. Indy Reads is that place. And it's more than that because all proceeds support a great cause, adult literacy. Most of the books are used so donate a book and pick up a new (used) one. You may be surprised at all the books they have that you didn't even know you wanted. They also have a small selection of new books. If they don't have what you're looking for, you can order it. The one thing I don't really like is that the $1 children's books can be jammed so tightly that it's hard to look through them. The kids books are also arranged by color, which makes it harder for me to distinguish between titles as I glance through. Prices are excellent throughout, and the space is really nice. Check it out!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: A downtown without a bookstore is like a sad place. Indy Reads is not just a place to browse books, chat with book lovers, and attend book readings. It's also a great cause, supporting adult literacy. Most books are used, so you can donate one and get a new (used) one. You may find books you never knew you wanted. They also have a small selection of new books. If they don't have what you want, you can order it. The only downside is that the $1 children's books can be tightly packed, making it difficult to browse. The children's books are arranged by color, making it harder to see the titles. Prices are great, and the space is nice. Give it a try!

input: Wish I would have came on Yelp and read the previous reviews, it would've saved me a lot of time and frustration. I ran in today to see if someone could take a look at my right passenger front wheel. My tire pressure light was on and I noticed a piece of tire was lifted. I go in and he tells me it's a couple hours wait. Ok, I'll give you that I just showed up so the wait thing is to be expected. I ask the guy if I can make an appointment to come back. He says its first come first serve. Really? When I've made appts previously with other Just Tires? Why not just say you don't want my service? Bottom line? Guy was rude and lacked any customer service. Went down the street to Mr. Tire and was in and out with a replaced new tire in half an hour. Oh, and they appeared WAY busier based on the waiting area and cars in the garage.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I wish I had read Yelp reviews before coming here. I went today to have someone check my right passenger front wheel because my tire pressure light was on and a piece of the tire was lifted. The person at the shop said I would have to wait a couple of hours, which I understand since I showed up without an appointment. When I asked if I could schedule an appointment for another day, he said it's first come first serve, even though I have been able to make appointments at other Just Tires locations before. This made me feel like they didn't value my business. The guy was rude and showed no customer service skills. I ended up going to Mr. Tire down the street and they promptly replaced my tire in just 30 minutes. They seemed much busier with a full waiting area and lots of cars in the garage.

input: Fantastic experience! I own a flower shop so I am kind of a hard one to please when I send flowers to others but this shop did a GREAT job! I called this afternoon and told the woman that answered the phone to do whatever they would like for x amount of money. My only request was that it was bright and cheery. They hit the nail on the head and delivered it quickly. THANK YOU :)
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Amazing experience! As a flower shop owner, I have high standards when it comes to sending flowers to others. However, this shop exceeded my expectations! When I called this afternoon, I gave them free rein to create a bouquet within a certain budget, with the only request being that it be bright and cheery. They absolutely nailed it and delivered it promptly. Thank you so much! :)

input:
I gave it one star because it doesn't give me an option to give it zero. This place sucks. Where should I start?? Okay, arrived at 7 pm with reservations and was seated in the dungeon. Fine. We ordered queso fundido with chorizo and got a weird looking cheese skillet with tortillas NOT chips. Odd! So had to ask for chips. Should've asked for a trash can. So we asked for some salsa to dress it up a bit -- that took an hour and I'm not exaggerating! The salsa was a thick mushy mess. Could turn the bowl upside down and nothng would've come out. Our food took an hour and a half, too. By that time, we were full on chips -- which were the only good thing on the menu! Oh... My favorite part... I ordered a side of beans and rice to go with my carne asada tacos -- which were more like unseasoned beef tips -- and I got a bowl of hard WHITE rice with refried beans on top. WHITE rice??? Seriously?!

Terrible! Dont waste your time. Taco Bell serves better food than this and that isn't saying much! Service was just as bad!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I gave it one star because it does not offer the option to give it zero. The place is terrible. I arrived at 7 pm with reservations and was seated in an undesirable location. We ordered queso fundido with chorizo and received a strange-looking cheese skillet with tortillas instead of chips. We had to ask for chips separately. We also had to wait an hour for salsa, which turned out to be a thick mushy mess. Our food took an hour and a half to arrive and by then, we were already full on chips, which were the only good thing on the menu. I ordered a side of beans and rice to go with my carne asada tacos, but instead got a bowl of hard white rice with refried beans on top. It was terrible. Don't waste your time here. Taco Bell serves better food, and the service was just as bad.

input: This is a small coffe place own by Karyn, a blond sweet lady with a big smile! Great coffee and they have drive through
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Karyn, a blond lady with a big smile, owns a small coffee place that offers great coffee and has a drive-through option.

input:
This used to be Red's but they knocked of the "R" and re-launched as Ed's, although when I see the sign from outside I keep forgeting it's called Ed's - cause it just looks like part of the sign fell off. Ed's is huge. If you've ever been on a cruise ship, Ed's has a variety of activity spaces, restaurant, bars and lounges under one roof. 

It's endless entertainment. You could probably float around here for a whole week and never get bored. There is a pool room, video games, bowling, a dance area, restaurants, lounges, a stage and much more around every corner you turn. It's a good place for young kids and birthday parties once you're too old for Chucky Cheese. 

Although I've personally never seen a band here my partner has, and it's not that expensive to see good bands like Ween, Jurassic Five or Interpol. The venue's neither big or small, so Ed's can host lesser known but interesting musicians as they can sell upwards of 600 tickets. So for bands that aren't popular enough to fill the Coliseum, Ed's still helps them establish a presence in E-town.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Formerly known as Red's, Ed's is a massive entertainment venue with various activity spaces, restaurants, bars, and lounges. It offers endless entertainment, comparable to being on a cruise ship. From pool rooms, video games, and bowling to dance areas, stages, and more, there is something for everyone. Ed's is a popular destination for young kids and birthday parties, offering a vibrant atmosphere similar to Chucky Cheese. Additionally, Ed's serves as a music venue, hosting both well-known bands like Ween, Jurassic Five, and Interpol, as well as lesser-known but interesting musicians. With a capacity of up to 600 tickets, Ed's helps establish a presence in E-town for bands that may not be popular enough to fill larger venues like the Coliseum.

input: I've had the fortune of eating my way across Asia Pacific, so I might be biased in saying I don't understand the rave reviews. I will say though that the conversation and company I was with more than made up for this!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Although I have had the opportunity to explore various cuisines across Asia Pacific, I must admit that I fail to understand the hype surrounding this particular food. However, I must say that the delightful conversation and company I experienced during the meal made up for it.

input: Very disappointed they no longer have the salad & pizza bar! Used to go to other location all the time, moved away & thought they closed. Then I realized they relocated & was excited about having salad there; I loved the salad bar. Was hoping for a piece of pizza for dinner and some salad. Not anymore:-(  Not unless you want to order a whole pizza!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I am disappointed that they no longer have the salad and pizza bar. I used to go to the other location often but had to move away. I thought they closed, but later found out they relocated. I was excited about having their salad there because I loved their salad bar. I was hoping to have a piece of pizza for dinner along with some salad. Unfortunately, they don't offer it anymore unless you want to order a whole pizza.

input:
They used to make an Amiga bowl that had an abundance of shredded grilled chicken on the bottom of a flour tortilla bowl, a layer of rice topped with grilled onions and peppers with a queso sauce drizzeled over the top.
Tonight there was no rice nor any shredded chicken, it had been replaced with chicken crisps. They are the outer parts of a grilled chicken breast with no moisture and very few of them.
Having met the owner in the past and having his wife wait on me I knew something wasn't right.
I explained to the waitress that this dish had changed and wasn't good! She politely offered something else. What to order...if they had modified a basic dish what was next?
To my surprise a male manager came out and "informed" me that this is exactly what they had been serving for 10 years and I must have either special ordered something or was mistaken.
I said this is not what they had served me for the past 5 years and I never had requested a special order before. 
I also asked what they had done to the phenominal soft tacos? They were usually served in a soft warm flour tortilla and had moisture and flavor. Tonight they were stale and crisp and the filing was bland.  Again he informed me I was mistaken while he held my order that had been sent back to the kitchen in front of me.
I apologized and said I didn't wish for anything else, thank you.
Another manager came out a few moments later apologizing and stated that they are unfamiliar with what I had ordered and would "special order" anything I wanted. I declined.
Apparently their cook walked out tonight and they were winging it.
Too bad it was a good place to get a good mexican meal.
Two thumbs down on Poblano's.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: They used to serve an Amiga bowl with shredded grilled chicken, rice, grilled onions, and peppers, topped with queso sauce. However, tonight the dish was different, with chicken crisps instead of shredded chicken and no rice. I noticed the change and informed the waitress, who offered an alternative. The male manager then claimed that they had always served the dish this way for the past 10 years and questioned my memory. I also mentioned the disappointing soft tacos, which were stale and flavorless. The manager dismissed my concerns, but another manager later apologized and offered to special order anything for me. I declined and left disappointed, as it seemed the restaurant was improvising due to a walkout by their cook. Poblano's received a thumbs down from me.

input:
I like Deweys's primary because it's close to my house.  The pizza looks great and the crust is good.  My gripe with Dewey's is that the pizzas are just so salty.  We had the pepperoni, socrates revenge, and bronx bomber.  It's like a eatting a brick of salt.  I'm not sure if it's the amount of salt sauce combined with the salty meat, but the combo so overwhelming, I tastebuds are numb to any other flavor.  Otherwise, if they fix that, I would love it.  

As for the salads, they're a good size, but seems like something you can toss together yourself.  I usually not get because don't want to spend the money on it.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I like Dewey's primary location due to its proximity to my house. The pizza has great appearance and a good crust. However, my only issue with Dewey's is its excessive saltiness. We tried the pepperoni, Socrates revenge, and Bronx bomber pizzas, and they were all overwhelming in terms of salt content. It could be the combination of the salty sauce and meat, but it numbed my taste buds to other flavors. If they are able to rectify this issue, I would absolutely love Dewey's. As for the salads, they are decently sized but appear to be something easily put together at home. I usually opt-out of ordering them to save money.

input:
I came in with high hopes and left with slight disappointment. 

Our server was super attentive, and very friendly; however I feel like the food was disappointing. Our egg drop soup came out right away at a nice piping hot temperature and when the rest of our food came out it was practically room temperature. 

Feeling adventurous, I had ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts entree with brown rice while he ordered the Sesame Chicken platter. I like the idea of sharing food, but my food was too busy all on its own without adding something else to the mix. The brown rice was cold and very bland while the shrimp was overly sweet and I didn't feel like the candied walnuts and melon balls were complementary flavors.

The chocolate cake we had for dessert was amazing though; 6 layers of chocolate on chocolate. It was so sweet and rich, we ended up sharing a slice.

So to sum up, service was great, dessert was great, but the food needs some work. Sorry PF Changs, I just am not impressed.

One thing I will note (that our server told us) is that they are very big on catering to food allergies (especially gluten).
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had high hopes but left slightly disappointed. The server was attentive and friendly, but the food was underwhelming. The egg drop soup was hot, but the rest of the food was served at room temperature. I ordered the Shrimp with Candied Walnuts with brown rice and found it too busy and lacking flavor. The brown rice was cold and bland, and the shrimp overly sweet. The combination of candied walnuts and melon balls didn't work well together. However, the chocolate cake for dessert was amazing with six layers of rich chocolate. Overall, the service and dessert were great, but the food needs improvement. It's worth mentioning that the restaurant is accommodating to food allergies, particularly gluten.

input: We ordered the rib dinner, pork on a bun, Mac n cheese, baked beans, and cole slaw.  Mac n cheese is worthwhile to prostitute yourself out for! The meat on the ribs had great flavor but was as tender as the bottom of my nikes.  Pulled pork had a sweet taste and was overall very good.  Baked beans were okay, cole slaw was very creamy and I would not gets those again (they have an after taste like lake water). The overall experience of getting BBQ in an abandoned car wash is special, worth a try!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We ordered a rib dinner, pork on a bun, Mac n cheese, baked beans, and cole slaw. The Mac n cheese is amazing. The rib meat had great flavor but lacked tenderness. The pulled pork was sweet and delicious. The baked beans were okay, but the cole slaw had a strange aftertaste. Overall, the experience of having BBQ in an abandoned car wash is unique and worth a try.

input: I love the fries (wow, I'm still thinking about them because they're that good!) but I was not impressed by the beef kebob sandwich.  The sandwich was heavy on the onions and light on the meat, so it could have been better.  I do think that may have been an off sandwich, so I'm thinking of going back to give it a second chance (and to have another helping of fries!).  Smoothies also tasted like syrup and ice.  Prices are fair and service is great.  I love the mom and pop feel of the restaurant :).
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I loved the fries (so good that I'm still thinking about them!) but the beef kebob sandwich was not impressive. It had too many onions and not enough meat. However, I think it might have been a one-time issue, so I'm considering giving it another try (and having more fries!). The smoothies tasted like syrup and ice. Prices are fair and the service is great. Overall, I love the cozy mom and pop atmosphere of the restaurant.

input: It is under new ownership and now called Taqueria Burrito's Grill. Absolutely delish! I love it! The green sauce rocks! I love it on cheese enchiladas. I'm picky about mexican rice and I love theirs. I recently moved back to New Orleans from Houston and one thing I miss is those little Taquerias that most people don't know about. Truly authentic mexican and they recently moved from Houston as well so I knew I was at the right place. It's the only mexican food that I can find in New Orleans East. I'll be a frequent customer. I think I am going back today! Open 7 days a week. Breakfast served 9a-11a. Open past 5PM. There # is 504-242-0573 to call for take out. YUMMY!!!!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Under new ownership, the restaurant has been renamed Taqueria Burrito's Grill and is highly recommended. The green sauce is delicious and pairs perfectly with their cheese enchiladas. Their Mexican rice is excellent, and the restaurant offers truly authentic Mexican cuisine. Recently moved from Houston, they are now the only Mexican food option available in New Orleans East. Open 7 days a week, they serve breakfast from 9am to 11am and are open past 5pm. For take out, call 504-242-0573. Overall, a fantastic dining experience that is worth visiting again and again.

input: Had the Mexican Roll and Philadelphia Roll for take-out. Very disappointed with the portion size of the rolls. There was nothing special with the taste and overall bland.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Disappointed with the small portion size and bland taste of the Mexican Roll and Philadelphia Roll during take-out.

input:
I love going into this place to just browse and see what trendy item I can blow my money on. Living near mass ave shopping can be limited but also very competitive. Between silver in the city, boomerang boutique, global gifts, and homespun you pretty much can find whatever you are looking for as far as gifts go. 

Silver in the city is always my go to first. They are always on top of the newest "it" items for your home and style. They also allow dogs in their store so that's a huge plus because I'm typically walking my dog when I stop in. 

The only reason I am not giving them five stars is that although their employees are super friendly, they definitely watch you. I understand the need for this because they have little items that probably get stolen a lot but I always feel like I have no privacy to browse and debate any purchases. 

Cheers!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love browsing and spending money at this place near mass ave shopping. It's limited but competitive with shops like Silver in the City, Boomerang Boutique, Global Gifts, and Homespun. Silver in the City is my favorite, they have the newest items for home and style. They even allow dogs! The only downside is that the employees watch customers closely, probably because of theft. So I feel a lack of privacy when browsing. Overall, I enjoy shopping there. Cheers!

input: I had takeout because it was about 45 min prior to closing . I ordered the puttanesca. It was delicious . Perfect combo of salty spiciness. There was such a wide variety of menu combos or you could get the fold and creat your own . Genius ! My only gripe is they need to come up with a gluten free dough option. My tummy will pay for this gluttony later .
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had takeout about 45 minutes before closing and ordered the delicious puttanesca, which had a perfect combination of salty spiciness. The menu offered a wide variety of combos or the option to create your own fold. However, my only gripe is that they need a gluten-free dough option, as my tummy will suffer from this gluttony later.

input: Food was great!!!! I had the crab cake Benedict and it was delicious! Great service and smoothies
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food, especially the crab cake Benedict, was delicious! The service was great and they also had tasty smoothies.

input:
The one thing I really wanted for breakfast while in New Orleans was Grillades. I have made them at home from a recipe but never had them in a restaurant. When Yelp searching this place popped up so it was a must for breakfast. 

The restaurant has a diner style atmosphere. We were seated by the window so we got to watch traffic pass by on Canal Street. Our service was quick and our server was great. 

Of course I ordered the Grits and Grillades. Slow roasted beef with peppers and onions in a brown gravy over creamy Gouda cheese grits sounded perfect. It did not disappoint as it was so delicious!  I get excited when I go to a restaurant and order something I've cooked before and it tastes better than mine. This will be a must on any future New Orleans trips.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I really wanted Grillades for breakfast in New Orleans, so I decided to try a restaurant that showed up on Yelp. The diner-style restaurant had a great atmosphere, and we had a nice view of Canal Street. The service was quick and our server was excellent. I ordered the Grits and Grillades, which consisted of slow roasted beef with peppers and onions in a brown gravy served over creamy Gouda cheese grits. It was absolutely delicious and even better than the version I made at home. I will definitely be coming back here on future trips to New Orleans.

input: If I could select less than one star I would. Completely awful. After calling multiple times and no one answering, I finally was able to talk to a very unhelpful employee. He emailed me a specific unit, price, move in date and application. I filled out the paperwork but was unable to find the specific unit he indicated. When trying to call about my problem no one answered for 2 full business days. Then when talking with another very unhelpful employee, she told me that unit was already gone & suggested other units more expensive & not in the move in date discussed. When asking if they would honor the price originally discussed in email correspondence, they would not. Long story shorter, I cancelled my application & just wasted $50. This business only cares about money & does not care about the tenants at all.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Terrible experience. After numerous unanswered calls, I finally spoke to an unhelpful employee who emailed me a specific unit's details. However, I couldn't find that unit and no one responded to my calls for two days. Another unhelpful employee informed me that the unit was no longer available and suggested expensive alternatives. They refused to honor the originally discussed price. In the end, I cancelled my application, wasting $50. This business prioritizes money over tenant satisfaction.

input: Sierra and her sidekick, India, took impeccable care of my family last weekend during a family reunion.  We came to Santa Barbara from all over the world, and Sierra not only took care of purchasing everything we needed ahead of time, but she also thought of things we didn't think of, and went out multiple times to replenish drinks and food we went through.  They were flexible, fun, thorough and all-around fabulous.  I hope I have another event in Santa Barbara in the future, just so I can use JOTSB!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Sierra and her sidekick, India, provided exceptional care during our family reunion in Santa Barbara. They took care of purchasing all our needed supplies in advance and even anticipated our needs by going out multiple times to replenish drinks and food. Sierra and India were flexible, thorough, and a delight to work with. We hope to have another event in Santa Barbara just so we can use JOTSB again.

input: Meh...I wasn't impressed with this spot. Looking past the array of hand written signs and lack of available bagels, the food was ok. I got the pastrami, egg, and cheese. There was hardly any pastrami and the cheese wasn't melted. My wife also had the pleasure of adding spoiled creamer to her coffee. I think we'll just stick with Einstein's or St Pete Bagel.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Not impressed with this spot due to handwritten signs and lack of bagels. The pastrami, egg, and cheese sandwich had very little pastrami and unmelted cheese. Additionally, my wife had spoiled creamer in her coffee. We prefer Einstein's or St Pete Bagel.

input: Very nice employes very resonable price. Excellent homemade salad dressing. Good food, an all around good italian resturant.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Great Italian restaurant with friendly staff, reasonable prices, excellent homemade salad dressing, and delicious food.

input: I love their breakfast burritos. I usually get bacon, egg, cheese and potatoes. The potatoes are  well seasoned and cut small, so you don't end up getting a burrito that is about 95% full of overdone, mushy potatoes. You can actually taste the eggs, bacon and potatoes. Could use a bit more cheese, but that's a minor complaint. Nice selection of salsas at the salsa bar and the staff has always been friendly and welcoming. Very glad that they are located about a mile from my house! Hopefully they will be here for a long time.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love their breakfast burritos with bacon, egg, cheese, and potatoes. The potatoes are well seasoned and cut small, preventing a burrito that is mostly mushy potatoes. The flavors of eggs, bacon, and potatoes are all noticeable. More cheese would be preferred, but it's a minor issue. The salsa bar offers a nice range of salsas, and the staff is friendly and welcoming. I'm grateful that they're located close to my house, and I hope they stay around for a long time.

input:
I'm still new to Tucson, but having tried a large sample of the various pizza places near the U of A, I have to say that this is the best so far. 

In fact I'd say it's the best I've ever had. Better than the places I tried in NYC even. The crust is just magical. The five alarm (which I tried) is the perfect amount of spicy for those of us who crave that extra spicyness in our food. 

If you decide to try it, I doubt you'll be disappointed.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: As a newcomer in Tucson, I've explored numerous pizza places near the U of A. By far, the one I found to be the best is the preferred choice. In fact, it surpasses any pizza place I've tried in NYC. The crust is simply extraordinary. The five alarm variety, which I personally tried, provides the ideal level of spiciness for those who enjoy a little kick in their food. If you give it a shot, I highly doubt you'll be let down.

input: I heard alot about Honey's and how the food is so good here. I chose today my birthday to be my first visit .I read earlier reviews about how crowded it gets and they were not lying but I didn't wait no more than 20 minutes. Now let's get down to the food it was delicious. I had french toast, home fries, sausage and for dessert a slice of Jewish apple cake and it was to die for! I will be back most definitely.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had heard a lot about Honey's and how the food is amazing. I decided to visit for the first time on my birthday. Despite the reviews mentioning the crowd, I only had to wait for 20 minutes. Now, let's talk about the food - it was delicious! I savored the french toast, home fries, sausage, and ended with a heavenly slice of Jewish apple cake. I'm definitely coming back.

input: Tria's employees are very knowledgeable about the selection of beers and wines they offer. This is probably why I look forward to going to Tria. This location has outside seating during the warmer months and is a real treat if you can get a table out there. It always seems to be busy, which is a good thing. I've never had any of the food items at Tria, because the real treat here are the drinks.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Tria's knowledgeable employees, vast beer and wine selection, outdoor seating in warmer months, and bustling atmosphere make it a highly anticipated and beloved spot. While the food may be overlooked, the real highlight lies in the exceptional drinks.

input: Mae's is the best Chinese restaurant on this east side. We tried Mae's due to some rude pricks across the street. Lol! But, luckily things happen for a reason. The environment, the decor, the air inside is so much better to start. The food taste so much more fresher, like it was not frozen or reheated. No greasy/oily after taste. The service is very good,  always right there when you need something, staff is very friendly. My family and I love Mae's and what makes it better are the prices. We're large family and we can do really well with just $60. Lunch specials are awesome! I encourage you to try Mae's.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Mae's is the best Chinese restaurant on the east side. We initially tried it due to some rude individuals across the street, but it turned out to be a fortunate decision. The environment, decor, and air inside are far superior. The food tastes fresher, without any greasy or oily aftertaste, as if it was never frozen or reheated. The service is excellent, with attentive staff always available when needed, and they are very friendly. My family and I adore Mae's, and the prices make it even better. With just $60, our large family can enjoy a satisfying meal. The lunch specials are particularly impressive. I strongly encourage you to give Mae's a try.

input: This place is my absolute fave! The flavors are spot on, they taste exactly the way you imagine, but better! The strawberries & champagne, toasted marshmallow, and cheesecake  are a few of my personal favorites. I moved to Phoenix a few years back and was ecstatic when I found out they opened locations in the valley. This is a Tucson gem that I will continue to visit over and over!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I absolutely love this place! The flavors are incredible and exceed all expectations. Some of my personal favorites include strawberries & champagne, toasted marshmallow, and cheesecake. Luckily, they have opened locations in the valley since I moved to Phoenix a few years ago. It's a true gem in Tucson that I will keep visiting!

input: This location used to be good, several years ago. About 3 years ago it started to go downhill and now it is just terrible. There were 2 people working on a Saturday evening. Nearly all the tables were full and there were people waiting to order and to pay. The sandwich that was made for me was on hard bread, burnt and barely edible. They need to either shape up or ship out.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This location used to be good, but it has steadily declined in quality over the past 3 years and is now terrible. On a recent Saturday evening, only 2 employees were working while the place was packed with nearly all tables occupied and customers waiting in line to order and pay. The sandwich I received was made on hard, burnt bread and barely edible. It's high time they seriously improved or considered closing down.

input:
The girly loves this cemetery for photographing angels and such. Personally, I think she's a little creepy.

On the plus side, it's quiet, no zombies and the witches doing spells took time out to photobomb a bit.

So there's that.

Seriously, a well laid out cemetery and some of the better made stones and angels.

And no zombies. Remember that part.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The girl loves photographing angels at this cemetery, which I find a bit creepy. However, it is a quiet place with no zombies, and even the witches who do spells there took some time to photobomb. Overall, the cemetery is well laid out with beautifully crafted stones and angels. The absence of zombies is definitely worth noting.

input:
On a recent trip to Port Richey, I selected Holiday Inn Express for a couple of reasons.  The main reason was the option of two beds (as I was sharing the room with my brother).  The other reasons were:  price, vicinity to my aunt's home and complementary breakfast. 

My family and I typically stay at the Hyatt Place/House when we're traveling.  However, since it was just my brother and I, I figured we'd give Holiday Inn a shot. 

+  The staff were very friendly and helpful.
+  Free wifi.
+  Breakfast was very good, offering both hot and cold entrees. 

-  Sadly, the beds were WAY TOO soft.  It felt as if the mattresses were past their life expectancy.  As a result, I didn't really sleep well for most of my three nights there.
-  The a/c was hit and miss with the lack of reliable thermostat controls. 

There was a pool and hot tub, but since I didn't utilize either, it wouldn't be fair to rate them.  There also a small gym that I didn't use either. 

All in all, it was just ok.  Hyatt has spoiled me.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
During my recent trip to Port Richey, I chose to stay at the Holiday Inn Express for its advantages over other options. Firstly, the availability of two beds was essential since I shared the room with my brother. Additionally, factors such as the reasonable price, proximity to my aunt's home, and complimentary breakfast influenced my decision. Although our usual choice is the Hyatt Place/House, given it was only my brother and me, we opted for the Holiday Inn this time. 

Positively, the staff at the Holiday Inn Express were friendly and helpful, and they provided free wifi. Moreover, the breakfast options were excellent, offering a variety of hot and cold dishes. 

However, there were a couple of drawbacks. The beds were overly soft, giving the impression of worn-out mattresses, which affected my sleep quality for most of the three nights. Additionally, the air conditioning could be unreliable due to the absence of consistent thermostat controls. 

I did not have the opportunity to use the pool, hot tub, or small gym facilities, so I cannot provide a rating for them. Overall, the stay was satisfactory, but I have become accustomed to the higher standards offered by the Hyatt brand.

input: The staff wasn't too interested in helping customers, instead focused on the TV in the lobby, flirting with each other and just standing around. I found the food to be ok, not great, not terrible. I'll round up from the 1.5 I give them.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The staff was uninterested in assisting customers and spent their time focusing on the TV, flirting with each other, and idly standing around. The food was average, not excellent but not terrible either. I will give them a rounded-up score of 2 out of 5.

input:
The food is excellent. The customer service and quantity over time has continued to go down. I've been going to this place every couple weeks for two years. The portions over time have continued to gradually get smaller and smaller. I commented on this, because my take out dish is now to the point where it is less then half full when I order, when it used to go to the top. When I commented on this I was told I was wrong.  I proceeded to explain my case. I was told if I didn't want to take the food, I didn't have to pay for it. I said ok, and was the berated for not taking the food I ordered. 

Long story short, these people have lost my business. I am not going back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food used to be excellent at this place, but over time, the customer service and portion sizes have consistently decreased. Despite going there every couple of weeks for two years, the portions have gradually become smaller and my takeout dish is now less than half full. When I commented on this, the staff denied it and I had to explain my case. They told me I didn't have to pay if I didn't want the food, but then berated me for not taking it. As a result, I have decided to no longer patronize this establishment.

input: Food was great. Staff was nice, friendly and helpful with menu suggestions. The Happy Hour is a good deal and the house margaritas tasted better than many other restaurants I've visited. I had the chicken poblano which was great. My friend enjoyed his enchiladas and they allowed him to have 3 different types on one plate.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food was great, and the staff was nice, friendly, and helpful with menu suggestions. The Happy Hour is a good deal, and the house margaritas tasted better than many other restaurants I've been to. The chicken poblano dish I had was excellent. Additionally, my friend enjoyed his enchiladas, and they even allowed him to have three different types on one plate.

input: Try the salted caramel chocolate cake. It was the best we ever had. I also tried the Apple Brown Betty  - awesome. Good beer selection.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Highly recommend trying the salted caramel chocolate cake, it's the best we've ever had. Also, the Apple Brown Betty is amazing. They have a good beer selection too.

input:
A laid back bar for the college crowd. Cheap drinks.  They have projectors so u can watch the big game that day. However the screen needs to be two feet wider so the picture doesn't go off into the wall.

I came here during the day so it was really spacious, but I can only imagine how it is at night.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Laid back college bar with cheap drinks and projectors for watching games, though screen size should be increased by two feet to avoid wall cutoff. Spacious during the day, likely even better at night.

input: Terrible service. Called in an order for pick up and completely butchered my order. I asked for a half sausage half cheese pizza and felt like he had no clue what i was saying as i had to constantly repeat myself. i had my boyfriend call back to make sure the order was right and he repeated back the order that i ordered half sausage half BEEF??? So after we corrected him and picked up or pizza, we got back and opened it up and it was ALL SAUSAGE. This is the second time in the past month i have had terrible service. The first time i got there for pickup and they had completely forgotten to put my order in. Terrible.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Extremely poor service. Called in an order for pick up and the staff completely messed up my order. Despite clearly requesting a half sausage half cheese pizza, they seemed clueless and I had to repeat myself multiple times. I even had to have my boyfriend call back to confirm the order, and they still got it wrong by substituting sausage with beef. When we picked up the pizza, it turned out to be entirely sausage, not what we wanted at all. This is the second time within the past month that I have had such a terrible experience with their service. The first time, they forgot to place my order altogether when I arrived for pick up. Overall, absolutely awful.

input:
do not eat here. my husband, two friends and i went out for restaurant week to marmont steakhouse on saturday, january 26, 2013; our experience was horrific.  the four of us ordered the crab bisque soup for our first course, it was cold and we sent it back to be reheated.  my second course was the calamari it was bland, fried too hard and rubbery.  finally two ppl from our party ordered the lobster ravioli for an entree.  it was not lobster ravioli but beef. i asked our waiter and one other waiter to please double check with the chef because this is not lobster, i expressed that i have not eaten beef or pork since 1994, and that it would make me ill. they both came back separately and argued that it was in fact lobster. another party of maybe 6 ppl ordered the lobster ravioli, they had the same problem and sent their dishes back to the kitchen too.  the server finally came over after i'd eaten two of the ravioli to apologize for the kitchens error and telling us that was in fact beef. 
i have been in the bathroom all day with diarrhea from the beef ravioli! the staff was very nonchalant about it and offered an insincere apology.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Avoid this restaurant called Marmont Steakhouse at all costs. Our visit on January 26, 2013 during restaurant week was a terrible experience. The crab bisque soup we ordered as our first course was served cold and had to be sent back. The calamari for my second course was tasteless, over-fried, and rubbery. To make matters worse, two people in our group ordered lobster ravioli for their entree but were served beef instead. Despite repeatedly informing the waiter and another staff member about the mistake, they insisted it was lobster. Another table also had the same issue and had to send their dishes back. It was only after I had already eaten two ravioli that the server finally admitted the mistake and apologized. Since then, I have been suffering from diarrhea due to consuming the beef ravioli. The staff showed a lack of concern and their apology felt insincere.

input: It simply does not get any better than Tako for sushi. Everything is fresh & delicious. The private rooms are so fun for a festive night out, it's BYO & when my girls get together we enjoy the feast & atmosphere! Some personal favorites are the jalapeño yellowtail(a must!!), kani salad, bird's nest roll & the naruto (served in cucumber instead of rice. Honestly, you can't go wrong when ordering. And so reasonable!! I rarely spend over $35 including tip when we go, and we do not hold back at all when ordering. Highly, highly recommend Tako!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Tako is the ultimate sushi spot. The fresh and delicious food combined with their fun private rooms make for a fantastic evening out. It's BYO, which adds to the festive atmosphere. Must-try items include the jalapeno yellowtail, kani salad, bird's nest roll, and the naruto, served in cucumber instead of rice. Ordering is foolproof, and the prices are reasonable. Even with a generous order, you'll rarely spend over $35 including tip. Tako comes highly recommended - don't miss out!

input: Very good local ice cream. Expresso chip. Moose tracks. Graham Slam are all custom made flavors.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Excellent homemade ice cream flavors include espresso chip, moose tracks, and graham slam.

input:
My hubbie and I have been taking our trucks here for a few years and can't complain. Every Wednesday is ladies day, so you get a discount on any of their wash options. (Firemen also get a discount on Mondays) . This isn't a hand-wash, so it's not perfect  but a good $5 carwash if your "baby" needs a quick bath.

They do run a special every now and then on auto detail packages 2 for 1. My husband and I always buy when they're running this special, since they have always done a nice job.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We have been bringing our trucks here for years and have no complaints. On Wednesdays, ladies receive a discount on all wash options, and on Mondays, firemen get a discount too. Although it is not a hand-wash, it is a decent $5 carwash for a quick bath for your vehicle. They also occasionally offer a special on auto detail packages, where you can get 2 for 1. We always take advantage of this offer because they consistently do a great job.

input:
Everything about this place is average. The food is just ok, the service sort of depends on your luck - sometimes good sometimes not so good. 

Had the drunken noodles once and Thai green curry once. Both were average.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is average in every aspect. The food, including the drunken noodles and Thai green curry, is just okay. The service may vary depending on luck - sometimes good, sometimes not so good.

input:
This is a milestone review for me on Yelp.  I had been struggling with which one to chhose.  I decidede to make it Redemption.  This was seriously one of the best meals of my ENTIRE life.  

This review was from about 2 months ago.  Sorry it is a little dated.  Such as life.  

The setting is an old church.  It is really a beautiful surrounding for a restaurant.  Although I am an old church architecture nerd.  It was really cool to look around.   

The service was incredible.  I was hear as part of a group of 7 other characters, several were part of the NOLA restaurant scene.  We wanted a good time with the meal and they provided it!   

Paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian.  I was not fortunate enough to have enjoyed the original.  I can not comment on the faithfulness to the founders recipe.  I can say this there is no highe calling for a soft shell crab than to be cold smoked and fried in preparation for this dish.  On to your 77 virgins and mecca for you!  But I experienced heaven eating this.  

Seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's - This was superlative.  Again did not try the original, but the mirliton and seafood stuffing was heavenly, and more importantly improved the taste of the fresh flounder rather than competing for the spot light!   

The combination was quite possibly one of the 10 best meals of my life.  If you have been here, you should try it!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This Yelp milestone review is from about 2 months ago at Redemption, a beautiful restaurant set in an old church. As an old church architecture nerd, I found the setting really cool. The service was incredible, especially considering we were a group of 7 with some members from the NOLA restaurant scene. Now on to the food - the paneed smoked soft shell crab a la Christian was heavenly. While I can't compare it to the original, the cold smoked and fried preparation elevated the dish to new heights. The seafood stuffed filet of fish a la Christian's was also superb, with the mirliton and seafood stuffing enhancing the flounder. Overall, this meal ranks among the top 10 best I've ever had. If you haven't been here, you should definitely give it a try!

input:
I love this place. It's just down the street from me so I'm there probably every other week... don't judge me! They rotate their flavors regularly and if at first you don't see a topping you'd like be sure and ask if they have it because they keep some under the counter!

This place also busts out some pretty intense EDM music over their sound system, which is somewhat bizarre but wholly awesome!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I love this place nearby. I visit every other week as they rotate flavors regularly. If you don't see a topping you want, ask because they keep some under the counter. They play intense EDM music, which is bizarre but awesome!

input:
Amazing. We had; Steak Tartare, Caribbean Seafood Pepper Pot and the Curried Goat. Everything was really wonderful. Tartare maybe the best i've had. The goat with the sweet curry and gnocchi was very different and I loved it. I had a bite of the lime cheesecake and it was top notch, too. 

No drinks, because it's 2 days after Mardi Gras and I'm still in recovery mode. The service was among the best I've had in this town, which is know for it's hospitality industry. Great great great!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We had an amazing dining experience. The Steak Tartare, Caribbean Seafood Pepper Pot, and Curried Goat were all wonderful. The Tartare was possibly the best I've ever had. The goat with sweet curry and gnocchi was deliciously unique, and I loved it. The lime cheesecake was also top notch. We didn't have any drinks as it was 2 days after Mardi Gras and we were still recovering. The service was exceptional, among the best in town, known for its hospitality industry. Overall, a great experience.

input:
I went here on a Wednesday night and, though it wasn't busy, there were no open tables without a reservation,  except the tall tables in the bar area. It still seemed to be a very quiet place anyway. 

The location is not attractive, the street is dark and mostly empty at night, but the inside is stylish in a masculine, refined sort of way; dark wood, low light, maps on the walls and prints of watercolors depicting old Missouri scenes. It was a great place for a quiet, intimate dinner. They've got a couple of TVs up above the bar. 

They seemed very well staffed, as if each table had its own server. 

The menu is one page but very intriguing, I had so many questions for our server about "what is this?" and "what is that?" and he was totally nice and knowledgeable about the menu items. He seemed nervous and unsure at first, but he was friendly and made sure to check on us frequently. 

We decided to split 3 small plates and a side dish between the two of us and, honestly, it was a little too much food for just two people. Perhaps we don't have hearty enough appetites.

Their menu is so varied and interesting, it's really all over the map in terms of seasonings and ethnic origins but the main focus seems to be rustic and warming - at least at this time of year. I have a feeling they may change it up from time to time. I'm sure you'll get things here you won't find anywhere else. The prices are very reasonable, considering the planning and good execution of the food. You'd certainly find more expensive, and less original places in Clayton and down town. 

We ordered the smoked trout, the venison hot dogs, the mini monte cristo sandwiches, and the french fries. 

The venison hot dogs and the smoked trout were fantastic and interesting. The french fries were very well made, and the dipping sauces delicious. I was so impressed with these that I was then a bit underwhelmed by the mini monte cristos. Since everything else there seemed to have a unique spin on it, I expected them to do something original here as well, but they were just like any monte cristo you might have. They were very tasty of course, but nothing new. 

With the food plus two draft beers, our total was $52.05 before tip and we were stuffed and satisfied. I applaud them!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I visited this place on a quiet Wednesday night and all tables were reserved except for the tall ones in the bar area. The interior was stylish with dark wood, low lighting, and attractive watercolor prints on the walls. The staff was attentive, and the menu was intriguing with a variety of dishes from different cuisines. We split three small plates and a side dish, which turned out to be more than enough food for two people. The smoked trout and venison hot dogs were fantastic, but the mini monte cristo sandwiches were underwhelming compared to the other dishes. The prices were reasonable considering the quality of the food. Overall, the experience was satisfying and our total bill, including two draft beers, was $52.05.

input: "High Score!"...unfortunately I wasn't playing a video game with my friends, but rather wracked up the highest weight for my frozen yogurt. Why did is "win" this completely made up competition? Because this place is THAT good. Seriously, everything tastes great and even the fat-free options still feel like I'm splurging on my constant being-a-girl diet. The location is great if you're out an about on South Street and need something sweet. :)
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I got the highest weight for my frozen yogurt at a great place on South Street. Everything tastes amazing, including the fat-free options. It's perfect for satisfying my sweet cravings while being out and about.

input: I went last night with a few friends and let me say I was impressed, not necessarily with the quality of the food (nothing wrong with it by any means) or the decor, but the servers: how they don't kill every 4th customer is beyond me. I heard tables on both sides of us giving the most ridiculous of complaints to our/their server. Both tables were demanding as hell and already said loudly to eachother that they weren't tipping because of x, y and z reasons, and then were dumbfounded that there's a gratuity on their bill (it says it in the menu, anything over $50) their server, smaller girl so with purple hair, carried upwards of 4 plates at once, explained the menu perfectly and had an eagle eye for every table in her section and dealt with ridiculous complaints like a true professional. Thumbs up and five stars to the staff, customers, learn how to be basic humans, or stay home.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I went out last night with some friends and I have to say, I was impressed. Not so much with the food or decor, but definitely with the servers. It amazes me how they manage to handle difficult customers without losing their cool. We had tables on both sides of us who were incredibly demanding and complained about the smallest things. They even made it clear that they weren't going to tip. It was surprising to see them act surprised when the bill included a gratuity charge (which is clearly stated on the menu for bills over $50). Our server, a small girl with purple hair, handled everything flawlessly. She carried multiple plates at once, explained the menu perfectly, and kept a close eye on every table in her section. She dealt with ridiculous complaints like a true professional. I give a big thumbs up and five stars to the staff. As for the customers, they need to learn some basic decency or just stay home.

input:
I did not end up purchasing a vehicle here, but the shopping experience was straight-forward and better than most other dealerships. 

I found that their list prices were fair and competitive, as well as the certification and warranties on used vehicles - I just chose a different car make/model than I shopped for at Hallmark. The salesman and sales manager were nice and were not pushy. I was able to quickly get attention and test drive the car I wanted to check out. 

Had I liked the car better than what I was comparing it to, I would have likely bought from them. Based on some pretty terrible experiences at other places, I would recommend trying this dealership if you are looking to buy locally.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Though I didn't purchase a vehicle here, the shopping experience at this dealership was straightforward and better than most others. The list prices were fair and competitive, and they offered good certification and warranties for used vehicles. The salesman and sales manager were nice and not pushy. I quickly received attention and had the opportunity to test drive the car I wanted. While I ultimately chose a different make/model, I would have likely bought from them if I preferred their car. Based on my negative experiences elsewhere, I recommend giving this dealership a try if you're looking to buy locally.

input: Gross, just gross. I ordered the white meat fried chicken with Mac and cheese and garlic mashed potatoes as my sides. Chicken was slimy and salty. Sides were both cold and practically flavorless. Not to mention service was strange. Server busted out laughing while I was giving my order. It made me uncomfortable as if he was laughing at us. I didn't understand. Will not be back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Ordered white meat fried chicken with Mac and cheese and garlic mashed potatoes as sides. Chicken was slimy and salty, sides were cold and flavorless. Service was strange with server laughing during order, making us uncomfortable. Won't return.

input: Delicious! We had the warm and cold lobster rolls and both were great.  Bread was amazing too!  A little on the expensive side but you get what you pay for and it was quality food.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The warm and cold lobster rolls were delicious, and the bread was amazing too. Though the prices were a bit high, the quality of food justified it.

input:
The Habit Burger is a straight up legit burger place.  It's always been a toss up for me between in n out and habit burger.  I got me a double char and choco shake at the goleta habit and it was as usual, delicious.

The onion rings are very good also.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The Habit Burger is an excellent burger place, always competing with In-N-Out for my preference. I recently tried the double char and choco shake at the Goleta location and, as expected, it was delicious. Additionally, their onion rings are also very good.

input: My husband and I practically live here, and have through the past 8 years or so.  They have great food, prepared fast, great drink specials.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We have practically lived here with my husband for the past 8 years enjoying their great food, fast service, and amazing drink specials.

input:
It is typical Broad Ripple charming spot. Small, trendy and bustling with activity. They do not take reservations. Which is somewhat annoying when you are traveling from another part of town. Whatever, we just had to arrange to arrive earlier than we would have liked to hopefully secure a table, which we did. When we arrived it was quiet and only several tables had guests seated. As our dinner progressed it became more crowded until every seat was filled. Nice lively scene except then you can not hear squat! It made dinner conversation difficult. Boo!!!! I think this could be an easy fix for them. 

Meal/Drinks:  The cocktails were creative and tasted wonderful. Our servers suggestions were pretty spot on as we enjoyed most of her suggestions. 

The guacamole was very good with the exception of the fact that my friend has a nut allergy and we asked to have them left off and of coarse they arrived with them on! They really weren't necessary in my opinion either as I don't think they add much to the dish. The reason I wanted to try this restaurant- The Harvest salad! We all split this as well and it was good. The combination of fruit and root vegetables was delish! The figs were so good and the herbed goat cheese mouse was a highlight on this plate!

Two of us ordered the Veracruz Trigger fish and the other ordered the Serrano Scallops and all of it was wonderful. The white sweet mashed potatoes were interesting! I am glad we tried them. The Veracruz sauce was wonderful and full of flavor. It was a lot of food though. Had we known we would have probably skipped one of the first course selections or split an entree. That'a ok though- lunch for today :)

We also tried the Tostones and Stewed Black Beans. Beans were very good, full of flavor! Tostones seemed very dry but maybe that is what they are supposed to be- this is the first time I have had them. BUT, dipped in the Stewed Black Beans they tasted great!

We passed on dessert as they had no gluten free, dairy free options. Delicia offers many options for restricted diets, which we loved. Just no dessert, which is probably better anyway-we were so full! 

Go, you will not be disappointed. Just go before 7pm on a Friday night to ensure a table.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Broad Ripple is a trendy and bustling spot, but they don't take reservations, which can be a hassle. We arrived early to secure a table and the place gradually filled up, making it difficult to have conversations. The cocktails were creative and delicious, and the server's suggestions were great. The guacamole was good, but they included nuts despite our request to leave them out. The Harvest salad with fruit and root vegetables was tasty, especially the figs and herbed goat cheese. The Veracruz Trigger fish and Serrano Scallops were both wonderful, accompanied by interesting mashed sweet potatoes. The Tostones were a bit dry, but they tasted great when dipped in the Stewed Black Beans. Despite no gluten-free, dairy-free dessert options, Delicia offers plenty of choices for restricted diets. Overall, it's recommended to go before 7 pm on a Friday night to secure a table and enjoy a satisfying meal.

input:
This makes my 6th or 7th time to Jackson's in the last 2 years and I thought that after tonight's visit they deserved a review. 

I had the panini Reuben.  Panini was amazing. Great use of garlic. Loved the cut of the meat. Not stringy but nicely chinked in thin slices. Cheese was well melted throughout the mix of kraut and meat. Rye Bread was wonderful. Would love to have it as a staple in my house. 

Salad came out same time as sandwich which was not good.

Presentation was a little sloppy. 

Like every other place I have had a panini (except Panera where they do it right), the sandwich was served directly on a plate. Why don't they serve on a napkin? Particularly when they bring the salad out at the same time as the sandwich?  If the sandwich sits for more than a few moments, the bread gets soggy from the steam.  Nothing serious, but for the price, which is a little high, it seems lacking.  While the price is a little high, i think it is justified considering the food and drink quality. 

They have a great selection of wines and beers that are likely to fit any palette.  

Wait staff have always been friendly. But you can tell this is a place where people are expected to hustle. Sometimes short or even distracted the service can be lacking. 

The second time I visited was during a medium lunch rush and the wait time was 15 min to get drinks. My trip tonight it was about 8 min. For a sat night this is not bad. But not great either. My bartenders were awesome and never left me wanting (except for getting my salad with the main course).

Overall a good experience and I will be back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I've been to Jackson's around 6 or 7 times in the past 2 years and I wanted to give them a review after tonight's visit. The panini Reuben I had was amazing, with a great use of garlic and a nicely cut meat that wasn't stringy. The melted cheese throughout the mix of kraut and meat was delicious, and the rye bread was wonderful. However, the salad came out at the same time as the sandwich, which was not good. The presentation was a little sloppy, as the sandwich was served directly on a plate instead of a napkin. This caused the bread to get soggy if it sat for too long. While the price is a bit high, I think it's justified considering the quality of the food and drinks. They have a great selection of wines and beers to choose from. The wait staff have always been friendly, but sometimes their service can be lacking due to being short or distracted. The wait time for drinks during my visits ranged from 15 minutes during a medium lunch rush to 8 minutes on a Saturday night. Overall, it was a good experience and I'll definitely be back.

input:
I went there for a pedicure and gel manicure.  It was my first time and the reviews was what enticed me. I loved loved Young, who did my pedicure.  She was very friendly and has a very positive attitude.  She took her time with my pedicure and was very thorough with the massaging (which was the best part). 

Unfortunately Young didn't do my manicure.   I had a gel manicure that needed to be soaked off.  The owner did my nails.  She first scraped my nails with the cuticle pusher, but when it wasn't coming off fast enough, she used the drill.  I was really worried as I didn't want my nails to be thin.  But I just let her do her thing.  I'm usually not picky so when she was working on my nails I didn't watch what she was doing until I realized after close examination she didn't fully take the old gel polish off.  
Not only that, the polish didn't go on smoothly, there's are noticeable bumps on my nail bed and the sides of my nails weren't even fully covered.  

I am so disappointed.  I love Young, but I don't know if I'll be going back due to my experience with my gel manicure.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Went for a pedicure and gel manicure based on positive reviews. Loved Young, who did my pedicure. She was friendly, took her time, and gave a thorough massage. However, the owner did my gel manicure and didn't fully remove the old gel polish. Nails were scraped and drilled, leaving bumps and uneven coverage. Disappointed and unsure about returning due to the gel manicure experience.

input: I just had the trio that was an appetizer that was amazing. Also I try there pizza it all really good.

input: This place is a hidden gem on the Westside of Tucson. Great food at a reasonable price. I highly recommend the the Indian taco and their sweet fry bread in delicious. They also have daily specials like my favorite $1 tacos on Tuesday and Fridays. I eat here at least once a week.

input: They don't just have great cookies, cupcakes, and puddings! input: Skip the fancy desert after dinner to go here, it's an excuse to walk around Broadway.  The homemade ice cream is really good.  Cake Mix is my favorite.   Great place to top off a date.

input: So happy I found a bomb local sushi place!! Always ignored this shop going to domino's but I'm so glad I popped in. Will be coming here more than I should from now on. input: The best thai food I've tried in the area. I live about 30min away and wish I lived closer. The red curry and the pad thai and the chicken satay with peanut sauce is so so good! Lunch specials are great!

input: I took my family and my daughter today for the very first time. There was a lot of things to do for my daughter and she loved it! However, I was disappointed by the cleanliness of the place. Despite the high admission price, there was no staff seen cleaning throughout the day, electrical cords were accessible to kids, and dust was everywhere. input: I was a walk in and absolutely loved the clean location and the friendly staff. Tammy did an amazing job on my eyebrows and being a first time guest the service was free! They also have great packages for all kinds of waxing services. Will definitely be back!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I loved the clean location and friendly staff at this salon. Tammy did an amazing job on my eyebrows, and as a first time guest, the service was free! They also offer great packages for all types of waxing services. I will definitely return.

input: There is nothing like the other pics showed!!! I never give out review on Yelp, but I had to comment on this restaurant! input:

input:
This is a cool place.  I wonder how many people know that an Ouzaria is?  The ambience here is definitely upbeat - I'd rate it a great place for a group or first date.  They have a couple of semi-secluded tables in the back room that keeps it from getting too loud, but it's not a quiet romantic place.  

We brought my Mother-in-Law, who enjoys good food as long as it's not too weird.  I guess my wife is about the same, now that I think about it.  We tried three tapas plates; a three-cheese sampler, featuring feta, goat cheese and kasseri cheese, greek meatballs and pan-seared scallops.  We liked all three of these dishes.  The scallops were especially good - big and tender.   For tapas, they were pretty big portions, so keep this in mind.  The waitress suggested ordering one thing at a time, but we didn't heed her advice and ordered it all up front.   Two at a time would probably be a good idea.  Along with the tapas, we ordered a traditional Greek salad, which ended up being the lone clunker, surprisingly.  We just didn't like the dressing - too sweet for our tastes.  The gyro meat was fine, though, so maybe we'll just get a gyro next time.   One more thing:  The Spanish granacha (can't remember the label) was excellent for just $6 and a nice pour. 

Okay, now for the belly dancer:  She was cute and a good dancer, but I think this is just something that requires more alcohol on my part.  We did have a few laughs about it, though.  I opted not to get a dollar out to stuff in her skirt or whatever.   Fun but a little awkward. 

I've been to a few other Greek places in town that had better food, but for a night out, Momo's is definitely the choice.  We'll be back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This cool place known as Momo's is an Ouzaria. The ambience is upbeat, making it a great choice for a group or a first date. While it's not quiet or romantic, it does have semi-secluded tables in the back room to keep the noise level in check. We brought my Mother-in-Law and ordered three tapas plates: a three-cheese sampler, Greek meatballs, and pan-seared scallops. All three dishes were enjoyed, with the scallops being particularly impressive. The tapas portions were quite large, and it's recommended to order two at a time. The traditional Greek salad was disappointing due to the sweet dressing, but the gyro meat was fine. The Spanish granacha wine was excellent and reasonably priced at $6. The belly dancer was cute and danced well, but it may require more alcohol to fully appreciate. Overall, although there are better Greek places for food, Momo's is our choice for a fun night out. We plan to return.

input: I haven't been here for at least three years and it's due to the service. Everytime I went to this store, just to look mostly, the staff were stuck up and one girl was even telling me how to hold a book so I don't break the binding. She even told me I have to pay for it if I hold it wrong. It was so odd that I just left and never went back. When I was in highschool, in the late 90's, this store was great but being grown up now I expect better service. Although they may have changed, after more than 10 visits with consistently poor service, I am hesitant to give them another chance.

input: You will have to stand in line, you will have to squeeze onto a wooden bench with a lot of strangers, you will not have heat or a/c and .... it is worth it. input: Can't say I would rush back as the ambiance wasn't exactly four star or higher. I'm not saying if I'm in the area and craving some sushi I wouldn't stop again. So prepare yourself for a slightly beaten up space but with pleasant help and ok food.

input: I'm so impressed with this coffee shop. Coming from Sacramento, my husband and I know good coffee. This place is such a gem, I wish there was something like this back in Sac! Anyways, this is my go-to Reno coffee shop for sure. Their Matcha lattes are so good. Sigh.

input: I just recently moved to Idaho and today I went to Chipotle and she comped me one meal (out of 3) and it made my week let alone my day lol. She was so nice to start with and had the best customer service! She definitely stood out in the staff, her name was Taylor. She's absolutely awesome!
