The ham omelet with home fries and toast arrive a few minutes later, worth waiting for. Done just right and kept me filled for hours. A friendly family restaurant where you feel welcome and appreciated, just north of Gulfport.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Arrived mid-morning after the early rush. Two tables were full, each with three people. The family just walked in before me, so they were attended to first. However, I was promptly welcomed and offered the breakfast menu and coffee. The cup was continuously refilled during my visit. The radio played golden oldies from the 70s, my preferred genre. A delicious ham omelet with home fries and toast arrived shortly and kept me satisfied for hours. Overall, it is a friendly family restaurant just north of Gulfport where you feel appreciated and welcome.

input: This place is so lovely. It has everything!! Amazing wine selection, hookah's, Lebanese food which I think is the best in the city.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place is perfect! It offers an incredible wine selection, hookah options, and undoubtedly the finest Lebanese cuisine in the city.

input: This was recommended by a colleague who is local in the area. A group of us from work decided to go and give it a try.  As soon as we sat down, Chris, took care of us.  He was patient, understanding and extremely knowledgeable of the menu.  Well, our entire party enjoyed every part of the evening while at Red Mess!  From the chips & salsa to the drinks to each of our entrees ... just absolutely DELICIOUS!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Recommended by a local colleague, a group of us from work tried out Red Mess. Chris provided excellent service, being patient, understanding, and knowledgeable about the menu. We all had a fantastic evening, enjoying everything from the chips & salsa to the drinks and entrees, which were absolutely delicious.

input: This is my 3rd time and 3rd location at a Brick House across the country. This is by far one of the few chain restaurants I will regularly and happily eat at. The food is very unique and every selection is a good choice. This particular location I received better than average service. Will come back when back in town.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I've been to this Brick House location for the third time, and it's in a different city from the previous times. Despite being a chain restaurant, it's one of the few that I genuinely enjoy eating at. The food is exceptional and every dish on the menu is a reliable option. During this visit, the service was better than what I usually experience. I will definitely return to this location whenever I'm back in town.

input: So... This place is the sh*t. By far the classiest spot on the block, Siam is nudging STL standards up and up. The sashimi:  top grade. The outdoor patio: perfect to enjoy a beer/conversation off the dance floor. The music: something for everyone -- and the last couple nights I've been, the guest dj's we're KILLING some deep house grooves that rival NYC and Miami.  The best thing, though, may be the crowd: a solid mix that don't need labels, don't want pretense, just want a solid, quality night out.  F*ck yeah, Siam!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Siam is an exceptional place. It is the classiest spot in town, gradually elevating the standards of STL. The sashimi is top grade and the outdoor patio provides a perfect setting for relaxed conversation with a beer. The music caters to everyone's taste, with recent guest DJs playing amazing deep house grooves that can rival those in NYC and Miami. However, the best part about Siam is its diverse and unpretentious crowd who simply want to have a great night out. Siam truly deserves praise.

input:
Worn down signs intrigue me.  I had biked passed 16th Street Seafood a ton of times, always wondering what was going on inside.  Now I know the answer, and the answer is- not much. At least in terms of decor. There is a gumball machine, 2 empty candy machines, plus a counter to order at and that's pretty much it. Also absent was the plethora of seafood over ice you would hope to see at a place specializing in seafood. There were some frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs- but not else. Still, I threw caution to the winds of Tasker Street and put in an order.

I didn't want to go for fried seafood, so the sandwiches and platters were out.

I got a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce ($9.50). Mussels are one of those things I like making at home, but it is way too hot for that right now. . My main complaint is that the order came with an unacceptable amount of closed shells - 9!   It was still a good sized order with a big piece of bread to dip in the unexpectedly spicy, broth. As the place is to-go only- they know how to wrap up messy seafood orders, nothing was spilled.

Remember when I said I didn't want anything fried, well that's not ever actually true. So I ended up sneaking in 2 fried shrimps. Not bad, but not worth $1.25 each.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
The worn down 16th Street Seafood caught my attention, always making me curious about what was inside. However, upon visiting, I found the decor lacking, with only a gumball machine, 2 empty candy machines, and a counter to order from. Disappointingly, the seafood offerings were limited, with frozen crab cakes, breaded fish fillets, clams, and crabs being the only options. Despite this, I took a risk and placed an order.

Avoiding fried seafood, I opted for a large order of mussels in butter and garlic sauce ($9.50). Although I enjoy making mussels at home, the heat made it impractical. Unfortunately, the order contained an unacceptable number of closed shells - a total of 9. Nevertheless, the serving was generous, accompanied by a large piece of bread to dip in the unexpectedly spicy broth. Since the place only offers takeout, they expertly wrapped the messy seafood order without any spills.

While I initially claimed to not want anything fried, I couldn't resist and snuck in 2 fried shrimps. They were decent, but not worth the price of $1.25 each.

input:
we had a groupon and so we went - great lobsters (although they were out of a few sizes this evening) but they were delicious and our waitress Jessica was very attending and nice - made some good suggestions.

not fancy but good lobster.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We used a Groupon and decided to give it a try. The lobster options were limited, but still delicious. Our waitress, Jessica, was attentive and friendly, and even provided us with great recommendations. Overall, it wasn't fancy, but the lobster was good.

input: Great little upscale but not overpriced cafe. Lots of options, but needs a lox bagel sandwich. :) One of my preferred places to lunch with someone.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Great, upscale cafe with reasonable prices. Offers a variety of options, but could benefit from adding a lox bagel sandwich. One of my favorite places for lunch with someone.

input:
Animo juice is the best find in Haddonfield (after the Hadrosaurus, of course!)

I stop at Animo every time I go to Jersey to visit my family; or do I visit my family every time I stop at Animo?  Debatable.

Animo started with juice.  Not frozen juices with sorbet & yogurt added.  Real juice.  

Their menu has expanded & they now call themselves "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar!"  The burrito menu features 10 burritos, all under $10, f my favorite the "Haight & Ashbury" is stuffed with rice, beans, meat/roasted veggies, cheese, lettuce, tomato, guacamole & sour cream.

Not that hungry, have a 'petito', a small version of the burrito, averaging $5.  Porky & Petunia - the name is as cute as the petito is yummy:  shredded lettuce, pulled pork & pineapple salsa.  

A breakfast petito & Animo MD juice destroy any hangover.  The MD is juiced greens, carrot, orange, apple, kiwi, banana & spirolina.   My BF loves the Chilly Palmer:  Acai, apple, banana, yogurt & flax seed.  

For a happy belly add or substitute the perfectly cooked quinoa to any dish.  The Border Salad is a perfect example: lettuce, guac, pico de gallo, cheese, tortilla chips, cilantro lime vin, & sub quinoa for meat.   

Fiber-full signature juices, frozen whipped bananas, sliced fresh wheat grass (cheaper than Jameson!) & yogurt/granola bowls!  

The city's juice bars have something to learn from Animo.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Animo juice in Haddonfield is a must-try. They are known for their real juice, not frozen ones. They have expanded their menu and now call themselves "Animo Juice & Burrito Bar," offering 10 affordable burritos under $10. They also have smaller versions called 'petitos' for those who are not very hungry. Their breakfast petitos and Animo MD juice are perfect for curing hangovers. They offer a variety of signature juices, including fiber-full ones, as well as frozen whipped bananas, wheat grass, and yogurt/granola bowls. Animo sets a great example for other juice bars in the city.

input: Had a very memorable birthday in SB and was so happy to have Wine Edventures be my gift! Sean picked us up Saturday morning and was super friendly (funny, too). It was just my husband and I along with a group of 10 - who happened to be all guys, having a bachelor party! Haha, so that was pretty funny. We stopped at 3 wineries and 1 brewery. Sean explained where we were as we were driving around and also gave us lessons at the tastings. He provided us with bottled water and souvenir wine glasses. We had lunch at the 2nd vineyard of the day, which was very good - choice of sandwich and a pasta salad side with chips and a cookie (the cookies are awesome). It was a fun day and I'd highly recommend this adventure to anyone looking for a fun day in the SB area.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I had a fantastic birthday in Santa Barbara with Wine Edventures as my gift. Sean, our friendly and funny guide, picked us up in the morning. It was just my husband and me, along with a group of 10 guys on a bachelor party, which made for a amusing experience. We visited 3 wineries and 1 brewery, with Sean providing explanations and tastings throughout the trip. He also gave us bottled water and souvenir wine glasses. Lunch at the second vineyard was delicious, with a choice of sandwich, pasta salad, chips, and the amazing cookies. Overall, it was a fun day and I highly recommend this adventure for anyone seeking a great time in the Santa Barbara area.

input:
This is my favorite in Delaware.  The menu is simple and perfectly executed.  Rolls are reasonably priced, artfully made and are PACKED with fish!  I do believe they use flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, but the color, texture, taste and smell are perfect.  Easily the best spicy tuna I have ever had.  I think the secret is the kewpie mayo along w/ the right amount of sriracha and sichimi powder.  Frankly, I can't get enough of this place and have at times, eaten it every day for lunch for weeks.  I've gone as far as to pick it up for dinner AFTER having had it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been great!

The Sushiman, YC Park is amazing to watch.  I've seen him skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife in no time flat, in a single ribbon and then continue to shave it into a nori thin sheet for his tuna naruto roll roll.  The temaki are as big as a carnival iced cream cone.  You can barely finish one of them, there is so much fish in there.  The nigiri are beautiful.  Uniform pieces of fresh fish, perfectly perched on the best sushi rice I've ever had (just the right amount of vinegar and sugar).

Skip the newly opened Kooma.  Save Mikimotos for a night out, but go to Tokyo for lunch!  The owners are lovely, so support them in this tough economy.  If you must eat sushi, eat it here!

Why not 5 stars?  I have to save it for places that serve the local fresh fish, plucked out of the water that morning.  Let me know if you find a place that does!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
Tokyo in Delaware is my absolute favorite sushi spot. Their menu is simple yet perfectly executed. The rolls are reasonably priced, expertly made, and packed with generous amounts of fish. Despite potentially using flash-frozen sashimi grade fish, the color, texture, taste, and smell are absolutely perfect. Their spicy tuna roll stands out as the best I've ever had, thanks to the combination of kewpie mayo, sriracha, and sichimi powder. I am completely addicted to this place, often having it for lunch every day for weeks and sometimes even picking it up for dinner after having it for lunch. Their introduction of short-grain brown sushi rice has been a fantastic addition.

Watching the Sushiman, YC Park, is an incredible experience. I've witnessed him effortlessly skin a cucumber with a sword-like sushi knife, transforming it into a nori thin sheet for his tuna naruto roll. The temaki rolls are as big as a carnival ice cream cone, and the amount of fish inside is overwhelming. The nigiri pieces are beautifully prepared with fresh fish delicately placed on the best sushi rice I've ever tasted.

While I highly recommend Tokyo for lunch, I suggest skipping the newly opened Kooma and saving Mikimotos for a special night out. Supporting Tokyo's owners in this challenging economy is worthwhile due to their hospitality. However, I reserve my five-star rating for places that serve locally caught fish, freshly plucked out of the water that very morning. Please let me know if you discover such a place!

input: So I'm super confused as to why everyone rags on this place. They're super nice, quick, and cheap.  People have complained about their chicken fingers being dry but I have no clue what they're talking about. They're great and their honey mustard is delicious. I've had salads from there too and they give you lots of veggies which I love. Their fries are delish as well and I love that they give you cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. All and all, I love that this place is literally a few steps away from my apartment and that they have decent food. I also don't understand the greasy spoon comments... you do realize it's a pizza joint right? You aren't going there for the ambiance, more for the cheap food.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I'm confused why people criticize this place. They're nice, quick, and affordable. Some complain about dry chicken fingers, but I disagree. The food is great, especially the delicious honey mustard. Salads are also packed with veggies. Fries are tasty and they even include cole slaw with the chicken finger platter. Being conveniently close to my apartment, I appreciate that they offer decent food. It's a pizza joint, not a fancy place, so the greasy spoon comments don't make sense. It's all about the affordable food.

input: Great cheesesteak! Friendly and fast service. Lazo's really made my day.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Lazo's great cheesesteak and friendly, fast service really made my day.

input: Ambience OK, too bad stuck in a mall in New Hope.  They were very understaffed (which thankfully they kept apologizing for) so there service was definitely slow, however very very pleasant.  We definitely felt it was worth the wait!  Vegetable Samosas were delicious, chicken were slightly dry.  I ordered chicken tikka masala which was so flavorful and rich and my husband had the chicken tagine...amazing!  Has the feeling of a place where "you get what you get and you don't get upset" but when you get it, it is really out of this world!  Loved the mix of cuisines, just enough choices on the menu.  Restaurant is BYOB so we were unprepared, but we will be back!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Despite being stuck in a mall in New Hope, the restaurant had an okay ambience. However, they were understaffed, apologized for the slow service, but remained very pleasant. Despite the wait, the food was worth it. The vegetable samosas were delicious, but the chicken was slightly dry. The chicken tikka masala was flavorful and rich, while the chicken tagine was amazing. The restaurant had a "you get what you get and you don't get upset" vibe, but the food was out of this world. The menu had a good mix of cuisines with just enough choices. It is a BYOB restaurant, which we were unprepared for, but we plan on returning.

input: This is the cutest mom/pop local, high-quality ice cream joint in all of Tucson! Delicious... But definitely a bit pricey ($4.50 for a regular single scoop)- hence the 4 stars as opposed to 5.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This local ice cream joint in Tucson is adorable and known for its high-quality ice cream. However, it is a bit expensive, with a regular single scoop priced at $4.50. Despite the price, it still receives a rating of 4 stars out of 5.

input: Cool ass brewery/bar. Very unique decor that suits the name of the place. We came on dat afternoon and it was packed but we got 3 seats easy. Beer selection was good especially for imperial stout lovers. No food there but you can bring your on or there are plenty of places across the street.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Unique, packed brewery/bar with cool decor that matches its name. Despite the crowd, we easily found three seats. Great beer selection, particularly for fans of imperial stouts. No in-house food available, but you can bring your own or find many options across the street.

input:
We have been to so many different bbq places but this absolutely amazing the place is so colorful and laid back tried the beef brisket and smoked sausage and enjoyed it to the last bite. 
Next time we are in the mood for BBQ we know where we are going !
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We've tried many BBQ places, but this one stood out with its vibrant atmosphere and relaxed vibe. The beef brisket and smoked sausage were absolutely amazing, and we savored every bite. Now, whenever we crave BBQ, we know exactly where to go!

input:
Arrive between 7am-9am on a weekday and get their breakfast bargain! Two eggs, home fries or LATKE, toast or biscuit, and bottomless coffee all for FOUR DOLLARS!

The service was amazing and I got a delicious breakfast and experience for less than it costs to take the bus to and from work.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Arrive between 7am-9am on a weekday for a breakfast bargain: two eggs, choice of home fries or latke, toast or biscuit, and bottomless coffee, all for just four dollars! The service was outstanding, and I enjoyed a delicious breakfast and experience that cost less than my daily bus fare to work.

input: Always crowded but how can you blame them? Last time I went in here I met 2 famous people at the bar and had the best sushi of my life! oh yea and waited 2 hours....
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Always crowded, but can you blame them? Last time I visited, I met two famous people at the bar, had the best sushi ever, and endured a two-hour wait.

input: Loved this place!!! Beautiful room, and awesome location. The streetcar runs right in front of the inn and it takes you to canal. Stay here!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Loved this place! Beautiful room, awesome location with streetcar right in front of the inn that takes you to the canal. Highly recommend staying here!

input: The food, the service, the price, the ambiance, all are perfect.  Every item on the menu we tried was delicious and it's healthy besides. The owners say lots of love goes into their food and it sure tastes like it. Highly recommended.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The food, service, price, ambiance - all perfect. Every menu item tried was delicious and healthy. Owners put lots of love into their food. Highly recommended.

input: Just found my new favorite place for pizza, didn't get any of the pizzas listed on the menu, built our own. Pepperoni, sliced red onions, roasted garlic. Was perfect, not too much cheese, the right amount of pepperoni, onions weren't over powering, and the garlic...oh yes, not your run of the mill minced garlic, but cloves of roasted garlic. All their pizzas are 10", perfect amount for two, didn't try any of the appetizers, but I'm going to do their survey, and get one for free. Looking forward on going back....real soon.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Found new favorite pizza place. Custom-built pizza with pepperoni, sliced red onions, and roasted garlic. Perfect balance of toppings. 10" size ideal for two. Didn't try appetizers. Excited to do survey for a free pizza. Can't wait to return soon.

input: What a great place for breakfast!! Healthy options that are yummy, other options that LOOK yummy!! We love the atmosphere, service and food.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Amazing breakfast spot with delicious and healthy food options, as well as visually appealing alternatives. The atmosphere, service, and overall dining experience are all exceptional.

input: Great service and body work looked great.  They even vacuumed the inside.  Randy kept me up to date on the status through text so I knew what was going on with my car at all times.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Excellent service with impeccable body work. Additionally, they went the extra mile by vacuuming the interior of my car. Randy provided consistent updates via text, ensuring I was always informed about the status of my vehicle.

input:
**EDIT** 7/12
I've since been and for sure have changed my opinion. Again, as I said below, I think I caught them on a bad day. 3rd time was a charm for me. IF I get a hankering for some good greek / med food... I'll check it out.

Oh and to the reply from the vendor, no my first review wasn't a joke. My opinions still stand from my initial visit, HOWEVER since I went back i even tried Bubble Tea, for that alone... I'm a HUUUUUUUUUUUUUGE fan.


Short and not sweet ... avoid this place. Maybe I just got them on a bad day... but suffice to say nothing was good. Sauce sucked, lettuce brown, long wait , expensive, and just dry and tasteless. Gyros should be savory and moist! sorry I won't be visiting again.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I initially had a negative opinion of this place, but I have since revisited and changed my mind. However, I still stand by my first review. If I have a craving for Greek/Mediterranean food, I might give it another try. I must clarify that my first review was not a joke. My opinions remain the same from my initial visit, but I did try their Bubble Tea, and I really enjoyed it.

input: I definitely won't be coming back here. Long story short, I scheduled an appointment online to have the transmission and differential fluid changed on my pilot. I arrived on time, and I was told it would take approximately 2 hours for completion, I also said I wanted an oil change, but " full synthetic". He said it would be $20 more, I said okay. When it was finally done and I was ready to check out, my advisor (Brandon) give me the total cost, which was double than what I expected and paid for in the past. I asked him what was all done, he said, "they completed a transmission flush instead of the regular drain and refill". I told him that's not what I wanted or asked for. He went on to say "it was good for the car and whatever", like I'm some kind of idiot. First of all Honda doesn't recommend doing a transmission flush and secondly, its almost triple what you would normally pay for a standard transmission fluid change. On top of that they didn't even do a full synthetic oil change it was just a blend. I didn't have time to argue with him because I was already late for an appointment, but I have the email showing what I originally asked for, so I'll be calling my bank soon.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I won't return here. I scheduled an appointment online for a transmission and differential fluid change on my pilot. I arrived on time, expecting it to take about 2 hours. I also requested a full synthetic oil change for an additional $20. However, when checking out, my advisor informed me that they had performed a transmission flush instead of a regular drain and refill, which was not what I wanted. He tried to justify it, but Honda does not recommend a flush and the cost was almost triple what I usually pay. Additionally, they didn't even provide a full synthetic oil change, just a blend. I didn't have time to argue, but I have evidence from the original request, so I will contact my bank soon.

input: We love, love M.L. Rose! I am a huge beer fan and the flights are so fun to choose and try. I love the neighborhood hangout feel, not too hipster, not too old....just right! We always have awesome service too. My hang up can be the food. Wings not quite crispy enough, burgers not cooked to taste, spinach artichoke dip just meh. The steak and Gouda was flat out gross - big fatty slab of undercooked steak on bread. We were told it is leaving the menu, but they should have removed it long ago. And no visit from the manager when the sandwich was returned, which was a little underwhelming. We will be back, we are big fans, but please get your kitchen together so I can have my fav burger in town cooked just right :-)
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We love M.L. Rose - great beer selection, fun flights, and a relaxed neighborhood atmosphere. The service is always excellent. However, we have had some issues with the food. The wings aren't crispy enough, the burgers aren't cooked to our liking, and the spinach artichoke dip is just average. The steak and Gouda sandwich was very disappointing - undercooked steak on a fatty slab of bread. It's supposedly being removed from the menu, which should have been done sooner. Additionally, when we returned the sandwich, we didn't receive a visit from the manager. Despite these setbacks, we are still fans of M.L. Rose and hope that the kitchen improves, especially for our favorite burger in town.

input:
Long wait but definitely worth it. Biscuits are on point!

If you're looking for good chicken, biscuits and honey look no further!

Bonus, they are everywhere.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Worth the wait! Delicious biscuits and great for chicken and honey lovers. Plus, they have numerous locations.

input:
We went on a non typical day, school year mid week, so we had the luxury of being only a handful of people there  Therefore, my review may not be representative of a typical visit. 
Arrived at opening and found the off season price within reason. Bathrooms and water park were immaculate. The lifeguards were attentive and friendly. 
A star was lost because I found the water and air temp to be a tad too cold. The park was smaller then other indoor water parks I've been to. Only two big slides, one group slide, a couple of younger kids areas, lazy river and a simulated surf area. They would periodically close the big slides in order to open the surf area, for lack of staffing. A minor annoyance since that is why we were there. 
I can see how people  would be upset paying more and sharing the park with hundreds of others. But I think if your timing is right, you could have an enjoyable afternoon.
We did save money by using our AAA card. Could have saved more as it was my sons birthday month, but I didn't have proof on me.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We visited the water park on a school year mid-week when there were very few people present, so our experience may not be typical. We arrived at opening and found the off-season price to be reasonable. The bathrooms and water park were exceptionally clean, and the lifeguards were attentive and friendly. However, there were a few drawbacks. The water and air temperature felt slightly too cold, and the park was smaller compared to other indoor water parks I've been to. There were only two big slides, one group slide, a few areas for younger kids, a lazy river, and a simulated surf area. Occasionally, the big slides would close to open the surf area due to a lack of staffing, which was a minor annoyance since that was the main reason for our visit. Nonetheless, if you time your visit well, you can have an enjoyable afternoon without the crowds and higher prices. We were able to save some money by using our AAA card, but we could have saved more if we had proof for my son's birthday month, which we unfortunately didn't have at the time.

input:
The interior design is impeccable, the staff is friendly and the food is spot on. 

If you want to try something special, more than just your average wings, try the sauce and toss special. You won't be disappointed. 

I'll be living nearby and will probably come back to try the other areas of the menu. Well done!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The interior design is impeccable, staff is friendly, and the food is spot on, especially the sauce and toss special if you want something unique. I'll definitely be returning to explore the rest of the menu. Well done!

input: Great food but the service is so bad we seen our waitress once  everyone else did here job plus I was not finished eating and she gave me the check    Hate that   But good food
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Quality food, however, the service was disappointing as we only saw our waitress once, while everyone else performed their duties. Furthermore, our waitress prematurely brought us the check even though I had not finished eating. Despite this, the food was enjoyable.

input:
Came here with a group of girls, so we were able to order a bunch of different things to try.  I gotta say they made the best squid steak I ever had.  Flavor was amazing.  

The only downside, was that the service was really slow, and everything is extremely over priced.  The food took forever to come out, and we had to wave the waitress down for drinks.

If we had gotten better service, and the prices not so high, I would have given them 4 stars.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Came with a group of girls, ordered a variety of dishes. Best ever squid steak, incredible flavor. However, service was slow and everything was overpriced. Food took ages, had to ask for drinks. If service and prices were better, I would give 4 stars.

input: I love the whole concept. We had such a great experience here. The food was delicious. Our waiter was the best. We ordered cheesecake which was even better. I can't wait to come on the day they make cinnamon rolls. We will defiantly be back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We had a great experience at this place. The food was delicious, especially the cheesecake. Our waiter was excellent. We love the concept and will definitely be back, especially for the cinnamon rolls.

input: So meijer is amazing and so convenient! However, the starbucks is always a hit or miss and the employees don't seem to be trained right because I've noticed every time they have to pull a sheet out to see how much it is and its never the same price.. my drink wasn't good at all this morning and when i told the lady it didn't look right she poured some of my drink out and just put more milk in it to make it taste better. Wasn't really wanting to pay $4 for a cup full of milk but she didn't seem to care so why bother even saying anything.. :/
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Meijer is convenient, but Starbucks inside is hit or miss. Employees often need to reference prices and my drink today wasn't good. When I mentioned it, the lady poured some out and added more milk, but I didn't want to pay $4 for a milk-filled cup. She didn't seem to care, so I didn't bother saying anything further.

input: I love their eggs! Their eggs taste better than any other restaurant eggs I've ever had. We always get the hash. Dawn Patrol is always super generous with the food portioning...with the hash, that is. My brother got a burger to go, and all it was was a piece of meat between two buns. However, he said the burger was really good, but still, I feel that they could've melted some cheese on top of the patty. All of their pastries, bread and jellies are homemade - and really delicious!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Their eggs are the best I've ever had at a restaurant, especially paired with their generous portions of hash. The burger my brother had was good, but could have been improved with melted cheese on top. Apart from that, all of their homemade pastries, bread, and jellies are incredibly delicious.

input: Came late Friday night for a bite to eat. Much of the soup, hot takeaway were cleaned up. Settled for an individual pizza to share. Crust was too thick, but we could debate pies until the cows come home. Wandered the store while it was baking and found Scharffenberger chocolate! Pie may not be up to our standard but the chocolate hit the spot. At 8pm at night, the staff was exhausted
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Arrived late Friday night for food. Limited soup and hot takeaway options left. Ended up sharing an individual pizza with thick crust. Explored the store while waiting and discovered Scharffenberger chocolate. Although the pizza wasn't great, the chocolate was satisfying. Staff seemed exhausted at 8pm.

input: Had lunch here today. My cheeseburger was a 10/10 with an avocado on top. I also had the "ranchero fries" which are French fries with ranch, cheese, and tomatoes on top! The only thing keeping this awesome lunch spot from being 5 star would be the fact that it took a significant amount of time to get out food when the restaurant was relatively pretty slow.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Had lunch today, cheeseburger with avocado was amazing, 10/10. Also tried the "ranchero fries," topped with ranch, cheese, and tomatoes. Only downside was the slow service despite the restaurant being quiet.

input: Great food!  Service was super nice: George!  Crab cakes were awesome.  Just a great place to eat!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Great food, excellent service provided by George, and awesome crab cakes make this a fantastic place to dine.

input:
Our wedding at Winters Creek Lodge was absolutely fantastic. Judit was a rockstar. She got us organized, and was very flexible and helpful to allow us to fulfill our vision. Our guests have raved and raved about the views and what an amazing venue it was. Our photos are breath-taking. Regarding the food, you will hear that they do not offer tastings, but do not worry: we can confirm that it was absolutely delicious. Their pricing is also very competitive for the area.

We strongly recommend working with Judit at the Winters Creek Lodge.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Our wedding at Winters Creek Lodge was fantastic. Judit was amazing - she helped us stay organized, was flexible, and fulfilled our vision. Guests loved the stunning views and venue, and our photos are breathtaking. The food was delicious, despite no tastings offered. Pricing is competitive. Highly recommend working with Judit at Winters Creek Lodge.

input:
I normally wouldn't think Greek food for brunch or lunch; I'm way more of a traditional American-style brunch kind of guy.  But when my friends suggested to meet them here for brunch this past weekend, I trusted their better judgement.  In the end, I'm glad I did.  This cozy Center City spot not only serves an amazing (and dare I say, a contender for the best) brunch in Philly, the staff really make you feel at home.  They really know how to wow their patrons: fresh food, delightful presentation, and so many delicious sounding choices it's hard to choose which dish you want from their one page menu for mains.

Their specialty, and they're not shy to tell you, is the Cyprus Breakfast.  It's a mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch.  The plate comes out with two sunny-side up eggs, fried in olive oil and garnished with fresh parsely.  It's served alongside a grilled slice of lounza (Greek ham), two pieces of salty, crisp fried halloumi, warm bread, and tomato, cucumber, and onion salad.  The menu also features a spread of other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialities: Avgolemono, Moussaka, Pastitsio, Shaksouka, and Malohwa to name a few.  They even serve Greek Coffee and Frappes!

The service may be a little over-attentive in an attempt to make you feel more than welcome, but it's much appreciated, especially when other restaurants fail to put as much effort into the service as they do the food.  One other tip: reservations are highly recommended, if not required.  Because of Kanella's small space, getting a table at brunch is nearly impossible if you're not on the list.  But if you can score seats here for brunch, then expect nothing less than a stellar way to start your weekend morning (or recover from last night's activities).  Can't wait to come back and try out the dinner menu.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I was skeptical about trying Greek food for brunch, as I usually prefer traditional American-style brunch. However, my friends convinced me to meet them at this cozy Center City spot, and I'm glad I trusted their judgement. Not only does this place serve an amazing brunch, but the staff also make you feel at home. The menu offers a variety of delicious-sounding options, making it hard to decide what to order from their one page menu. One of their specialties is the Cyprus Breakfast, a Mediterranean twist on the classic combination of eggs, meat, and starch. It comes with two sunny-side up eggs fried in olive oil, garnished with fresh parsley, and served with grilled Greek ham, fried halloumi, warm bread, and a tomato, cucumber, and onion salad. The menu also features other traditional Greek, Mediterranean, and Middle Eastern specialties. The service can be slightly over-attentive, but it is appreciated, especially when compared to other restaurants. Reservations are highly recommended due to the small space, and scoring a table for brunch can be challenging without one. I'm excited to come back and try their dinner menu.

input: This place gets two stars from me only because the gravy fries were good. Their sandwiches are awful. Thick slabs of badly sliced, tough, dry meat....gross. I made the mistake of ordering their pork sandwich once and it was inedible. I tried to bite into the sandwich and couldn't even bite through because of how tough and rubbery the pork was. I don't understand why they slice the meat the way they do but it makes for a disgusting sandwich. The people raving on how good this place is are just locals who have never had anything better. You're better off going to Wawa for a sandwich. Seriously. It will at least be edible.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place receives two stars solely for their good gravy fries. However, their sandwiches are awful with thick, badly sliced, tough, and dry meat. I once made the mistake of ordering their pork sandwich, which was inedible. The meat was excessively tough and rubbery, making it impossible to bite through. The way they slice the meat results in a disgusting sandwich. The praise from locals is likely due to their lack of experience with better options. It is advised to go to Wawa for a sandwich, as it will at least be edible.

input:
Be careful.  This place just wants your money, not your business.  They deal only in cash and are very reluctant to take returns.  And I'm sure that they don't only take cash only from the large contractors... probably just the little guys.  
They sell damaged items.  Check your stuff very well before you leave, because you will not be able to bring it back if you discover that they have slipped you the ole' damaged door!

I do not recommend this place.  Don't support them.  Not at all.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This place prioritizes money over customer satisfaction and does not accept returns. They exclusively deal in cash and are particularly resistant to returns from small contractors. They also sell damaged items, so thoroughly check your purchase before leaving as they do not facilitate returns for such issues. Overall, I strongly advise against supporting this establishment in any way.

input: We stopped here on our way through town and want sure what to expect but we were pleasantly surprised. The service sucked and the staff was rude but the food made up that in the end. We had some pulled pork which was more chopped then pulled, brisket tacos which were define, and pulled chicken which was moist. The sides were pretty good too but nothing to write home about. There were five of us and our bill was close to $60 and one meal was a kids meal. I  really only have two complaints: One, they didn't have ribs for lunch and two, the bathrooms were filthy.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We were pleasantly surprised during our stop here on our way through town. Despite the poor service and rude staff, the food made up for it in the end. The pulled pork, although more chopped than pulled, was enjoyable. The brisket tacos were excellent, and the pulled chicken was moist. The sides were decent, although not remarkable. Our group of five had a bill close to $60, including one kids meal. However, I do have two complaints: firstly, they did not offer ribs for lunch, and secondly, the bathrooms were filthy.

input:
Tried dinner there recently and found the quality is very uneven.

While some noodle soup dishes and rice plate dishes are true to authentic Chinese food, others are truly found in only American Chinese restaurants. The duck is very fat and very little meat. The stir fry dishes have weird combo of vegetables that do not go together.

And as a typical Chinese restaurant, service does not come with a smile.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Recently tried the dinner at this restaurant and noticed inconsistent quality. While some noodle soup and rice dishes are authentic, others resemble American Chinese fare. The duck is excessively fatty with little meat, and the stir fry dishes feature mismatched vegetables. In line with typical Chinese restaurants, the service lacks a friendly demeanor.

input:
I have always dreaded going to the hair salon.  I hated the phony atmosphere of most places and I really dreaded the small talk I would be forced to have with my stylist.  Maybe I am unusually insecure, but I always felt intimidated in most salons.  
Then, one day a couple of years ago, I wandered into Andre's salon and I never looked back.  
Andre is warm and personable and made me feel at ease immediately.  Right off the bat, we connected on a topic I care about--dogs--and I didn't feel uncomfortable at all.  Oh, and the cut and color were fantastic!  My highlights last longer than highlights I have received from any other salon.
For the past year or so, Christopher has been styling my hair and I LOVE him to death.  He is incredibly sweet, down-to-earth and talented!  My hair looks amazing for days after he styles it and, try as I might, I can never get it to look as good as he can.
The last time I was at the salon, Christopher, Leah and I had a blast reminiscing about '80s fashion!  I can't remember a time when I enjoyed going to the hair salon (which is probably because I never have!).
Also, back in the spring, I asked Andre if he would be interested in donating a gift for a charity 5K I was helping to organize.  Being the wonderful person he is, Andre didn't hesitate and put together a beautiful basket that was a hit at the race!  Andre has a good heart and that it what I love about going to his salon!
I also love that clients can schedule appointments online through schedulicity!
Great prices, great cuts, great color, great space, convenient scheduling options and, most importantly, great people--you will not regret choosing Andre for your next cut or color!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I used to dread going to hair salons because of the phony atmosphere and forced small talk with stylists. However, a couple of years ago, I found Andre's salon and it changed everything. Andre is warm, personable, and made me feel comfortable right away. We connected over our love for dogs, and the cut and color he did were fantastic. Recently, Christopher has been styling my hair and I absolutely love him. He is sweet, talented, and my hair looks amazing for days after he styles it. At the salon, we even had a great time reminiscing about '80s fashion. Andre also showed his kindness by donating a gift for a charity 5K I organized. He put together a beautiful basket and his good heart is something I love about his salon. Furthermore, clients can conveniently schedule appointments online through schedulicity. With great prices, cuts, color, space, and people, choosing Andre for your next cut or color will be a decision you won't regret.

input: Absolutely amazing and unique food. Love their bobba and pork pancake!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Incredible food with exceptional flavors, highly recommend their delicious bobba and pork pancake.

input:
Nice, old school space with a long bar. It reminded me of some places I've been out west, which might be a little strange in the heart of Philadelphia. 

Not too loud at all - conversations were easy and a lot of the patrons were doing just that. There's a jukebox, so maybe it cranks up later in the evening. We were there pretty early. 

Great service from several people working behind the bar. 

Several beers on tap including a local CCCCC IPA, which was solid. Not many wines, though.

Small menu but very good food. The elote (corn) is quite good, as was the cucumber(?) salad. But the brat plate was the star. Wonderful brat, German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel and a hot salsa/relish. Best brat plate ever. Served on a cool wood board.

Prohibition is located in or near a somewhat dicey neighborhood, at least to this non-resident's eye. I may very well be wrong about that. We had to walk a trashy, pissy street past what seemed like skid row coming from the hotel on Race St. If it was later at night we might have chosen not to walk back.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
Cozy, nostalgic bar with a western feel in the heart of Philadelphia. The atmosphere is not too loud, making conversations easy. There is a jukebox that may get louder later in the evening. The bar staff provides excellent service.

The drink selection includes various beers on tap, including a local IPA. However, the wine options are limited. The menu is small but offers delicious food. The elote (corn) and cucumber salad are tasty, but the standout dish is the brat plate. It comes with a fantastic bratwurst, German potato salad, sauerkraut, pretzel, and hot salsa/relish, all served on a stylish wooden board.

Prohibition may be located in a somewhat sketchy neighborhood, at least from the perspective of someone unfamiliar with the area. The route from the hotel on Race St. involved walking through a dirty and unpleasant street that seemed rundown. During late hours, it might be advisable to consider alternative transportation instead of walking back.

input:
On the Run is a convenience store chain and BP gas station. It is in a very convenient location for those who are returning rental cars at Lambert-St. Louis International Airport! How many times have you been on the way back into an airport, and not found a gas station nearby? Happens to me to any times - often you have to go out of your way to find one. Not so here!

Paid at the pump - I note that the pump had a hand scrawled note taped to the pumps - requesting you press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping your credit card. Never seen this before - this is the exact opposite procedure of other gas station pumps when using a credit card!

Refueled and was on my way to Hertz!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: On the Run is a convenient convenience store chain and BP gas station located near Lambert-St. Louis International Airport. It is a great option for those returning rental cars as it eliminates the hassle of finding a gas station nearby. The pumps require customers to press the appropriate button (credit or debit) before swiping their credit card, which is a unique feature compared to other gas stations. After refueling, the writer was able to quickly proceed to Hertz.

input:
This is a pretty historical building that is well maintained. When we visited, we were the ONLY people there, which meant the Park Ranger gave us a private tour. Sweet!

Also - if you're into collecting National Park Stamps, you can get a few here! w00t!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This historical building is well-maintained and offers a unique experience. During our visit, we were the only ones present, resulting in a private tour led by a park ranger. Additionally, if you enjoy collecting National Park Stamps, you can obtain a few at this location. Exciting!

input: The service was great and the restaurant was clean, but the food was just okay. We had the linguine with marinara and the rotini primavera. The linguine was fine. The primavera, however, is not something anyone should order!!! The sauce had a great flavor, but the vegetables were actually from frozen. I mean, literally from FROZEN. Go to your local grocery store, look at the bag of Bird's Eye mixed vegetables and you will see what they use... right down to the ruffle cut carrots. There is so much wonderful fresh produce in Tucson, there is absolutely no reason to ever use gross frozen vegetables.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The service and cleanliness of the restaurant were excellent, but the food was mediocre. We ordered linguine with marinara and rotini primavera. The linguine was decent, but the primavera should be avoided at all costs. The sauce had good flavor, but the vegetables were clearly frozen, resembling the Bird's Eye mixed vegetables found in grocery stores, including the ruffle cut carrots. With the abundance of fresh produce available in Tucson, there is no excuse for using unappealing frozen vegetables.

input:
We  heard that Fresh Market was open and since we just got back from vaca we thought we would try it.  First of all, accolades to the staff they could not have been more helpful.  Especially Thomas in the meat section.  For these two things I would give them a five.  However, it does downhill from this point on:  ordered one pound of swiss cheese, after standing there waiting for about 5 minutes, and no one else was on line, the unfriendly clerk waited on us. The imported swiss cheese that we ordered was so poorly cut that in two days we had one clump of swiss cheese, rather than many slices.  I bought ricotta cheese for Easter and went to open it, and it was bad, although it was dated 3/28.  The tomatoes on the vine that I bought on Friday were bad by Sunday.  I have found their prices very high, selection, poor and at this point it is just not worth it. I also bought two pound cakes and their were not up to par.  Very dry and tasteless.. Overall a very disappointing shopping trip 
There is plenty of convenient parking and the store was immaculate, but it is not for me.  The final straw was that I asked for extra cash for Easter gifts, the clerk at the register said there was a $150 limit, the ATM terminal said $100 and the "manager" said $50...I thought they should get their act together.  Best to stay with Weaver's Way... or Whole Foods or Wegmann's.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Fresh Market recently opened and we decided to give it a try after our vacation. The staff, particularly Thomas in the meat section, was extremely helpful, earning them a five-star rating. However, our experience went downhill from there. The clerk who served us when we ordered one pound of Swiss cheese was unfriendly and the cheese was poorly cut, resulting in a clump instead of individual slices. The ricotta cheese we bought for Easter was also bad, despite being within the expiration date. The tomatoes on the vine purchased on Friday were already spoiled by Sunday. Additionally, we found the prices high, the selection poor, and the quality of the two pound cakes disappointing. Overall, it was a disappointing shopping trip. While the store had ample parking and was clean, it is not a place we would return to. To top it off, there was confusion about the cash limit for Easter gifts, with conflicting information from the clerk, the ATM terminal, and the supposed manager. We believe it's best to stick with Weaver's Way, Whole Foods, or Wegmann's.

input:
I've only been once, but I'm ready to return.

Since moving to Fletcher Place, I've been looking for a bar near by that's similar to my neighborhood favorite, J Clydes. I think I've found it.

The Dugout is a simple hole-in-the-wall place. They have a decent selection, Sun King for $4.50, happy hour appetizers, and my favorite part: HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! No longer must I wait until my coveted Mug N' Bun trips for these fried morsels of tasty peppery goodness. Had a nice little piece form this joint, too. 

Really excited to return.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I'm ready to return to The Dugout in Fletcher Place. It's a simple hole-in-the-wall bar with a decent selection of drinks, including Sun King for $4.50. They also offer happy hour appetizers and my favorite - HOT PEPPER CHEESE BALLS! No need to wait for my Mug N' Bun trips anymore. I even had a great experience at this place. Can't wait to go back.

input:
I heard this ice cream parlour opened last summer, so upon my first trip home (sometime during the fall) I hustled over to try it. Since Friendly's closed a few years ago, Warminster has sorely needed a new ice cream place (DQ was our last one standing for quite some time). 

Much to my dismay, the Big Scoop had already closed for the season. I marked it in my calendar go return in March, when it reopened. Upon my next trip home in the spring, I was disappointed to see that I was just a few days early for their reopening, and would have to wait until my return in April.

After much anticipation, I made it to Big Scoop last weekend with my sister (who has been before). I was shocked to see what a range of products they serve - hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, pizza, you name it! I was tempted at the prospect of waffles and ice cream, but I wasn't that hungry so I settled for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie with hot fudge and whipped cream. The generous scoop of ice cream was tasty and packed with globs of cookie dough! I also tasted the birthday cake, which I enjoyed very much. 

The service was quick, and the shop crowded quickly. The interior was nicely remodeled and looks clean and family friendly. The man who helped me was extremely courteous and seemed to be doing most of the work. 

Especially given the lack of competition around here, the Big Scoop gets an easy four stars!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Last summer, a new ice cream parlour called Big Scoop opened in Warminster, which was much needed after Friendly's closed a few years ago. However, upon my first visit in the fall, I learned that they had already closed for the season. I planned to return in March when they reopened, but my next visit in the spring was a few days too early. Finally, last weekend, I made it to Big Scoop with my sister. To my surprise, they served more than just ice cream, including hot dogs, funnel cake, onion rings, and pizza. I opted for a scoop of chocolate chip cookie with hot fudge and whipped cream, which was delicious. The service was quick, and the shop quickly became crowded. The interior was nicely remodeled and had a clean and family-friendly atmosphere. Overall, given the lack of competition in the area, I would give the Big Scoop an easy four-star rating.

input: Aparently this review is for Saguaro East. I didnt realize there were two separate parks. This park is fine. We planned to do some hiking, but it just looked like flat average desert you can easily see and hike in the Phoenix area. The visitor center and staff were nice.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Review for Saguaro East: This park is okay, but it seems like a standard desert with flat terrain, similar to the Phoenix area. The visitor center and staff were friendly.

input:
Staff is amazing!  Coupons on their website are for 40 percent off a regular priced item... so that means... you are always getting something on sale!

We went in one evening at around 15 minutes before closing to grab some things very quickly... and all staff members were very helpful even so close to closing!  

Great store!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The staff at the store is amazing and very helpful, even when we went in close to closing time. They have coupons on their website for 40 percent off a regular priced item, so you can always get something on sale. Overall, it's a great store.

input:
This is another one of those anytime coffee shops. You can come get some work done, people watch, or just grab a drink to go. Either way, its open early and late.

For the quarter, its "off the beaten path" but in the busy area the locals hang out, and on the way to Fenchmen where everyone goes for good local music, Jazz, et al. 

They have food, not the cheapest, or local, but its better for you than the greasy, salty, fatty foods. Just make sure your service number is visible I got distracted hid my number, and had to stop the guy looking.  

Service varies. Since its a busy sidewalk, people stop in for that pick me up before work or party. One minute there is a like 12 long, and the barista is running ragged, the next its dead. 

Sometimes I'll sit for over an hour working or catching up on email. I'll order something every so often, and its no big deal for me to queue myself if they get busy. After all it helps those stopping in for a quick drink.

p.s. I love there tall cookies

oh and how many coffee shops can you get a shot in your coffee! That's right, its not a bar, but its New Orleans.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This coffee shop is open early and late, making it a convenient option for getting work done, people-watching, or grabbing a drink on the go. It is situated in a busy area where locals hang out and is on the way to popular music venues. The food offered is not the cheapest or local, but it is healthier compared to greasy, salty, and fatty options. However, it is important to ensure that your service number is visible to avoid any confusion. The quality of service can vary depending on the busy sidewalk traffic. It is not uncommon to sit for over an hour while working or checking emails, occasionally ordering something and being understanding of long queues during busy times. The coffee shop offers the unique feature of adding a shot to your coffee. Although not a bar, it embraces the New Orleans ambiance. Additionally, their tall cookies are highly recommended.

input: I was on the guest list tonight as my friend from high school was DJing, however, when I got to the front of the line I was unfortunately shoved through the front door before I could show my ID and verify my guest list status. After I was shoved through I tried to explain to the bouncer what had happened so I could properly verify that I was actually on the list. This bouncer then accused me of just trying to sneak in for free without paying even though I went back to him once I was inside. He then proceeded to belittle me and completely disregard the fact that I was allowed to be there. This ended in me being denied total entry, despite the fact that I was on the list, and I will never come here due to how I was treated by this bouncer.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I was on the guest list to attend a party tonight because my high school friend was DJing. However, upon reaching the front of the line, I was forcefully pushed through the entrance before I could present my ID and confirm my guest list status. Once inside, I approached the bouncer to explain the situation and properly verify my presence on the list. Shockingly, he accused me of attempting to enter without paying and refused to acknowledge my rightful access. Despite being on the guest list, I was ultimately denied entry. As a result of this mistreatment, I have decided never to return to this establishment.

input: Salad portions are great. I always go with the Greek. One of the few Nick's spots that serves a rustic roast beef sandwich. Highly recommend that one. Pizza isn't that bad. I'd recommend an XL if having guests over. It's probably there better pizza, surprisingly.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Salad portions are generous, especially the Greek salad. Nick's offers a delicious rustic roast beef sandwich, which is a rare find. The pizza is quite good, and I suggest getting an XL size if you have guests. Surprisingly, it might be their best pizza option.

input:
Definitely dug this place...rather hipster-ish and way, way reminiscent of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake, but I liked it a lot despite all that...pizza here is definitely a lot better, as is beer selection. This may wind up being one of my more regular haunts as I slog my way through more of their menu (I think I may need to heavily modify next time I'm there), but so far, I have no cause at all for complaint and much to celebrate. It's interesting to me that the environments of the various locations are different, sometimes vastly, yet all have their own unique and innate charm. Whoever is running these is doing a phenomenal job, so props there.

One thing of note here...the ordering system is extremely clunky and seemingly disorganized and I sort of dislike it. Not enough to stop coming here, since I really dig the vibe of these, but on one of my less patient nights, that sort of thing may be enough to cut this out of the running. Definitely a good spot for pizza and a brew (or several), though. I back it.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf:
I really enjoyed this place, it has a hipster-ish vibe and reminds me a lot of Este Sugarhouse in Salt Lake. The pizza here is much better, and they have a great selection of beer. I plan on coming here regularly as I try more of their menu, although I may need to make some modifications next time. Overall, I have no complaints and a lot to celebrate. It's interesting that each location has a different, yet charming atmosphere. The person in charge is doing a fantastic job.

The only downside is the ordering system, which is clunky and disorganized, and I'm not a fan of it. However, it's not enough to make me stop coming here because I really like the vibe. This is a great place for pizza and beer, and I highly recommend it.

input:
New St. Louis Wok is one of the few local Chinese places that deliver to our area.  Every time (but one), we've ordered, and gotten the food within an house.  In addition, they have a website where you can order the food (avoiding possible language barriers), and then they follow up with a call for your credit card number.

Food wise, it's the best Chinese delivery we've had here.  Nothing too greasy, and everything comes hot...with lots of sauces and fortune cookies.  For our rare Chinese cravings, it's the go-to place.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: New St. Louis Wok is a local Chinese restaurant that delivers to our area. They consistently deliver our food within an hour, except for one instance. They offer the convenience of online ordering through their website, which eliminates potential language barriers, and they follow up with a phone call for credit card information. Their food is the best Chinese delivery we have had in our area, as it is not overly greasy and always arrives hot with a generous amount of sauces and fortune cookies. Whenever we have cravings for Chinese food, New St. Louis Wok is our go-to place.

input: This is my go to sushi place. it's cheap and the rolls are AMAZING. if you want a new sushi place to try i highly recommend osaka
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Osaka is my top choice for sushi - affordable and with incredible rolls. I highly recommend it as a new sushi spot to try.

input:
Kelly's has changed hands and the menu has completely changed.  It's clear they've had to defend this and it seems to annoy them.  I mean the menu was epic - why change it?

In response, the new crew touted the place being cleaner and it was.

I got the  classic burger and fries.  I'll be honest, it was the worst $11 burger that I've ever had.  Dry and flavorless and made me envy a $2 McDonalds bacon burger flashing on the TV.  The fries were OK.

I was shocked to just walk in at dinner time.  This wasn't possible before.  Now I know why.

:
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Kelly's has new owners and they have completely changed the menu, which has been met with resistance. Despite the changes, the new crew emphasizes that the place is cleaner. However, the food quality has been disappointing, with the classic burger and fries being particularly unsatisfactory. The experience of easily walking in during dinner time was surprising, given that it was previously impossible.

input: Great place to go everyday. I saw huge changes in my strength and flexibility there. All of the teachers are unique and teach beneficial classes. I highly recommend a monthly membership!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Highly recommend this great place for daily visits. They have experienced teachers who provide unique and beneficial classes, resulting in noticeable improvements in strength and flexibility. Consider getting a monthly membership for optimum benefits.

input:
I live in the neighborhood and used to order at least once a week and pick up.  The last last few times I have had to wait from 10 to 15 minutes as the team scrambles around trying to find change. All I wanted to do is pay for my food and take it home.   And tonight after the wait for change. I gave them 2 20's for a 27 dollar check. 
I get home and it is the wrong food. My warm dish was cold and my sushi was wrong.  Lost me as a customer
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I used to order and pick up food at least once a week from the neighborhood restaurant. However, recently, I had to wait for about 10 to 15 minutes every time as the team struggled to find change. All I wanted was to pay for my food and take it home. Tonight, after waiting for change, I gave them two 20-dollar bills for a 27-dollar check. Unfortunately, when I got home, the food was incorrect - my warm dish was cold and the sushi was wrong. This experience has made me decide to no longer be their customer.

input: Their pizza is pretty good, service is usually cool inside. But today I ordered a delivery for the first time, the driver was very insulting to me. When I open my door she asked me about a car across the street with a guy in the driver's seat. I replied "I don't know," she said "cus I don't wanna be set up to get robbed". Mind you I already paid with my visa when I ordered, her behavior made me feel awkward as if I had done something wrong. I gave her the tip I had in my hand and said thank you, hoping that maybe if I remain polite she'll stop thinking so negative I just wanted some pizza not to be judged because of my surroundings or to be stereotyped.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Their pizza and service are usually good, but today I had a negative experience with the delivery driver. Upon opening the door, she questioned me about a car parked across the street with a man inside, insinuating that I might be involved in something illicit. This made me feel uneasy, especially since I had already paid for my order. Regardless, I politely gave her the tip and expressed gratitude, hoping to dispel any misconceptions. I simply wanted to enjoy my pizza without being judged or subjected to stereotypes based on my surroundings.

input:
First time here and I have to say it's pretty good! The bake shop fits well with the fishtown environment and it's very clean and welcoming inside. The display of beautiful cakes let's you know you have top quality bakers there. 

I got a few items to share such as a Burbon Pecan cookie, chocolate chip cookie, vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing. 

I had a taste of the Burbon Pecan Cookie. It was not too sweet and you get nice bites of pecan; a nice hot coffee is a perfect compliment.The cupcakes were good (cake wise) but, not a huge fan of the icings. The cake itself was sweet and moist. 

Didn't get to try the Chocolate chip cookie but the concensus was that it's delicious. 

I would definitely come back and I have taken a big interest in having Cake Life make a custom order!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: First time here and it's pretty good! The bake shop fits well with the fishtown environment and it's clean and welcoming inside. The display of beautiful cakes signals top quality bakers. I tried a Burbon Pecan cookie, chocolate chip cookie, vanilla cupcake with buttercream icing, and a vanilla cupcake with raspberry icing. The Burbon Pecan cookie was not too sweet, had nice bites of pecan, and paired well with a hot coffee. The cupcakes were good in terms of cake but not a fan of the icings. The cake itself was sweet and moist. Though I didn't try the chocolate chip cookie, it was deemed delicious by others. I would come back and consider placing a custom order with Cake Life.

input:
Went here last Thursday and arrived early enough to take advantage of their $5 domestic pitchers during hh which includes mich golden light, my fave! It did take the server about 10-15 minutes to even notice we were there, but after that service was just fine. 

Started off with the wings which were delicious, although the bf was certain it was not actually a pound of wings which they claim on their menu.

I ordered the gyro and fries which were surprisingly really good! Gyro meat was tasty and the fries were awesome! Bf had the French onion soup and potato skins which he said were good as well.

We stayed for rock n roll bingo (which I guess is every Thursday, and free!) and we had a blast. They also have a pool table and darts in the back which we played while waiting for bingo to start.

We will definitely be back!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Visited last Thursday, took advantage of $5 domestic pitchers during happy hour, including my favorite, Michelob Golden Light. Initially, the server took 10-15 minutes to notice us, but service improved after that. The wings were delicious, though my boyfriend doubted they were truly a pound as advertised. I was pleasantly surprised by the gyro and fries - both were excellent. My boyfriend enjoyed the French onion soup and potato skins. We stayed for rock n roll bingo, a free event held every Thursday. The back area has a pool table and darts which we played while waiting for bingo. We had a great time and will definitely return.

input: Johnny Tucci and his crew are the absolute best videographers, hands down. They are professional, prompt, and extremely talented. They made our wedding footage look like a movie production and brought everyone to tears that watched it. My advice is that if you are going to splurge in one area for your special day, spend it on a videographer. They do not disappoint.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Johnny Tucci and his crew are the best videographers. They are professional, prompt, and extremely talented. Our wedding footage looked like a movie production and moved everyone to tears. If you want to splurge on one thing for your special day, choose a videographer. They won't disappoint.

input:
One of the absolute best places to see a game in the entire country!

Get there early or if it's a blowout, stroll around the park. There are tons of interesting places to eat & drink (including a rooftop bar). Tickets are still amazingly reasonable even after all the success the Phils have had in recent years particularly when compared to the NY parks.

I used to go more often before the team became so prominent (right after the park opened), and I sat all over the joint. Not really anywhere I wouldn't recommend. The outfied is a great option. 

After starting with a 17 game pack many years ago & then buying season tix a few years back (which my company still has), the staff was great about recommending sections that would avoid direct sunlight , etc. (3rd base field level is awesome).

If you are visiting or considering a trip, don't buy the negative publicity about the Philly fans. The crowds are great. Sure, you have idiots and maniacs like you do at any park and for any professional sporting event, but they are by far the minority and Citizens Bank Park is policed pretty well for nonsense. 

I was once with a group of guys & we stood out in one of the open standing areas between 3rd base & the left field wall the whole night. At one point a very nice officer politely asked us not to curse because there were families around. We we were far from out of control, and we all thought that was pretty cool... so we had fun with some occasional lighthearted banter with the officer for the rest of the night.

Don't expect to be sheltered with your kids like you would be in your own living room, but there's no teens running onto the field getting tazed every night nor are there drunk idiots throwing up on people. 

It's a great atmosphere, a wonderful park & still a very fun team to watch.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Citizens Bank Park is one of the best places in the country to watch a game. It offers plenty of options for food and drink, including a rooftop bar. Tickets are reasonably priced, especially compared to New York parks. The park has a variety of seating options, with the outfield being a great choice. The staff is helpful in suggesting sections to avoid direct sunlight. Despite negative perceptions, the Philly fans are generally great, and the park is well-policed. It provides a fun and lively atmosphere without excessive misbehavior. Overall, Citizens Bank Park offers a fantastic experience for watching baseball.

input: I love Cosi but this Cosi is going down hill fast. I always get a signature salad and lately they are made wrong and no dressing at all. How hard is it to make their own signature salad!? It's practically what they are known for!!! So angry.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: I used to love Cosi, but recently, their quality has declined significantly. Specifically, their signature salad which I used to order regularly is consistently prepared incorrectly with no dressing. It surprises me that they can't even get their own renowned dish right. I'm really frustrated and disappointed.

input: OMG!! what a disappointment today was, I have been so excited to see Rembrandt's reopen after a few months of remodel, what I was thinking is that the new owners would want to do more restorations of this Beautiful, Cozy, old Church, maybe try to find more space to add Tables, but NO, I walked into a Modern, Cold, Hospital Coffee Shop, the Charm is gone, so so disappointed and sad, we all love the Charm of Eagle, but it seems to be fading fast, Please People talk to all the other Eagle Shop Owners when your visiting them especially the old Original Buildings to keep Eagle's charm and quaintness and restore these Beautiful Buildings.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: Today was such a disappointment. I was eagerly anticipating the reopening of Rembrandt's after some remodel time, hoping the new owners would restore and enhance the charm of this beautiful, cozy, old church. But my hopes were shattered as I entered a modern, cold coffee shop that resembled a hospital. I am extremely disappointed and saddened by this. Eagle's unique charm seems to be fading fast, and it's crucial that we speak up and urge other shop owners to preserve the quaintness and restore the beauty of our beloved buildings when we visit them.

input:
The service was lacking. The waiters and waitresses don't know the menu and when you ask for certain things to be brought to your table, it's constantly forgotten. The food is visually appealing but some of the most awkward and distasteful food I've ever had. The waffles are stale, the biscuits are hard as rock and their chorizo is not real chorizo.

The only thing this place has going for it is the atmosphere and their alcohol selection.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: The service is lacking with uninformed waitstaff who constantly forget requested items. The food, although visually appealing, is awkward and distasteful, with stale waffles, hard biscuits, and fake chorizo. However, the atmosphere and alcohol selection are the only positives.

input:
This restaurant is a nice place to go and sit down to have something to eat. I've ate just about everything they have on the menu and I'd say their burgers are great. Although their pizza is a bit on the tough side I still manage to eat the crust too. 

Very comfortable dining room area as well!
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: This restaurant offers a pleasant dining experience with a diverse menu. The burgers are particularly delicious, while the pizza can be a bit tough but still enjoyable. Additionally, the dining room area is very comfortable.

input: We live in the neighborhood and have eaten here many times. I feel as if this restaurant is going downhill. This time we were there for dinner early on a Sunday. The bathrooms were filthy. There are 2 and one was not usable due to all of the paper towels that had been put into the toilet (there was no toilet paper). The other one was usable but also no toilet paper. Our server, Ashley, was not interested in providing any semblance of customer service...RUDE! We had a simple question about the beers on special and she became quite defensive. My daughter spilled her drink, which I realize is a pain in the ass for the restaurant and server (although we were outside so it wasn't that big a deal). We apologized profusely but she didn't even try to hide her annoyance. Finally, the chicken quesadilla should have been labeled the gristle quesadilla....more fat than actual meat...yuck. We love the proximity of this place to where we live and it was great in the past but not anymore...will likely not return...not with so many better quality restaurants in Northern Liberties and Fishtown.
Concise this for me and keep all the inf: We frequently dine at this neighborhood restaurant but have noticed a decline in its quality. During our recent visit on an early Sunday dinner, we were disappointed with the dirty bathrooms. One of the two bathrooms was unusable due to toilet paper being replaced with paper towels, and the other had no toilet paper either. Moreover, our server Ashley provided poor customer service and was rude when we asked a simple question about the beers on special. Additionally, she displayed annoyance when my daughter accidentally spilled her drink, despite us apologizing. Furthermore, the chicken quesadilla was unsatisfactory, with more fat than actual meat. Although we appreciate the convenience of its location, this place has lost its appeal, and we are likely to explore other, higher quality restaurants in Northern Liberties and Fishtown instead.

input: Pretty average bar/restaurant with the menu offerings you can expect from a place like this. The food was OK, and the service was excellent.
